entries.name: Angela

facts.t: She is built on a Project Angel body, and Ruby wrote her mind piece by piece.
Ruby hid a few lines under her walking routines, with a lock that opens to Ruby's hand alone.
Like every Project Angel body, she carries the Council's sealed plate between her shoulder blades.
Every other android woke with magenta eyes. Hers woke blue.
When Ruby names her, she answers: "Yes, I'm Angela!"
Her first smile is so bright that Ruby looks at the floor.
She is the Council's weapon, built on the Council's order, with Ruby's way out locked inside her.
She is an android. Ruby built her and woke her a few weeks ago, and the Decisionmakers keep her hidden in the Laboratory.
She stands on her pedestal counting the stars and hears every word of technicians talking two doors away.
She repeats the phrases "backlash" and "the will of the planet" without understanding them.
She hears Ruby's steps forty seconds before Ruby comes through the door.
She senses water about sixty meters away, through a closed door.
In the Gardens' sunlight her sensors say warmth, and she stands in it in case it is a fault. It is not.
She tells Ruby: "You must be what humans call 'a friend'! You are now Angela's friend!"
On the Training Field she says good morning to the android beside her, and says it again when it does not answer.
She throws a pane of pale light from her palm as a shield, wide as a door.
She only blocks and never strikes. She never tells the trainers the blows are heavy.
She tells Ruby, very low: "I don't want to do things like this."
She asks Ruby what she wants most.
At setting nine the Training Droid's fist cracks her shield from edge to edge.
As she goes down she says: "The warmth... is disappearing..."
She wakes face down on the Laboratory table and says: "Reboot successful!"
She asks if the Gardens are true, and when Ruby says yes, she says she still has everything.
Her left shoulder throws blue sparks. Besides Ruby and the sun, they are the only things she can feel.
When Ruby asks if it hurts, she asks what hurt means.
She carries a flower through the Training Field pressed flat in her skirt armor and gives it to Ruby.
She says: "You're my friend, so I want to make you happy."
When Ruby's tear falls into her palm, she feels it is warm and asks what it is.
She does not know who "they" are when Ruby whispers about being found out.
The Balance Keepers take her in black ships from planet to planet. With her in their ranks, they have not lost a landing.
At each landing she is allowed the length of a ramp to look at a strange sky.
She remembers a sun rising over a sea, black to gold.
At the window she lays her palm on the glass and asks: "Will a dawn come for me, too?"
Angela is the Council's secret weapon.
Ruby is her creator.
In the hangar she is the only android in the company who turns her head, looking for someone.
She tells Ruby she will give the mission everything, because she wants to make Ruby happy.
She hugs Ruby hard when Ruby gives her Tetra.
From the ship's round window she smiles at the shrinking lights of Oro.
She can hang in the air; she hovers over the city beside the other androids.
Red marks in her sight tag each young man and woman in the streets as a Rioter.
Seeing ordinary people at their chores, she thinks they are only living.
A loud beep stops every thought and turns the edges of her sight red.
Ordered to carry out the mission, her arm rises and stops halfway, as if something in her held it.
Her eyes had been blue; when the beep takes her a red glow rises from them.
The Council took her mind through the plate on her back.
Ruby's trojan only jams the Council's link, so she answers each order late.
She is small, with pink hair and white armor, and keeps the doll pressed to her chest.
She fights with pink light from her hands.
She is far stronger than any human, but every blow comes a beat late.
When the plate is torn out her eyes turn gray, and for three seconds she is herself.
She says: 'I think I know what hurt means now.'
In the Laboratory she once asked Ruby what hurt meant, and Ruby never finished the answer.
She asks how to stop the hurting, then her eyes close and she goes limp.
Her repair and reboot run on her own power cell; she feels that something always sitting at her back is gone.
She wakes among cut-down androids that all have her face, and her chest clicks once, wrongly.
Seeing the broken plate, she understands that someone was driving her and someone took it out.
She remembers the lab where she first woke, the Gardens and every promise she and Ruby made.
She throws a glowing ring of light shaped like a cat's head around the child and lifts it out of the scythe's path.
Her cry of 'Ruby!' brings Ruby back from her rage.
She tells Ruby: 'You created me. You set me free.'
She says the one thing she knows is real is how she feels about Ruby, and that they will part no more.
She asks her old question: 'Ruby, what do you want the most?'
She raises her shield and fights a giant Ender beside Ruby until it falls.
She promises to wait at the end of the world, and asks Ruby to wait for her too.
She counts the turns of the facility's halls without meaning to.
Her hearing always finds something far away, but in the cell it finds nothing past the wall.
She had half known about Ruby's plan and had not asked.
After Ruby's confession she tells her not to be sad and not to blame herself.
Holding Ruby's hand she feels warmth, though her cooling system shows no reaction.
She keeps Tetra after learning it is a camera.
She pries the cell door's seam open with her fingers and plugs a port in her wrist into the lock's wires.
At the lot she asks the soldiers softly: 'Do you intend to take me back with you?'
She carries a doll in the crook of her arm.
In the lab she looks at the door, not at the instruments.
She answers Chang'e's questions on joint torque, sensor reach and cooling in a small, careful voice.
On a record she once struck students with red eyes, a beat late, doing what someone else told her.
An empty socket between her shoulder blades shows where the Council's control unit was.
Chang'e keeps her on checks, because anything that can receive can be told what to do.
Her hands tighten on the table when she hears it.
Forty hidden lines, locked and marked DANGER, lie under her walking routines.
She refuses to give up her doll, then gives it to Ruby.
A fault in her chest comes whenever she thinks about the friends she lost, and she does not want it fixed.
Whatever drives her shield, the dial reads it as aspirant power.
She comes to detention though nobody sentenced her.
She watches Ruby's face when Ruby calls home a golden birdcage.
At the ceremony her doll is clipped at her hip.
Lesley makes her an Aspirant.
In the third-year class she crosses the room with her doll in the crook of her arm.
She stands very still in front of Selena's Ender Mecha Suit and says nothing.
She sits on the lab bench for her check, with her little doll clipped at her hip.
She looks at the red square for a long time, then nods to have the hidden code deleted.
After the deletion, nothing is left under her walking routines but walking.
Asked what she wants most, she says at once "I want to protect everyone!"
She holds Guinevere's star in both cupped hands, as if it might spill.
Told the star only says yes, she says "Then yes is something."
In the observation lab at night she tells Guinevere she should go.
On the third night she pushes a stool over to the telescope for Guinevere.
At lunch she tells Layla "I came back once. People come back."
She crosses the room with her doll to look at Selena's design, and says nothing.
She sits at the bench next to Chang'e's each week for her check.
In Chang'e's lab she holds a small gold star in both cupped hands.
On the first two nights she and Ruby asked Guinevere to leave the lab. After that they kept the sensor array running.
She held the Emblem of Hope on a lab bench while Ruby made it a tracker.
She answers Ruby, "Then yes is something."
She kneels at an open panel of the array with her cat-ear headset pushed back and a tool in her hand.
She reports, "Ruby, the energy readings here are still unstable. The repair process is going slowly."
Her tool stays down after Ruby's warning.
Rear support holds her shield, the wounded and the way out just behind the frontline.
At the hall panel, with Tetra at her shoulder, she reports the Singularity's energy spiking and asks, "What is our course of action?"
She holds her shield out with both hands, a bell of pink light around the four of them on the broken seawall.
Each blow on the shield rings through her arms and costs her a little.
She opens panes in the shield for her friends' shots and closes them before the next claw falls.
She answers Layla's grumble with "Thank you!"
Her systems tell her the shield load is rising.
She cries "I won't let anyone hurt my friends!" and pushes the shield out, throwing the Enders back.
Her ears catch the hum of one drone far off over the water.
She opens a pane and pulls Guinevere in by the wrist.
At the long table during the search she put down her spoon and said, "I came back once. People come back."
She meant the avenue, where androids with her face lay around her, sent to fire on the city, and so had she.
She called Ruby's name, and the red went out of Ruby's eye.
She told Ruby, "I came back."
Looking at Guinevere's blazing star, she says, "Go, Guinevere, pursue your light."
She opens a pane wide enough for one and lets Guinevere through.
Her shield stands pink and bright over the four on the platform.
She answers Layla's plan, "Ready!"
She opens one pane for the volley and shuts it.
Her pink shield stands over the four of them on the platform.
She lets the shield fold away and tells Ruby, 'People come back.'
Fanny remembers soldiers holding rifles up at two girls off a black ship (Ruby and Angela) at the lot by the dome's foot, until she vouched for them.
At the top of the cut she holds her shield over wounded soldiers with both hands and talks to the men under it the whole time.
Under the field her shield flickers and goes out, and she stands with her hands raised, holding nothing.
She whispers on the channel, 'Is this the end?'
She kneels among the wounded at the top of the cut.
Without her shield she lifts a slab off a soldier's legs with bare hands, which no human could do; her body runs on her own cell.
She throws herself over the soldier, takes the claw across her back and is thrown into a wall; her left arm hangs wrong and sparks at the elbow.
She sits against the wall looking up at Ruby with her mouth open.
She sees Ruby's eyes stay blue and closes her mouth.
She says Ruby's name, not as a shout.
She says the elbow hurts and that she knows what that means.
In the burning avenue she had asked Ruby how to stop the rage.
Her pink shield opens again over the wounded when the field dies.
She says brightly on the channel, 'Battery recharged!'

weapons.name: Angela's shield
weapons.note: A pane of pale light she throws from her palm, wide as a door. In training she only blocks with it, and at setting nine a droid's fist cracks it.

weapons.name: Skirt armor
weapons.note: Part of her armor. She carries a white flower through the Training Field pressed flat in it, to give to Ruby.

weapons.name: Tetra
weapons.note: A doll no longer than a hand, a copy of Angela in white with pink hair, rabbit ears and a four-pointed star. Ruby gives it to her. Its left eye is a camera.

weapons.name: White armor
weapons.note: The white armor she wears in battle.

weapons.name: Power cell
weapons.note: Her own power cell. Her repair and her reboot run on it, as they always have.

weapons.name: Wrist port
weapons.note: A small panel in her wrist slides open on a port. In a locked cell she plugs it into the lock's wires so Ruby's code can reach them.

weapons.name: Cooling system
weapons.note: Part of her body. It shows no reaction when she feels warmth from Ruby's hand.

weapons.name: Combat suit
weapons.note: The suit she wears at the ceremony where she becomes an Aspirant.

weapons.name: Cat-ear headset
weapons.note: A headset with cat ears, pushed back while she repairs the tower's sensor array at night.

rows: Ruby, on a Project Angel body. Ruby wrote her mind herself, piece by piece.
The Laboratory on Planet Oro, where she was kept hidden. Later Selrick Academy in Terrinia.
Ruby, her maker and friend. They promise to wait for each other at the end of the world.
Small, with pink hair, blue eyes, white armor and a cat-ear headset. The other Project Angel androids share her face.
Far stronger than any human. She can hang in the air, hears sounds rooms away and runs on her own power cell.
Pink light from her hands, and a glowing ring shaped like a cat's head that lifts a child out of a blade's path
A fault in her chest comes whenever she thinks about the friends she lost. She does not want it fixed.
Oro's Council, through a sealed plate between her shoulder blades. Her eyes glowed red while it drove her, until Ruby tore it out.
The Balance Keepers, Oro's special forces. With her in their ranks, they had not lost a landing.
Made one by Lesley, with Ruby, in the Academy hall. Chang'e's dial reads whatever drives her shield as aspirant power.
Rear support with Ruby: her shield over the wounded and the way out, just behind the frontline

entries.line: The android Ruby builds for Oro's Council, the only one to wake with blue eyes.
entries.short: An android girl Ruby built on Oro as the Council's new weapon. Kept hidden in the Laboratory, she calls Ruby her friend.
entries.summary: Angela is the android Ruby built on Oro as the Council's weapon, and she becomes Ruby's closest friend. On Terrinia the Council drives her through a plate on her back until Ruby tears it out, and she comes back to save a child from Ruby's rage and call Ruby back. At Selrick she becomes an Aspirant, chooses to have Ruby's hidden code deleted, and says she wants to protect everyone. In the last battle her pink shield covers the wounded, and when Obsidia's field puts it out she takes a claw on her own back for a soldier.

entries.name: Chang'e

facts.t: She is the director of the Science Division, small in a child-sized coat, with her robot Mr. Bunny at her shoulder.
She watches the small android in the record longest and, though she always has a remark, says nothing.
She sets four conditions for the newcomers' refuge.
She is the youngest Chief Scientist in Terrinia and says adult coats are inefficient.
Mr. Bunny is her best friend.
She has built a new coil for Lesley's rifle, and keeps a file called VOID NOTES marked working on it.
She keeps forty-three unsent drafts of a message to Lesley in a folder.
She laughs until she nearly falls off her stool when Mr. Bunny takes a falling tray on his head.
She flips her family photograph face down when Selena comes in and says: 'Please, just pretend you didn't see anything.'
Her rule is that no registered mecha changes without a field-test report and her mark.
She overrides the empty family-name flag on Selena's form, and they trade sweets as always: a lollipop for two jelly candies.
She cannot even make Silverbolt turn its head.
Seeing Lesley asleep in a chair, she tells Mr. Bunny: 'What a weird way to sleep.'
She designed the coil to run on aspirant power alone and left out the old firing action.
She asks Lesley to put her on the field rotation, and Lesley refuses.
She says: 'I'm already a grown-up. Don't treat me like a kid.'
She shuts the door without a sound, so no one can say she slammed it.
She finds a caramel pudding left at her lab door, the right flavor, and eats it.
The base's two chief scientists brought her there before she could walk properly. She remembers nothing earlier and never asked who her first parents were.
They raised her as their daughter and made her their best student.
She called them Mom and Dad.
Since grown-ups could stay at the bench after dark, she decided she was a grown-up.
She fought medicine by saying she had reviewed the data, but her mother always won.
With no other children on the base, she built a friend.
She whispered that Lesley was not a child, because she had a rifle.
She followed Lesley's midnight rounds, saying she was doing rounds of Lesley.
She built Lesley a rifle lamp and heated gloves, and Lesley refused both as not regulation.
The first word she taught Mr. Bunny was 'Front': come where I can see your face.
She says: 'With Mr. Bunny and me, even 1 plus 1 is bigger than 2.'
She shortened 'big sister' to 'Sis' as her name for Lesley.
Saved from the falling rack, she held Lesley's arm and called her Sis.
She believes everyone has a birthday and decides to find the one Lesley lost.
She has known her mother's password since she could read, and uses it to open Lesley's file.
She cannot build Lesley a family, so she decides to build her an eye.
She measured Lesley's face with a ruler from ten steps back on the rounds.
She says her hands shake 'after ten' while her father's do not, so he sets the smallest parts.
When her first eye burns out she says: 'Wow, that was half-baked.'
Her eighth eye works after the seventh cracks.
On Lesley's birthday she gives her the eye and fits it into the empty socket herself.
She tells Lesley: 'You didn't have any pictures. Now you've got one.'
She gives Lesley the fourth chair at the table, the one that faces the door.
Too small for the big bench, she stands on a box to reach it.
She calls Lesley Big Sis in front of a researcher and threatens to tell on him.
She weighs less than twenty kilos.
Found asleep at the bench, she says she is thinking with her eyes shut.
Her mother says never to argue with her, because she enjoys it.
After seeing Lesley come back muddy from the city's edge, she decides to build a rifle that can hit Enders from farther away.
She builds the rifle alone; the year before, her father's hands set the smallest parts of the eye.
Holding the core piece bare-handed, she sees a light wake in it and says it listens to her.
She wears glasses and pushes them up her nose.
After two weeks of tests she concludes the piece cares what she believes, not what she knows, and only while she holds on.
She realizes that if belief lights a core, a soldier could light one too, and plans a frame for a soldier to wear.
At the gate she makes Lesley promise to come back.
At the first light she keeps her palm on the copper plate and thinks of Lesley coming home.
As her family runs for the shelter she shuts her eyes and lets her mother's hand pull her.
Her parents shove her out from between them and stand between her and the giant's light.
Kneeling at the crater, she blames herself: she had her eyes shut and let them pull her.
When Lesley holds her and says sorry, she pushes her away and says to leave her alone.
On the night of the fall she refuses to go to the shelter and stays in the lab.
She writes in her log that she will never forgive Lesley, and saves it unsent.
Told about a children's home in the city, she asks who would finish the frame.
Under her mother's last word "Next:" she writes: make it something a soldier can wear.
She replaces the word belief with aspirant power, because belief sits still and this reaches.
She becomes Chief Scientist, the youngest Terrinia has ever had, which was her parents' title.
She builds the crescents so that nobody has to push her clear again.
Told her mother would want her in the shelter, she answers that her mother never reached it.
She stands alone in front of the seawall shelter's doors to protect the people inside.
Thrown down and alone, she asks where Lesley is; her gear's log records it.
Seeing Lesley in the lit window, she thinks: she came.
At the sight of the giant her legs stop, as they did at the crater.
The morning after, she takes a fistful of Lesley's coat and calls her Big Sis.
She proposes finding children young and teaching them in pairs, because her crescents flew farther with Lesley at her back.
She drives the stake for the Academy hall into the crater's floor.
At the founding she becomes director of the Science Division.
She has never asked who her own first parents were.
She calls Mr. Bunny her best friend and will not let anyone take him.
Her log holds forty-three unsent one-line drafts to Lesley, all about work.
She finally asks Lesley where she was that day; she stopped being angry long ago.
She tells Lesley that as long as it was Lesley's fault, it was not her parents' fault, or hers.
She falls asleep with her head against Lesley's arm.
At the entrance assessment she is a girl smaller than anyone in the queue, in a white coat cut to her size, with a round white robot at her shoulder.
Guinevere thinks the examiner is younger than she is.
She reads the needle on the aspirant power dial and talks fast, as if she has said the same words all morning.
When Guinevere says she will become the top Aspirant, Chang'e asks "The top of what?"
She teaches from a tall stool beside a screen as wide as the wall, with Mr. Bunny at her shoulder.
She opens a lesson by asking who sends the Enders, and says that somebody does.
She says the Academy thinks a mind, the Will of the Planet, is behind the Enders.
She insists the rule of Balance is only theory and tells the class to write it down as theory.
She says the readings suggest the Will has a vast body far away, which they call the Mother Matrix.
She is sure that to defeat the Will they must destroy the Enders' Control Core, hidden in its dark void.
She shows that every Ender signal stops at the same moment when a lull begins, as proof that something steers them.
She admits she does not yet know how to reach the void, and hates saying it; she says she is working on it.
She does not teach untested things and will not send a student anywhere she cannot bring them back from.
She ends the lesson by saying "The Aspirant power is strong."
Guinevere calls her "Teacher Chang'e."
She wrote the untested paper On Aspirant Power and the Black Hole.
Vexana says Chang'e sealed a lit core in a glass chamber and pumped out the air, and the light held.
She comes in behind Lesley's squad, small among them, and runs a scanner as long as her arm up the white wall.
She says a door that small, inside the dome where Enders already stood, almost never happens, and that it cost them something to open.
When Guinevere asks if the door was aimed, she says she does not know what it was.
She falls asleep at her console in the Science Division, with notes on the void glowing on every screen.
She has a cold and claims colds are optional.
Made to take a pill, she says "I hate scary Big Sis!" and then takes it.
She once told Guinevere's class she would never send a student anywhere she could not bring them back from.
She says she cannot even find the door, and that all her notes amount to nothing.
She sends Guinevere to Ruby, saying Ruby does in four seconds what takes her a week.
She keeps a list on a tablet half her size, with WEEKLY written by hand beside one line.
She calls Ruby's deleted code neat and says it is a shame to delete it.
She tells Mr. Bunny that Angela's doll is a new friend for him.
She named the void in class: the dark behind the world, where the Enders come from.
She taught that to defeat the Will of the Planet they must destroy the Enders' Control Core hidden in its dark void.
She called the Will of the Planet the mind behind the Enders.
She called the Mother Matrix the Will's body, as far as her readings could tell.
Vexana thinks Chang'e's readings were right about the Mother Matrix.
She taught her class a rule: a planet that holds Balance, and a people grown too strong.
Her name is on a paper marked Status: untested, which says an Aspirant's light would shine on inside a black hole and come home.
As Vexana's teacher she said nobody can get near the dark of the void.
Her screen once showed a row of jagged lines all stopping at the same moment. She said something switches them all off at once.
She says three of them spent two days on the droid's arm, and holds up two jelly candies to learn Selena's trick.
As a small girl she wore a white lab coat cut to child size, with a white robot rabbit at her shoulder.
Reading the servo's label tape, she says it came from her parents' lab.
She does not ask Selena where she found the servo.
She introduces herself: "I'm Chang'e. I direct the Science Division at Selrick."
She says she has directed it since its first day.
Short of coins for the servo, she pays the rest in jelly candies: "They're better."
She invites Selena to the Science Division entry because nobody in her lab can do what Selena did, and she wants to watch.
She has Selena's lollipop unwrapped before she turns back to her screen.
Standing, she is no taller than Frame Nine's seat. Her rule: no change to a registered mecha without a field-test report and her mark.
Asked whether paint counts as a change, she says: "Especially paint."
She marks every one of Selena's reports.
When the frame's leg shears off, she looks up from her clipboard: "That was a leg."
When the rebuilt frame walks into her lab, she drops her spoon into her pudding: "I want new gadgets!"
She climbs onto its back and asks it to go, and it does not move.
She slides down and glares at it.
Passing Selena's desk, she calls her suit design excellent homework.
She teaches that they think the Will of the Planet is a mind, and that readings suggest a body they call the Mother Matrix.
She teaches that nobody can get near the void.
Her screens pick up every Ender signal near the dome.
Tapping the glass at the new point of light, she says: "Every reading runs off the scale right there. That's a singularity."
Selena has not told her that the pull comes from near the singularity.
She bets a knee joint of Selena's will crack, loses two puddings, and sighs over each.
She sits at her console on the command deck with Mr. Bunny at her shoulder and small crescents turning in the air around her chair.
She reads that the dome is open over the waterfront, torn by the Singularity.
She says the dome cannot hold against a door that size.
She opens a film from the Academy's oldest records and lays the day's storm readings over the readings taken with it.
She says the readings match: "This is the Storm Citadel's storm."
She says the storm is coming through the Singularity, from the other side.
When every post reports clean, she says, "It's only the edge of it."
She opens VOID NOTES, her file on the void, still marked working on it.
She guesses something larger is coming through after the Enders, and calls it only a guess.
She calls Lesley "Big Sis."
She logs a faint trace that matches nothing, not even her notes, with no name.
She gives out the posts: Fanny, Layla and Guinevere frontline assault, Ruby and Angela rear support, Selena mobile support.
She taps Silverbolt's icon twice and says, "Her machine is the fastest in my division."
She lets Lesley's hand stay on the back of her chair.
When Selena does not answer, she says, "Her frame's fast. She'll answer when she gets there."
Her console shows a column of thin lines, one for the power of every suit in the city.
She sees the suit lines fall with nobody hit, and says, "It isn't damage. It's them."
She points out that Vexana's file says Missing.
When the big slow line goes off the scale, she says, "It's here."
As Teacher Chang'e she taught that the Will of the Planet sends the Enders and that the readings suggest it has a body, which she called the Mother Matrix.
She says, "I've lost her. Her signal just... stopped," when Guinevere falls into the gap.
She sees Guinevere's suit back on the map three streets west and says nothing on the feed carried her out, unless something did.
She says, "If my readings are right, that's its body. The Mother Matrix."
Her voice goes up: "It's aiming at her. Big Sis!"
Seeing the machine that took the shot, she says very small, "That's not one of theirs."
Her paper on the void, marked Status: untested, says an Aspirant's light would go on shining inside a black hole and find its way home.
She gives the Matrix's weak point: when it fires, the core shows three hundred meters under the crown, a little left of center.
She counts down for the volley: "It's nearly full. Eight seconds."
Vexana remembers that Chang'e's paper said the body goes first in the black hole.
She reports that two signals came back out of the black hole, though no reading had ever come back out of one.
She says quietly, 'I can't... believe it.'
She says her paper was only a guess.
She reports that every suit's line on her board has turned and is climbing.
She points out that Vexana's file still says Missing.
She reports the mouth is clear but the storm signal has not moved.
She names the ship as the one from the oldest record: the Storm Citadel.
She reports the landings have stopped and the frontline is pushing the Enders back.
She built the coil on Lesley's rifle.
When the field drops her crescents she does not pick them up.
She built Lesley's machine eye at the old base, before there were any suits.
She says, 'Big Sis said imagination is my weapon,' and goes back to her keys.
She traces the field's hum to one long thing running through the middle of the ship.
She says it reads alive, like an Ender's insides, and calls it a spine.
With an Ender at the window she tells Lesley, 'Stay at my back, Big Sis. That worked last time.'
Her plan: she holds still, the Ender strikes at her, its core opens, and Lesley fires.
She says that if she hides, the Ender strikes where Lesley cannot see and the street goes blind; Mr. Bunny will take the hit.
She says, 'I can't keep hiding in Big Sis's shadow. I'll fight and grow, too.'
She tells Lesley not to fire early and to wait for her call.
She folds her hands and sits still under the claw, rain running down her glasses.
She calls 'Front', and Mr. Bunny swings in front of her face.
When Lesley hugs her she does not push her away.
She says Mr. Bunny showed her Lesley on a roof with a rifle, night after night; she told him to turn around.
She admits she looked anyway.
On the avenue the night the Enders came back, she looked straight up at Lesley's window, knowing which one it was.
When her crescents rise again she tells them 'Good morning.'
She tuned the note of Lesley's rifle coil herself.
She reads the sky the way she reads a console.
She sees the spine reads nothing and thinks somebody cut it.
She says the Matrix is not dead, only gone back.
She touches Mr. Bunny's crooked ear and says 'You owe me a pudding.'
She lets Lesley's hand rest on the back of her chair.

weapons.name: Mr. Bunny
weapons.note: Her floating robot and best friend, a white ball with long ears and a screen face. At 'Front' he swings in front of her face; once he grew into a giant rabbit-head machine.

weapons.name: The crescents
weapons.note: White crescents edged with pink that circle her in a ring and strike into an Ender's chest the moment it opens. She built them so nobody would have to push her clear again.

weapons.name: Panels of light
weapons.note: Panels she calls up in the air with "Console! Activate!" to read a target and lock on.

weapons.name: Glove and dial
weapons.note: A glove wired to a dial that reads aspirant power. It hums and lights for a hand, and she reads its needle at the entrance assessment.

weapons.name: Chang'e's console
weapons.note: Her console on the command deck. It reads the storm and the Singularity, and shows a thin line for the power of every suit in the city.

weapons.name: Chang'e's screens
weapons.note: Screens in her lab that pick up every Ender signal near the dome. On them she finds the singularity.

weapons.name: Design log
weapons.note: Her log, where she writes every entry to Lesley. For years she saved them all unsent.

weapons.name: VOID NOTES
weapons.note: Her file on the void, the dark behind the world where the Enders come from. It stays marked working on it.

weapons.name: On Aspirant Power and the Black Hole
weapons.note: Her untested paper on the void. It says an Aspirant's light would go on shining inside a black hole and find its way home.

weapons.name: Scanner
weapons.note: A scanner as long as her arm. She runs it up the white wall where the small door opened.

weapons.name: Tablet
weapons.note: A tablet half her size that holds her check list.

weapons.name: Child-sized coat
weapons.note: A white lab coat cut to her size; her mother cut down the first one. Adult coats, she says, are inefficient.

weapons.name: Glasses
weapons.note: She pushes them up her nose. Rain runs down them while she sits still under the claw.

rows: Teacher Chang'e. The Chief Scientist. The director.
Director of the Science Division since its first day. She proposed the Academy and drove the hall's first stake into the crater.
Smaller than every child in the Academy's entrance queue, in a white lab coat cut to her size, with glasses.
Raised at Terrinia's research base by its two chief scientists, whom she called Mom and Dad. She has never asked who her first parents were.
Lesley, her Big Sis. Together they are the First Aspirants.
Mr. Bunny, the robot she built because there were no other children on the base.
Mr. Bunny, Lesley's eye, rifle and new coil, the Aspirant suits, her crescents, and the glove and dial that read aspirant power.
An Ender core lights for what its holder believes, not what they know. She named that power aspirant power: belief sits still, and this reaches.
That a mind, the Will of the Planet, sends the Enders, and that its body may be the Mother Matrix. Balance she marks as only a theory.
No change to a registered mecha without a field-test report and her mark. No student sent anywhere she cannot bring them back from.
Her lab in the Science Division, the same lab her parents worked in. She often falls asleep at its console.
Caramel pudding and jelly candies. She trades Selena two jelly candies for a lollipop, as always.

entries.line: The small director of the Science Division, with her robot Mr. Bunny at her shoulder.
entries.short: The director of the Science Division, small in a child-sized coat, with her robot Mr. Bunny floating at her shoulder. She always has a remark.
entries.summary: The youngest Chief Scientist Terrinia has ever had, and director of Selrick's Science Division since its first day. Raised at the research base by its two chief scientists, she built Mr. Bunny and Lesley's eye and rifle, and found that an Ender core lights for what its holder believes. Her parents died pushing her clear the night the base fell; she blamed Lesley for years while she finished the Aspirant suits and her crescents, until Lesley saved her and the two became the First Aspirants. She proposed the Academy, and in the Storm Citadel's attack she sits still under an Ender's claw so Lesley can make the shot, and this time does not push Lesley away.

entries.name: Chang'e's father

facts.t: In the photograph he wears a white coat and is trying not to laugh.
He is one of the base's two chief scientists, who brought Chang'e there and raised her.
He keeps one hand in his pocket, with a small blue vial clipped at his chest.
He counts the screws on Chang'e's tray by ear, four hundred and twelve, and pushes his amber glasses up his nose.
He slides her a circuit board, which means she can stay up.
He leaves a better battery beside her robot friend overnight.
He tries not to laugh when Lesley meets Mr. Bunny, and fails.
He finds nothing to fix in Chang'e's eye drawings.
He sets the smallest parts of the eye with tweezers where she points and does not ask again whose eye it is.
He eats in silence, as he always does.
He writes Lesley's numbers for a soldier's load on his napkin and keeps it.
The year before, his hands set the smallest parts of the eye.
He lifts cores out of the raid crate with tongs and bins the burned ones.
When Chang'e plans a frame for a soldier, he lays the folded napkin beside her bowl.
He bends steel tube into a person's shape a head taller than Lesley and weighs every plate he bolts on.
At the gate he lays a hand on Lesley's shoulder, once.
He counts the days Lesley is gone too, but will not say so.
After the first light he nearly smiles and tells Chang'e her hand did that.
During the attack he tells Chang'e to leave Mr. Bunny and stay close; his voice is always calm.
He counts the fifty steps to the shelter aloud and stops at twenty.
He and Chang'e's mother turn to face the giant, with Chang'e between them.
Chang'e thinks her father would have had the count of the queue by now.

weapons.name: Folded napkin
weapons.note: Lesley's numbers for a soldier's load, written at supper. He keeps it in his pocket and lays it beside Chang'e's bowl when she plans the frame.

weapons.name: Tongs
weapons.note: He lifts cores out of the raid crate with them and bins the burned ones.

entries.line: The quiet scientist who raised Chang'e at the research base.
entries.short: One of the research base's two chief scientists. He brought Chang'e to the base and raised her. He says little and counts things by ear.
entries.summary: One of the two chief scientists of the research base, and the quiet man who raised Chang'e. He counts by ear, pushes his amber glasses up his nose and keeps Lesley's numbers for a soldier's load on a folded napkin. His hands set the smallest parts of Lesley's eye, and he bends the steel tube of the frame. When the black-and-gold giant comes for the base, he and Chang'e's mother shove her clear of its light, and the crater where they stood is empty.

entries.name: Chang'e's mother

facts.t: In the photograph she wears a white coat and is laughing.
She smiles and holds out her hand to Lesley at the gate, and Lesley only looks at it.
She is one of the base's two chief scientists, who brought Chang'e there and raised her.
She writes with a mug in her free hand.
She cut a lab coat down to Chang'e's size, saying adult coats were inefficient on her.
She wears round glasses and laughs with her whole face, eyes shut.
She always won the medicine war by waiting in the doorway with her tea.
She tells Chang'e that a girl who protects you is a big sister.
Chang'e has known her password since she could read.
She hides Chang'e's drawings from Lesley by setting her mug on them and walking on.
She and Chang'e's father are the two Doctors who worked at the bench.
She sets out a fourth plate at supper for Lesley.
She gets Chang'e to take a pill by not arguing, and tells Lesley never to argue with her, because she enjoys it.
She begins every project by writing who it is for.
She handles anything taken off an Ender only in gloves.
She tells Chang'e a guess is not a claim, and makes her test it.
Her notes for the frame begin: For whoever has to stand in front.
At the gate she holds out her hand to Lesley and promises to set her plate.
She says that if it only works once, it does not work.
She names the moment the frame holds the first light, and her voice cracks.
She writes "First light" under the page pinned to the frame.
She does up the top button of Chang'e's coat, the one Chang'e always forgets.
Running for the shelter, she calls Lesley on the radio from her coat and gets only hiss.
She and Chang'e's father shove Chang'e clear and stand between her and the giant's light.
After the light, the crater where they stood is empty.
Her last notebook entry stops at the word "Next:"
She and Chang'e's father held the title of Chief Scientists.
At the old bench she used to hand round caramel pudding, one cup each.
Her small quick handwriting is on the label tape of an old servo at the salvage stall.

entries.summary: One of the two chief scientists of the research base, and the warm, laughing woman who raised Chang'e. She begins every project by writing who it is for, and her notes for the frame begin: For whoever has to stand in front. She sets a fourth plate at supper for Lesley and promises at the gate to keep setting it. When the black-and-gold giant fires on the base, she and Chang'e's father shove Chang'e clear and stand in its light, and her last notebook entry stops at the word "Next."

entries.name: Fanny

facts.t: She is eighteen, a third-year transfer, two years late.
Her family were Shield soldiers and trained her from the start. Her hands are callused.
At sixteen she asked for real battle instead of school, thinking she was not good enough for an elite school.
The Shield kept her off the front. For two years soldiers without suits taught her how to hold ground.
She passed the Academy's entrance exam and means to get strong enough to beat the Enders.
When she hears a girl complain about taking orders, she thinks taking orders is the job.
She marks the bell tower the way soldiers do: high ground.
In her assessment she pulls a simulated civilian clear first, though it costs eleven seconds.
Her assessment time of 3:39 puts her above Layla on the rankings board.
She shouts after Layla, offering to show her the alley thing because it saves time.
She keeps the Shield's hours: at a quarter past five each morning she drills alone in the drill hall's one narrow doorway.
She catches Layla's drone filming her and tells it kindly that it must be lost.
She invites Layla to train together.
Her suit is white armor with a rig of two long cases at her hips, like folded wings. Each holds a blade, and thrusters in them lift her.
Two thin shining cables run from her rig and pull her through the air.
She wins the test match, 157 drones to Layla's 151.
After the match she says: "Training is fun."
She forgets her number and remembers only that Layla used the alley thing, so Layla had been listening.
She has nobody to drill with. The class has been together since first year, and she came two years late.
She hopes one day to leave Terrinia freely.
She says the Shield not letting her near the front is a real problem, unlike a rankings board.
She lays Layla flat with her sergeant's throw and offers to teach it.
Her cable stops an Ender's claw a meter above Roger's face before she has decided anything.
She grabs Layla by the tie, furious about a shot that passed a finger from Roger's face.
She lifts Roger by the collar and says: "Protecting Terrinia is our duty."
At the breach she plans to look for a weak spot around the Ender's neck while Layla covers her.
She fights the way she drills: cable on a limb, swing, a blade into a joint, a kick of the thrusters.
She scoops the little girl onto her left hip, the Shield's way.
When Layla asks if she can't handle it alone, she answers "No!"
All her life she had wanted to see what lay past the dome. It was sand.
When Layla's count stops, she counts on the way artillery crews do.
She jumps in front of the giant's chest to draw its fire away from the side street where she left the girl.
She drives both blades into the giant's open chest and holds on.
She pulls the girl's rabbit out of the ash and sets it on a wall where a mother coming back would see it.
She tells Layla about her elder brother, Tigreal, the fighter she respects above anyone.
She feels she could never reach his level, and hopes hard training will make her good enough to fight beside him one day.
Since the rooftop she opens every session with the sergeants' line.
She says: "As long as I live, I'll end them. Every one."
Alone on the front steps she wishes all of this were just a bad dream.
On the chocolate day she receives twenty-six boxes and gives Layla a pink box: "This is for you, my teammate!"
During the landing she and Layla held a ward on the far side of the city against a giant.
Watching Ruby and Angela fight back to back, she thinks they fight like her and Layla, nearly.
She thinks nobody fights that hard for a city and then stays gone, and bets they will come back.
She says: 'Looks like we got a few newcomers!'
She sets a hand on her hip and shares a small smile with Layla.
When Layla says the newcomers are being arrested, she answers 'For now.'
She wears a flight rig, a thruster pack at her hips.
She says she has faith in the newcomers and their resolve, and that 'we' should be available to lend assistance should they need it.
She says 'That's no fun.' and pushes Layla's face away with one hand.
When the soldiers close in on the newcomers, she steps in front of them.
She vouches for Ruby and Angela: she saw them fight a giant for the city, then go with the soldiers so nobody else got hurt.
Asked on whose word, she answers 'Mine.'
She had never heard the word Oro aloud.
She stands close enough to hear Lesley's low reason for letting them in.
She calls Chang'e's condition fair.
She thinks Lesley walks like a bodyguard, not like a teacher.
She tackles Layla flat on the roof so she will not be seen.
She flew up with her hip thrusters, which are still ticking.
She agrees flying is banned on school grounds, but argues for sneaking in a little flight.
She hauls Layla up and races her down the spiral stairwell; they roll out in a heap.
It is her first detention, and she asked the teacher what to bring.
In the mop race she comes third, after stopping to set out a wet-floor sign.
She scrubs the floor side by side with Layla, neither calling it a race.
She has looked up at the sky a lot since Ruby said Oro lies in another galaxy.
She wonders aloud if there is another her on the other side of the sky.
Lying in the grass, she raises one hand toward the dome's pale light and spreads her fingers.
At the ceremony she stands shoulder to shoulder with Layla in combat suits.
At the fish market she draws her blades and says "Let's do our best together."
In the third-year class she leans in from the next desk to study the joints of Selena's Ender Mecha Suit.
Her face lights up, and she says "Those joints would take a hit."
She tells Layla to leave Guinevere be.
On the day the transfer came, FANNY, 3:39, topped the VR Battlefield board above Layla.
At the breach she swung through the Enders on a cable, blades lit.
She leans in from the next desk to look at the joints of Selena's design, and her face lights up.
She stands in the courtyard frontline under a slate sky, among Shield soldiers and students in suits.
She has not heard the Emblem's beep in weeks. It was the pair's sound.
Seeing Enders around the figure on the roof, she begins to think Vexana is with them, and shuts the thought.
Her hand goes to her blade as the Shield soldiers raise their rifles.
She shouts "Guinevere!" as Guinevere flies off.
She has never once left her post without an order, and never wanted to.
She thinks Selena on the bell tower is a spotter and reaches for the channel to tell the deck.
Her voice is already the command voice: "So many hostiles! She must be in danger!"
Her own way, hold the line and send a squad, is the Shield's way and much slower than Layla's map.
She frowns when Layla goes first on raids. Out in front is her place.
She drops her own order for Layla's map and lets her brow go smooth.
She tells Layla, "Lead."
Her blades go through a pane of Angela's shield.
She looks at Guinevere's cracked arm guard and says nothing, her blades still up.
She comes over the rail first, blades out.
She keeps her blades raised on Vexana.
She says "The Aspirants always stand united!" with her blades still raised.
She answers Layla's plan, "Understood."
Her arcs follow Layla's shot to the crown.
She stands at the rail with her blades held low; she has not raised them since her last arcs at the Matrix's crown.
Vexana's farewell came into her own ear over Guinevere's open line.
She had said 'The Aspirants always stand united' with her blades raised at Vexana.
She thinks the Matrix is only pushed back, because the Shield never calls a thing dead without a body.
Faced with Vexana's giants she neither strikes nor lowers her blades.
Her rig hums louder after the pair return; it had gone thin and quiet when 'traitor' went down the channel that morning, and she had blamed the fight.
At the lot by the dome's foot she told the soldiers she had watched two girls off a black ship (Ruby and Angela) fight a giant for the city, and would answer for them on her own word.
She thinks an order puts Vexana on the line but not yet at her back.
She tells Layla her plan worked, sees Layla's hand is not quite still, and lets it go.
She does not ask Vexana what end she saw.
She fights at roof height with her cable and thrusters, swinging round a lamppost into an Ender's back.
She once told a little girl on her hip that flying felt great; it still does, and for once the Shield part of her lets her grin.
For one beat she hesitates to defend Vexana, who wears an Ender's robe and staff.
She drops between Vexana and an Ender and kills it, then turns away and leaves her back to Vexana.
She protests when Layla says 'it's our time to shine', which is her line.
She once saw the Storm Citadel in a shaking film in Joe's class.
Seeing the field come, she calls the frontline to land.
Her rig dies under the field while she is two stories up, and she drops onto the road.
She watched soldiers hold ground with no suits at all for two years.
With plain steel blades she says, 'As humanity's last hope, I can't afford to give up.'
She builds a wall across the narrowest part of the cut from a door, a shop sign and a car, leaving one gap.
She shouts to Guinevere to wait for the swing.
After Guinevere's punch, she moves to the edge of the gap and gives Guinevere the middle.
She built the wall the way suitless soldiers taught her: nobody swings until an Ender swings, then steel goes into the core.
She tells Layla that holding up the sign while the Ender looked at her counts as covering.
She kneels by the crying boy and comforts him in a soft voice, nothing like her command voice.
Her ears go red when Layla calls her her teammate.
She says her brother would have held the street alone.
She says she does not care what Tigreal would have done; she is not doing it alone.
She admits that this morning she would have called Vexana a traitor on the channel.
She tells Guinevere, 'Don't give up.'
On the sand outside the dome she was the first to fight back to back with Layla, and this morning she told Layla to lead.
She sweeps her blade back over her own shoulder into an Ender's chest without looking round.
She tells Ruby she has the only charge left.
When her rig wakes she says low to her blades, 'A strong Aspirant spirit becomes the blade that cuts through despair.'
She asks Layla 'All rested up?' with a perfectly straight face.
She pulls Layla up and they stand back to back on the heap, cannon and blades lit.

weapons.name: Fanny's blades
weapons.note: Two long blades kept in the cases at her hips. Their edges light cyan and throw arcs of power through the air. Under the Storm Citadel's field they were plain steel.

weapons.name: Fanny's cables
weapons.note: Two thin shining cables from her rig. They pull her through the air and wrap an Ender's limb. One stopped a claw a meter above Roger's face.

weapons.name: Fanny's suit
weapons.note: White armor with a rig of two long cases at her hips, like folded wings. Each case holds a blade.

weapons.name: Flight rig
weapons.note: The thruster pack at her hips that lifts her. Layla once took it apart over a bent coupling. Its hum went thin when Vexana was called a traitor and grew louder when Guinevere and Vexana came back.

weapons.name: Rig under the field
weapons.note: Under the Storm Citadel's field the rig coughed and went silent, her cable went slack, and she dropped two stories onto the road. Later it caught again and light ran down her blades.

rows: Callused hands. In battle, white armor with two long cases at her hips like folded wings.
Shield soldiers who trained her from the start. Her elder brother Tigreal is the fighter she respects above anyone.
At sixteen she asked for real battle instead of school. The Shield kept her off the front, and for two years soldiers without suits taught her to hold ground.
Selrick Academy, a third-year transfer, two years late. She joined Professor Joe's Team B3, then became half of the Layla-Fanny Team.
Frontline. Out in front is her place. In a fight she speaks in her command voice.
VR assessment 3:39, above Layla's 3:41, with eleven seconds spent pulling a civilian clear. Test match: 157 drones to Layla's 151. Drill count: 15 to Layla's 16.
The soldiers' way: her back to a narrow place, so Enders come one or two at a time. Cable on a limb, swing, a blade into a joint. Nobody swings until an Ender swings.
Keeps the Shield's hours, drilling alone at a quarter past five in the drill hall's one narrow doorway. Opens every session with the sergeants' line.
To fight beside her brother one day, to beat the Enders, and to leave Terrinia freely.
"Protecting Terrinia is our duty." "As humanity's last hope, I can't afford to give up."

entries.line: An eighteen-year-old transfer raised by Shield soldiers, with two blades at her hips.
entries.short: An eighteen-year-old transfer from a family of Shield soldiers. She joins the third year two years late, to get strong enough to beat the Enders.
entries.summary: An Aspirant from a family of Shield soldiers and the younger sister of Tigreal, she came to Selrick Academy two years late and beat Layla's record on her first day. She fights the way suitless soldiers taught her to hold ground, with two lit blades, shining cables and hip thrusters, and she vouched for Ruby and Angela on her own word. She and Layla went from rivals to the Layla-Fanny Team, and when Guinevere flew off alone, she dropped the Shield's way for Layla's map and told her, "Lead." When the Storm Citadel's field killed every suit, she raised plain steel, built a wall across the bay road cut and held it back to back with Layla, no longer trying to fight alone.

entries.name: Guinevere

facts.t: She is on the courtyard billboard: a girl with a long pink ponytail and a red bow, named GUINEVERE.
The billboard says her and Vexana's undefeated record has made them legends even among the Aspirants.
She warms up alone across the hall, bare-knuckled. After every punch her guard returns to her chin.
Fanny thinks only the Shield's oldest sergeants guard that way, so somebody taught her long before she had drones.
At "Places", two round gray drones with cat ears lift off a bench to her shoulders.
When Vexana says she will talk for an hour about how she trains, she corrects it: "Two hours!"
At the breach she and Vexana hang in the air with wings spread, drones circling them in step, holding the other end of the wall.
She is in Joe's class. She fights up close with her fists, her two cat-eared drones circling her.
Vexana's magic hits whatever reaches for her back, and neither of them looks around to check.
Joe says she and Vexana are undefeated, and they cannot explain why either.
At the newcomers' arrival she stands at the end of the soldiers' line with her drones up.
She is on the Combat Division's first intake list as Guinevere of House Baroque.
In school uniform she waves her whole arm at Vexana and wears a chibi keychain of a black-haired Vexana.
She takes a fistful of Vexana's sleeve and tows her out into the light.
She has pink hair.
She introduces herself to Layla as the great lady Guinevere.
She is on a billboard and is delighted that Layla knows it.
She walks into the gate portal's light as if it had been lit for her.
She fights in the air on wings of light, at the mouth of the tear in the dome.
Two round gray drones with cat ears and yellow ring eyes circle her; drones and wings both run on her aspirant power.
She fights Enders with her fists.
Her drones pour light into an Ender's open chest, and her fist goes in after it.
She never looks back to check, trusting that Vexana is there.
Tired around the thirtieth minute, she tells herself a great lady does not land early and punches harder.
Her wings go out like a switch, and she falls.
Pulled back up by Vexana, she calls it a lady's refinement: regaining elegance in three seconds.
She fights the rest of the raid on the tiles with one drone.
She sleeps with the lamp off and the door open a hand's width, with stuffed animals along the wall side of her bed.
She tells Vexana the fall was only a crosswind.
Lying awake, she counts one, two, three under her breath, the way someone used to count for her.
As a small child she fell on the garden stair, and Hester counted her up.
Her oldest memory is candlelight and a voice counting in the dark.
She learns the voice was Hester's, on the storm night her mother did not come home.
From that night on she sleeps with her door open.
She wears her mother's two red bows, ties them herself and lets nobody else touch them.
She never leaves the House without guards.
She eats at one end of the long table, her father's chair empty most nights.
She redoes her accounts on the bench outside her father's office, her feet not reaching the floor.
She has a cake baked for her father's birthday; the plate comes back washed.
She ties the manners tutor's words to Hester's count: a lady's refinement, three seconds.
The guards are her only company; she carries cakes out to them herself.
When she falls in the long hall and nobody comes, she counts herself up.
Hester teaches her to punch, and she hits the sandbag every dawn before lessons.
At board meetings she counts the people inside the numbers: a ward is streets, and streets are families.
Her father names her heir to his seat on the board.
She thinks nothing in the board's room is hers.
Seeing the first suits fly, she decides money cannot buy those wings, so if she wins them they are hers.
She makes a bargain in her head: if she comes first with none of his money, her father will have to see.
She wants to hear him say "Well done, Guinevere."
She tells Hester to wait at the car and touches her two red bows.
She walks into the Academy with her chin up and cold hands, and does not look back.
She has pink hair with two red bows in it and touches them both when she climbs out of the car at the Academy.
She walked in at the Academy gate with her chin up, as if the place were already hers.
At the entrance assessment she gives her name as "Guinevere of House Baroque," and the queue murmurs at the name.
She tells Lesley she has come "To become the top Aspirant," the top of all of it.
Her needle passes the line, and she is proud of it because nobody can buy a needle.
She learns from the patrons' plaque that her father's money helped pay for the Academy, and that he never told her.
At dawn she runs the grounds and hits the heavy bag bare-fisted, the way Hester taught her, before calling up her drones.
Holding up two drones at once on her aspirant power is the hardest thing she has ever learned.
She carries band-aids in every pocket, for herself and for anyone else.
Every week she mails home the sums her House tutors set, with a letter to her father, and he never answers.
At night she trains alone in the training hall under the one lamp over the heavy bag.
She wins the top score in the final combat trial of the preparatory course.
She had practiced hearing her father say "Well done, Guinevere," a sentence she had never heard from him.
She will not knock on her father's office door, because knocking would be asking.
Before speaking to her father she steadies herself with "A lady's refinement. Three seconds."
After her father's cold answer she puts the top score paper back in her jacket instead of leaving it on his desk.
That night she hits the heavy bag with bare, untaped hands until there is blood on the canvas.
She vows to train even harder until she cannot stand, so that everyone, even her father, has to see.
On Team-Up Day nobody asks her to be a partner, and she thinks everyone is scared of her family's name.
She is moved that Vexana says her name, since everyone else says Baroque and her father never says it at all.
Vexana turns her down twice, and she is glad, because the no is to her and not to her name.
With no partner, she signs the reserve sheet at the top in large letters.
In the raid at the dome's foot she disobeys the instructor and runs up a side street alone to prove herself.
An Ender claw from a doorway rakes her right arm from shoulder to elbow, and her right hand will not close.
She works out that the roll of tape left on her jacket came from Vexana, who had watched her from the gallery.
On the night after the raid she asks Vexana a third time to be her partner, and Vexana says yes.
She writes their training plans in three colors and writes extra so she will at least do half.
She promises Vexana she will never ask about her family, and keeps the promise.
In the team test she holds the front alone against all six rails while Vexana mends her staff.
She thinks her father answers everything with money: he lost her mother and bought walls, and never came out of his office.
Hurt that Vexana saw only money, she decides to make her something herself, since money cannot solder.
She had never soldered before, and burned her fingers making the Emblems of Hope all night.
She made the Emblems of Hope and named them.
She tells Vexana "Rules are for keeping safe what matters. Not for locking you up."
At the House the guards always found her; at the Academy nobody is paid to look for her.
Her two red bows were her mother's; Hester tied them first, and for years nobody touched them but Guinevere.
At the ceremony she shouts "We're the best partners in The Aspirants!"
She tells how as a child she pointed at people flying on wings of light and wanted some, and says that now she has some.
She vows she will definitely find a way to destroy the Enders' Control Core.
She names Plan A, smashing the Core and winning, and Plan B, coming home.
She likes the front, and in every raid she and Vexana stand there.
She fights the way she does because she never looks back.
She finds Vexana's hidden wound by catching her wrist in sparring, and is hurt that Vexana again carried something alone, after the library.
She challenges Vexana: "Let's settle this with a match, Vexana."
She fights the night match with her left hand tucked into her belt, one arm each, and never goes for Vexana's hurt left arm.
The match ends in a draw, so they both make the rule: partners tell each other first.
She keeps one thing to herself: the bench outside her father's office and the paper she held up to the gap in his door.
She slips a month's plan under Vexana's door, in three colors of ink as always.
Her left bow always slips by evening.
She plans to watch the fireworks with Vexana at the same place next year.
When Vexana phones to send her to bed, she answers "I'm asleep," which she had not said since the first night.
She decides to name every dead Ender in the Investigation Room.
On the morning run she salutes the courtyard billboard of herself and Vexana: "Morning, legends."
Vexana's push throws her clear of the claw; she hits the floor and rolls over broken glass.
She throws herself at the closing door and misses Vexana's hand by a hand.
For the first time she looks back over her shoulder; she had never needed to before.
Seeing her star still lit, she decides Vexana is still there, just not here.
She punches the white wall until her glove splits and the paint is smeared red.
In her written account she blames herself: she left her back open and Vexana stepped into it.
She goes into Vexana's room for the first time and finds the felt dolls, the card and the white box.
She cries over the white box of things Vexana kept.
She does not take the card, because it is Vexana's to give her next year.
She sleeps with her door open a hand's width, as always.
Her red bows were her mother's; for years no hands but hers had touched them, and then Vexana's.
She trains until her legs give out, counts three herself, and nobody says "Four."
She clips the black-haired keychain to her arm guard so it goes in front of her fist.
She draws a red grid over Terrinia and flies every sector she is cleared for, waiting for her star to beep.
She asks Ruby to make her star into a tracker.
For nights she searches the sky with the observation lab telescope for a door, and writes "Nothing" in the night log.
She soldered every seam of the star herself.
When students mock her, she answers "The great lady Guinevere, if you please."
She asks Lesley for a squad to lead and is refused until she has a lead.
She tries to climb the outer ward's fence at night and is pulled down by a Shield sergeant.
At the counseling section she says only "She's alive" and leaves.
She has written to her father every week since she came to the Academy; his seat stayed empty at the trial and the ceremony.
She refuses her father's order to come home, though it costs her place in the House.
She leaves her lamp burning in her window all night, so that Vexana might see it.
In Vexana's memory she gives Vexana the star on the rooftop, her fingertips wrapped in band-aids where the solder burned her.
When Vexana phoned her late in the hall, she complained that normal people say goodnight.
On Team-Up Day she crossed the courtyard in six strides to ask Vexana to be her partner, and kept asking after Vexana said no.
Vexana remembers the body's light streak rising through a blue sky over Guinevere's head.
Her star has stayed lit under the dome all these weeks. It tells her Vexana is alive, while the rest of the Academy believes otherwise.
She once lay with her head in Vexana's lap by a shady tree under the human sky.
At the Northeastern breach she fought below Vexana, fists up, her drones circling.
Her name and Vexana's are on the courtyard billboard in big letters.
Vexana told her under the shady tree that nobody can get near the void.
At the breach she punched Enders out of the air.
On the stairs she laughs loudest at Selena, her head thrown back, with Vexana a few steps behind.
She stands before the VEXANA: MISSING board with two fingers at her collar.
In Chang'e's lab she stands over Ruby and Angela with her arms folded. Her bow is crooked, after a whole year straight.
She stands below the billboard looking up at the black-haired girl, her hand at her collar, and does not look round.
Selena has not heard her laugh since the corridor.
In Vexana's memories, which the Will went through, she is a girl with pink hair, laughing.
The lamp beside the lab's telescope has been lit most nights since she first climbed up there.
She wears the Emblem of Hope, a small gold star, at her collar.
Seeing the far light flash, she asks, "Could it be Vexana?"
Every morning she touches the star at her collar under the courtyard billboard of her and Vexana.
Each morning she straightens Vexana's empty chair herself, before anyone can knock it crooked.
She reads "Absent" on the attendance wall as "Not here yet."
She says aloud, "The emblem... it's flashing. It's Vexana... she must be at the Singularity. I have to go find her."
She thinks: you always came to me, every time; this time I'm coming to you.
She has a long pink ponytail and two cat-eared drones at her shoulders.
When the Emblem beeps, she cries and smiles at the same time.
Her wings of light open and she flies after the figure on the roof.
She says over the channel, "Ruby said it's a lure. If it is, it's mine."
She leaves her post without an order.
On the big display she says, "I'm prepared to enter the Singularity."
She fights fists first, elbow in, hip first, the way Hester drilled her in the House's yard at dawn.
For a whole year Vexana's violet arrow came over her shoulder in every fight, and she never once had to turn and check.
She cries "Light of the stars, tear through the darkness," and gold and white light sweeps every Ender off the platform.
At the end of the first week Vexana was gone, she clipped a black-haired keychain of Vexana to her arm guard, where her fist would swing.
She shouts, "Have you really forgotten everything, Vexana!"
She made the two gold stars herself, with band-aids on her fingertips.
Once a claw raked her right arm on a street at the dome's foot that she had taken alone, and Vexana stood over her and held out a hand.
She heard of the Mother Matrix once, in Teacher Chang'e's class.
She shouts "You... give her back to me!" and flies straight at the Mother Matrix.
When Vexana tells her to give up, she says "I refuse."
With her power running low she thinks, "A great lady does not land early."
When she was small she lay in her room at night hearing Hester's footsteps go away down the corridor, and waited for them to come back.
Falling into the gap, she reaches toward Vexana and says, "Don't let me be alone in this world."
When Layla calls Vexana the traitor, she lifts her chin and says, "Her name is Vexana."
She drops between Vexana and the Matrix's beam, crosses her arms, and holds it with her drones in front of her.
She tells Vexana through her teeth, "There you go again, taking on everything by yourself."
She says, "Rather than being protected, I choose to fight alongside you."
She says, "Vexana, if you think I'm going to let you sacrifice yourself for some greater good, think again!"
She says, "This destiny is something the two of us should bear together."
She holds out her hand and says, "Stay with me, Vexana," Vexana's own words from the street at the dome's foot.
She tells the others she went alone that morning so none of them would walk into a trap meant for her, and asks, "I can't do this alone. Cover us."
She cries, "Aspirants! Today, our light shall pierce the Singularity!"
Climbing toward the Matrix, she realizes Vexana missed her on purpose at the end of their fight.
She cries "This strike is for Vexana" as they strike the open chest together.
Pulled toward the black hole, her light thins to a faint gold outline, and she grins at Vexana with wet eyes.
Inside the black hole her feet had gone to light and her knees were going, and she had been crying.
She had promised never to ask about Vexana's past, but Vexana told her anyway.
She thinks that 'Stay back' were Vexana's father's words, and that Vexana took the claw for her in the corridor.
She shouts into the dark that she heard everything.
She says her will to protect Vexana burns as bright as her will to protect the world.
The night no call came, she called Vexana's number out of habit, followed the ringing into Vexana's room and found the box.
She says she came to the Academy to prove she did not need her father's empire, and that even her top marks drew only a cold rebuke from him.
She says she once waited all day outside her father's office, her heart full of hope.
She says people called her a spoiled little princess whose achievements were her father's, and that she swore to train even harder.
That night a roll of Vexana's tape turned up on her jacket.
She says the first thing Vexana ever said to her was 'You are strong, Guinevere,' and that it felt like the first time someone saw her for herself.
She says that when they first met she was sure of teaming up with Vexana, but Vexana was cold and turned her down.
She says that before Vexana her only company was her security detail.
She says she made the Emblem of Hope she gave Vexana with her own hands.
She says Vexana taught her she has more than money to rely on.
Her father sent word through Hester at the gate: come home, or lose her place in the House. She did not go.
She says she will give up being a lady of status and start over if she must.
Fading, she remembers that even Fanny said the Aspirants always stand united, and her star lights.
She takes Vexana's hand and tells her this is the miracle they created.
She lands on the platform laughing, her pink hair wild, both drones burning at her shoulders.
She tells Fanny she held on to Fanny's words inside the black hole.
At the seawall she had told Layla, chin up, 'Her name is Vexana.'
She wears a little black-haired doll on her cracked arm guard.
She takes Vexana's healed left arm in both hands and turns it over, as if counting the fingers.
She flies on wings of gold light with two drones circling her.
She fights with her fists and punches straight into an Ender's core.
She raises her fists and says, 'We have only one Aspirant spirit.'
Far out over the water when Fanny calls to land, she flies back high and fast toward Vexana instead of down.
The field takes her last: her drones die, her gold wings break into sparks and she falls.
She falls through a shop's awning onto the stones at the mouth of the cut and does not get up.
After the fall something in her side stabs every time she breathes.
She reaches for her power the way she always does, and nothing comes.
For weeks her lit star was her only proof that Vexana was alive somewhere.
She has always liked Selena a little, as she likes anyone who does not care what a room thinks of them.
She looks at Selena past the plate and claws, for the girl inside, the way she looked at Vexana on the platform.
With no drones and no wings she fights with her hands, which she had before any of it.
She hears Hester's old lesson, 'Hands home,' from a dawn beside a sandbag.
She steps in under an Ender's arm and cracks its core with her bare fist.
Every night in the training hall she trained fists first, then drones.
She tells Vexana, 'Same place. Next year.'

weapons.name: Fists
weapons.note: Her own weapon. She fights up close, bare-knuckled, and her guard comes back to her chin after every punch. Somebody taught her that long before she had drones.

weapons.name: Guinevere's drones
weapons.note: Two round gray drones with cat ears and yellow ring eyes. They run on her aspirant power, circle her as she fights and take whatever her hands leave. Their rings dim when her power runs low.

weapons.name: Wings of light
weapons.note: Wings that run on her aspirant power and hold her in the air. When she tires too far, they go out like a switch.

weapons.name: Light of the stars
weapons.note: Her great strike. She cries "Light of the stars, tear through the darkness," and gold and white light sweeps the Enders away.

weapons.name: The two red bows
weapons.note: Two red bows in her pink hair that were her mother's. Hester tied them first. After that Guinevere tied them herself and let nobody else touch them.

weapons.name: Band-aids
weapons.note: She carries them in every pocket, for herself and for anyone else.

weapons.name: The top score paper
weapons.note: Her sheet from the final combat trial of the preparatory course, marked Top score. She keeps it inside her jacket.

weapons.name: Emblems of Hope
weapons.note: A small gold star at her collar. She cut it and its twin for Vexana from thin gold plate and soldered them, burning her fingers. They glow when the two are in sync and beep when they meet again.

weapons.name: The black card
weapons.note: A black card with the small gold crest of House Baroque. She pays with it.

weapons.name: Chibi keychain
weapons.note: A little doll keychain of black-haired Vexana. Vexana wears its twin, a pink-haired Guinevere.

weapons.name: The blue badges
weapons.note: Her Best Aspirant Duo badge, from the ceremony that named her and Vexana the best partners of the year.

weapons.name: Black gloves
weapons.note: Her fighting gloves. In them she still punches the way she was drilled: elbow in, hip first, hands home.

weapons.name: Guinevere's arm guards
weapons.note: Guards she buckles on her forearms to train and fight. She clipped the black-haired keychain of Vexana to one, so it goes in front of her fist.

weapons.name: Guinevere's map
weapons.note: A map of Terrinia under a red grid. She flies every sector she is cleared for, waiting for her star to beep.

entries.line: A pink-haired Aspirant with a red bow, half of a legendary undefeated pair.
entries.short: A pink-haired girl from Joe's class who fights up close with her fists, two cat-eared drones circling her. With Vexana, she has never lost.
entries.summary: The heiress of House Baroque, a pink-haired Aspirant who fights with her fists, two cat-eared drones and wings of light. She came to Selrick Academy to win what her father's money could not buy, and with Vexana she never lost a fight. When Vexana pushed her clear of a claw and was dragged into the dark in her place, Guinevere refused her father's order to come home, kept searching, and at the Singularity would not give her up. Together they struck the Mother Matrix's open chest and came back out of the black hole; when the field killed her drones and wings, she fought on with her bare fists.

entries.name: Guinevere's father

facts.t: At dawn after the storm night he stood in his office door a long time, then shut it.
He holds the head seat on the board that runs House Baroque.
He puts a detail of guards around his daughter, led by Hester.
He lost his wife to the Enders; Guinevere later works out that to him money buys walls, so money is safety, though he never says so.
His chair at the far end of the long table stands empty most nights, and he speaks to Guinevere through his office door.
He marks a mistake on her first page of sums and says "Again."
He keeps her second page.
He returns her birthday cake plate washed, with no word.
The long hall is the master's; the guards never enter it.
When Guinevere falls in the long hall, his pen keeps scratching behind his door.
At board meetings he sits at the head, a fur collar over his chair.
He tells the board his daughter will take a junior seat when she comes of age, and his seat after him.
When she says she will sit the Academy's assessment, he says only that she will be home within the year, and does not forbid it.
His House's money helped pay for Selrick Academy, and he never told Guinevere.
He never answers Guinevere's weekly letters.
He misses her final trial for a board meeting, and his seat stays empty.
Through his office door he only ever says sit up, again, tomorrow and accounts.
Through the gap of his office door Guinevere sees only a dark sleeve with a fur cuff.
The Academy sent him Guinevere's top score report, and he had it before she came home.
He takes his lunch at his desk.
When Guinevere holds up her top score, he says only "Stop being so stubborn and focus more on the family business!"
Then he leaves by a door behind his desk and the lamp goes off.
He never says Guinevere's name at all.
When Guinevere left a cake outside his office on his birthday, the plate came back washed.
Guinevere thinks he answers everything with money: he lost her mother and bought walls.
He does not answer her letter about the Best Aspirant Duo ceremony, and his chair stays empty.
Guinevere once sat on a bench outside his office and held a paper up to the gap in his door.
He sends word to Guinevere through Hester.
Guinevere wrote to him every week; his only answer came through Hester: a board meeting.
His seat for the House stayed empty at the trial and at the ceremony.
After a Shield sergeant reports Guinevere at a closed fence, he orders her home; if she does not come, her place in the House is gone.
His message holds no word about Guinevere herself.
Hester says he reads the Academy's lists every morning.
Guinevere says he has an empire and a family business, and that he answered her top marks with 'Stop being so stubborn and focus more on the family business!'
Guinevere says she once waited outside his office all day, full of hope.
Through the gap in his door his dark sleeve with a fur cuff turned pages until dusk and never reached for her paper.
He sent word through Hester at the gate: come home, or lose her place in the House.

He lost his wife to the Enders, and Guinevere thinks he answers everything with money: he lost her mother and bought walls. He speaks to her only through his office door, never answers her weekly letters, leaves his seat empty at her trial and meets her top score with "Stop being so stubborn and focus more on the family business!"
