On the storm night she was working late at the House's bank by the harbor, and she did not come home.
The two red bows came from her dressing table.
Guinevere's father lost her to the Enders.
Her portrait hangs at the far end of the long hall in the House.
A lamp burns under her portrait.

entries.summary: Guinevere's mother, whose portrait hangs at the far end of the long hall in the House, with a lamp burning under it. On the storm night she was working late at the House's bank by the harbor, and she did not come home: her husband lost her to the Enders. When the House cleared her rooms, Hester kept back the two red bows from her dressing table, and Guinevere wears them in her hair.

entries.name: Hester
aka: the woman in the gray coat

facts.t: Someone used to count for Guinevere whenever she fell.
She is the first person who ever counted for Guinevere.
She wears a gray coat, belongs to the House's guard and never laughs.
When small Guinevere falls on the garden stair, she says "Up, miss. One. Two. Three."
After that she counts three at every fall.
She tells the story of Guinevere's mother the way she gives a report.
As the newest guard in the House, she carried baby Guinevere down to the cellar with one candle on the storm night, counting the steps aloud so she would not cry.
After telling the story, she leaves the door open; her footsteps go, stop and come back.
She never tells that story again.
She kept back Guinevere's mother's two red bows when the House cleared her rooms, and ties them in Guinevere's hair.
Guinevere's father puts her at the head of his daughter's guard detail.
She eats her cake standing up.
She learned to fight from an old Shield sergeant before the House hired her, and finally agrees to teach Guinevere.
She teaches: elbow in, hip first, hands home after every punch.
She drives Guinevere across the city to the Academy's entrance assessment.
She waits beside the car in her gray coat, where Guinevere told her to wait.
She is a woman in a gray coat who drives Guinevere to the Academy gate in a long car.
She answers Guinevere with "Yes, miss."
She taught Guinevere to hit the heavy bag bare-fisted.
Four days before the final trial she came to the gate to say Guinevere's father had a board meeting.
She came to the trial on the House's pass and sat two rows behind the empty Baroque seat.
She did not clap with the stand at first, then clapped alone in her row when Guinevere got the top score.
When Guinevere rehearses her line in the car, Hester tells her honestly it sounded the same.
At the House she stops at the chair where the long hall begins.
At noon she tells Guinevere she should eat.
After the father's cold answer she comes past the chair and stops one step from Guinevere, without touching her.
Guinevere introduces her to Vexana with "That's Hester. Ignore her."
On the teacup ride she spins in the next cup with the cake box on her knees and no expression at all.
She never waves back when Guinevere waves at her.
She hands back the cake box one cake lighter.
She tied the red bows in Guinevere's hair the first morning it was long enough.
She knew exactly what little Guinevere meant when she pointed at the flying Aspirants and said "That."
At the House she counted three at every fall of Guinevere's, however long it took her to get up.
She waits outside the bars of the Academy gate in her gray coat, the long car behind her with its back door open.
She calls Guinevere "Miss Guinevere" and brings word from her father.
At the trial and the ceremony she sat two rows behind the House's empty seat.
She gives the father's order without softening it: come home, or lose her place in the House.
She inclines her head a single degree, then tells Guinevere low that her father reads the Academy's lists every morning.
She tied Guinevere's bows the first time, the morning Guinevere's hair was long enough.
Seeing Guinevere's healing knuckles, she tells her "Hands home after every punch, miss."
She once counted the cellar stairs aloud so a child in the dark would not cry.
When Guinevere walks away, Hester stays where she is; no car door shuts and no engine starts.
She drilled Guinevere in fighting, elbow in and hip first, in the House's yard at dawn.
When Guinevere was small, Hester's footsteps went away down the corridor at night, stopped, and came back after a long, still wait.
Guinevere's father sent word through her at the gate: come home or lose her place in the House.
At dawn years ago, beside a sandbag that hardly swung, she taught Guinevere 'Hands home.'

entries.line: The woman in the gray coat who counts for Guinevere when she falls.
entries.short: The gray-coated head of Guinevere's guard, who never laughs. Whenever Guinevere falls, she counts: "Up, miss. One. Two. Three."
entries.summary: Hester is the gray-coated head of the House guard detail around Guinevere, and the first person who ever counted for her. As the newest guard she carried baby Guinevere down to the cellar on the storm night, counting the steps so she would not cry, and later tied her mother's red bows in her hair. She learned to fight from an old Shield sergeant and taught Guinevere elbow in, hip first, hands home. She carries the father's orders without softening them, yet she clapped alone in her row when Guinevere took the top score.

entries.name: Karina

facts.t: A soaked woman carries a lamp with a flame behind glass down the ruined street, calling into every doorway.
Her flame keeps burning because Obsidia's storm cannot kill a flame.
Her lamp finds the child. She kneels and gathers it up.
The child's arms go around her neck and hold on.
Later she lays the living under a tarp between two broken walls, with the child at the end of the row.
Then she takes her lamp back out to look for more.
Selena says her guardian already called in her late arrival, and the note is there.
Soaked to the skin, she carries a lamp down the dark street on the storm night of 983, stopping at every doorway and calling for survivors.
She finds the child in the mud, kneels and gathers her up.
Her coat is wet through, she is warm under it, and she smells of smoke.
She sets the child under the tarp and goes back out with her lamp for more.
She is on the rescue team, the people who go into the ruins after a strike and carry out whoever is still alive.
She always keeps sweets in her coat pocket for the children she carries out.
When nobody comes for the child, she signs the team's log to keep her for one night, then another.
She tells the clerk: "You don't put down someone you carried out." She calls it her rule, and duty.
In all the years after, she never calls it anything but duty.
She tries the names Mara and Tess on the child.
When the child names herself, she says "Selena it is," and smiles.
Her flat is two rooms at the top of a narrow stair, her work boots by the door and the team radio on the shelf, never off.
When the sirens go she pulls on her boots and tells Selena to lock the door. She is gone all night after every strike.
On wet mornings she holds out a coat at the door: "Coat anyway."
After a raid she looks Selena over for cuts as she looks over everyone she carries out, then presses her forehead to her hair in relief.
When Selena comes in soaked from the roof, she says only: "Not in the lightning."
Her fingers stay on Selena's warm hands a breath longer than usual.
On the night the research base fell she went toward the burning far half of the city.
She came back the next afternoon and fell asleep at the table with her helmet on.
When Selena gets into the Science Division she says: "I want to see you graduate."
At dawn she stands in Selena's door with her rescue helmet under her arm: "Up. You'll be late."
One dawn she finds Selena's bed unslept, looks at her, and drinks her tea.
She phones the school with a fever for Selena, who never had one.
She never says the word fever afterward.
On the day before, she listens to the radio put all teams on standby.
That morning she does not say "The bell." She waits in the doorway while Selena laces her boots.
She takes a fruit drop from the pocket she mended years ago and presses it into Selena's palm.
She tells Selena: "I've noticed things. I never asked. I'm not asking now."
She says "Come home after," and again that she still wants to see Selena graduate.
She does not close the door as Selena goes down the stair.
She is out with the rescue teams; one of the lamps in the flooded wards would be hers.
She told Selena 'Come home after', without saying after what.
She still wants to see Selena's graduation.
Selena's first memory is of a woman with a lamp who knelt in the mud and gathered her up.
When Selena gave herself a name at a rainy window, Karina said 'Selena it is.'
During the battle she carries a lamp from door to door in the flooded wards.

entries.short: A rescue worker who carries survivors out of the ruins. On the storm night of 983 she found young Selena in the mud and kept her.
entries.summary: Karina is on the rescue team, the people who go into the ruins after a strike and carry out whoever is still alive. On the storm night of 983 her lamp found a small child in the mud, and when nobody came for her she kept her: "You don't put down someone you carried out." She raises Selena in a two-room flat with the team radio always on, calls it nothing but duty, and on the morning of the attack tells her, "Come home after," because she still wants to see her graduate. During the battle she carries a lamp from door to door in the flooded wards.

entries.name: Layla
aka: the girl with the pink-red twin-tails

facts.t: She has long pink-red twin-tails. She swings a long cannon up to her shoulder and charges it until the muzzle burns blue.
Before Fanny's run, she tops the VR rankings board with a time of 3:41.
She wears a frilled black uniform nobody issued her.
She has never been second, not once, since her first year.
When Fanny's time beats hers, she says "Humph!" and walks out.
At gear check she opens her cannon, works a hot pen at its cells and shuts it again before Fanny has oiled her second blade.
In the evenings she sits alone on the lounge sofa, one finger holding down a slat of the blinds, watching the sun go down over the city.
Every race that first week, on the spiral stair, with the mops and at gear check, was her idea.
She heard every word Fanny shouted after her through the closing doors and did not turn around.
Her family have been scientists for generations. A message from home calls her the hope of the family, and she leaves it unanswered.
She turns her gold FIRST PLACE trophy to face the wall.
She built her cannon herself and has rebuilt its barrel and sight twice, chasing a fault.
The seedling under its glass dome is the only thing in her lab she did not build.
At home talent had been enough. At the Academy the courses got hard, so she trains in secret and tells everyone the exams are easy.
She reruns Fanny's assessment five times, leaving the civilian under his sign. Her best is 3:40.
For three mornings she lies on the dark gallery above the drill hall while her drone films Fanny drilling.
She gives Fanny the smile she keeps for teachers and puts off training together for another time.
When she cannot win the drone count, she decides to win the look.
After losing the test match she waits in an empty corridor until her hands stop shaking, then vows to take back first place.
In the drill she shoots the Ender held on Fanny's cable and says Fanny should have led them over earlier.
She calls the Enders pushovers.
She wins the drill count, 16 kills to Fanny's 15. The sixteenth had been held on Fanny's cable.
At the real breach her heart pounds, but her hands do not shake.
She knows Fanny is right about the Ender's neck and does not intend to say so.
On the tower roof she does not trust her cannon's numbers and turns the dial down two notches.
She kills the Ender at the breach with a thin white bolt through the billboard and two walls of glass, into its core.
She watched Roger drag Joe out of the street and kept walking. Afterward her hands shake.
She plans the shot at the gold giant: its glow doubles every four seconds, she needs three seconds of full charge, and Fanny must stay right of the center line.
She shoves Fanny out of the giant's beam on her suit's thrusters and fires the full charge into it.
After the blast she looks at her cannon's cells instead of the wreck, then turns the dial all the way down.
A medic tapes her cheek and wraps her left forearm. She remembers only shoving Fanny clear of the beam.
Her grudge against Fanny kept her in the VR Battlefield until two and got her up before five.
She asks Fanny "All rested up?" and declares that they are training together from now on.
She admits that before the breach she felt Enders were nothing more than target practice.
She explains her cannon's drift and her fix: she made the faster half of the charge wait nine thousandths of a second.
She sets their dawn training for a quarter to five, earlier than the five Fanny suggests.
She has refused eleven partnership offers in two years.
After downing a single drone she complains that she is always the one getting hurt, though nobody touched her.
On raids she takes charge and goes first, so that Fanny will be covered.
She watches the stars past the dome longer than she meant to.
During the landing she and Fanny held a ward on the far side of the city against a giant.
She comes to the monitor room still in her suit, smelling of smoke.
She folds her arms and shares a small smile with Fanny, then catches herself.
She points out that the newcomers are being arrested.
She takes Fanny's flight rig apart without being asked and glares at a bent coupling.
She asks whether the two newcomers are 'funny in the head'.
She is excited at the thought of more battles on other planets.
She calls the newcomers 'armed newcomers'.
She adds her own word to Fanny's to vouch for them, insisting she only said they were funny in the head.
She asks 'Beside us?' when Chang'e seats the newcomers next to her and Fanny.
She stares at Fanny when Fanny calls that fair.
At the first intake a girl with pink-red twin-tails, whose sheet lists a long line of scientists, puts her hand in the glove, and the needle hits the stop with a click.
She answers Lesley without slowing, walks on to the far door and never looks back to see who is behind her.
Chang'e calls hers the best reading of the day.
Lesley notes that she does not look back, which is bad in a pair.
Her name heads the Combat Division's first intake list.
Late for class, she gallops along the school roof, thinking nobody checks it.
She scolds Fanny that flying is banned.
She complains that this time they will have the book thrown at them.
She hears herself say that at least they will be in detention together, and studies the ceiling.
In the mop race she slides the last meters on her back on the wet floor; Ruby wins.
She has messages from home that she has not answered.
She eyes the new coil on Lesley's rifle and wants it in pieces on her desk.
She decides the movement at the corner of Lesley's mouth was a smile.
She notes that nobody tows Lesley.
She lies down in the grass an arm's length from Fanny, telling herself it is only because the grass is warm.
She says, too fast, that she is not interested in the outside world and has not been sneaking a peek.
She does not let herself think about three small leaves under a glass dome.
She watches Fanny's raised hand from the corner of her eye.
At the ceremony she stands shoulder to shoulder with Fanny in combat suits, not arguing.
Guinevere has spoken to her exactly once, at the fish market.
She knows Guinevere from a billboard.
She and Vexana have shared classes for two years, and neither ever spoke first.
She keeps score: Vexana spoke first, so one to her.
At the fish market she tells Fanny "Behind me" and goes first.
At the entrance assessment she is the girl with pink-red twin-tails whose needle hits the stop.
She walks on to the far door and never once looks back to see who is behind her.
On Team-Up Day she stands alone on the upper walk with her arms on the rail.
She turns a boy away, saying "I'd only have to wait for you."
On the field nobody keeps up with her, and she never slows down for anyone.
Her eyes meet Guinevere's, but neither will walk over, and she turns back to the rail.
She does not sign the reserve sheet; Guinevere thinks she will not stand behind anybody and would rather stay in the VR.
In Chang'e's classroom she sits at the front, alone.
When Chang'e asks who sends the Enders, she answers "Nobody knows."
She asks Chang'e whom the strong people are supposed to endanger.
She always asks the first question, before Guinevere can.
When Guinevere waves at her in the hall, she looks, then lifts two fingers once.
When a paper plane hits Selena, every face turns to Layla, who is carefully copying a board with nothing written on it.
At lunch she sets her tray down across the table from Guinevere.
She tells Guinevere that portals don't give people back.
She tells Guinevere, not unkindly, that the star is a circuit and circuits glitch.
On the day the transfer came, her VR Battlefield record of 3:41 was knocked to second by FANNY, 3:39.
She walks out with her chin up and her mouth shut.
At the breach her cannon flashed white.
Her paper plane hits Selena's head in class and wakes her.
She stands at Fanny's left in the courtyard with the cannon on her shoulder.
She grabs Fanny's sleeve because the big display in the hall is tracking Guinevere.
She has marked weak points in the Enders' defenses in green on her tablet map: "This rescue operation is ready to go!"
She built the map in the time it took Fanny to give one order.
She flicks her map to the command deck.
She has gone first on every raid since the Enders came only in handfuls, so that Fanny would be covered.
She sees Fanny's frown and is ready to let her have it, as always.
She answers Lesley with "Copy" over the roar of her cannon.
She calls over the channel, "Guinevere! Report!"
She cries "I've locked on to the enemies!" and sends Ruby left and Fanny high.
She mutters that Ruby and Angela are funny in the head, because the pane is open before she asks.
When Angela thanks her, she fires instead of answering.
She calls Vexana "The traitor?"
She tells Guinevere the commander said to get to her, and they could not.
Seeing Vexana's burned arm, she lowers her cannon: "It's not a trap. Nobody burns their own arm for a trap."
She still could not tell Professor Joe why Guinevere and Vexana are undefeated.
Hearing Vexana say "This is the final farewell," she mutters, "Not on my count."
In Joe's class she had said "Weak spot. When it attacks. Obviously," as if it were easy.
Once she counted sixteen kills in one fight and was proud of it. Now she is counting angles for a girl she called a traitor.
Her plan is to make the Matrix look at the platform and fire at the shield, so its chest opens away from Guinevere and Vexana.
She gives the angles: Fanny thirty degrees up, left of the crown; Ruby on the rail; Angela keeping the shield high and opening a lane.
She tells Guinevere, "When it looks at us, it's yours."
She gives the order, "Fire!"
Her shot goes up first through Angela's pane, a thin cyan line.
When the chest opens, she says "Now," to nobody.
She counts under her breath while the pair are inside the black hole.
Fanny thinks Layla counts everything.
She tells the returning pair they took twelve seconds.
She answers 'Obviously' when Fanny says her plan worked, though her hand on the stock is not quite still.
She kneels on a roof with her cannon on her shoulder; her lips move as its cells fill.
She grins on her roof during the fight.
She calls 'And now, it's our time to shine!', which Fanny says is her line.
She asks Fanny what the spreading field is.
When her cannon dies she says, 'Huh...? No way... What...'
She climbs down a drainpipe with the dead cannon on her back and stands at Fanny's left.
Seeing Selena's true shape she says 'Why...' with all the edge gone from her voice.
She stands at the wall with her dead cannon on her back, counting.
She timed the Enders: from the lift of the arm to the split of the chest is always a count of three.
She thinks of the wall as the alley thing, which she once spied on from a dark gallery and then pretended never to have heard of.
Vexana knows which Ender will swing; Layla knows when.
The soldiers and Fanny strike on her count.
She throws her shoulder against the sliding shop sign to hold the wall.
She protests that she was only holding up a sign.
She thinks Fanny stole the idea of covering from the breach.
She tells the crying boy, 'If you're scared, you can hide behind me.'
She once said it to Roger as a joke; now she means it.
On the day of the breach she heard Joe's soft voice over the girl with the pink rabbit, then walked away to argue over who covered whom.
On her lab's top shelf a pink box with a teal ribbon stands beside her trophy.
She tells the boy Fanny is her teammate.
She notices Fanny is no longer looking past her.
She wonders whether Selena sent the Enders or just left.
She had called Vexana a traitor at the seawall, to Guinevere's face.
Since the sand outside the dome she has gone first on every raid.
She counts silently and drops so that Fanny's blade can pass over her into an Ender.
Her cannon wakes on her back, its cells lighting cyan from the bottom up.
She answers Fanny's joke with 'Since when were we resting?'
Her cannon fires on her own count in the last fight.

weapons.name: Layla's cannon
weapons.note: A long cannon she built herself, as tall as she is, white with a teal strip. She rebuilt its barrel and sight twice. Cyan cells on its stock fill as it charges, and a dial sets the power.

weapons.name: Full charge
weapons.note: Her strongest shot, a blue-white line after three seconds of charge. It split a giant's beam. It drifted left until she made the faster half of the charge wait nine thousandths of a second.

weapons.name: Low-charge shot
weapons.note: Turned down two notches, it fired a thin white bolt through a billboard and two walls of glass into an Ender's core.

weapons.name: Combat suit
weapons.note: Her Aspirant suit. Its thrusters let her fly, and on them she shoved Fanny out of a giant's beam. It was drained after that battle.

weapons.name: Three black drones
weapons.note: Drones in her lab with angry faces she drew on in cyan marker. For three mornings one filmed Fanny drilling while she watched from a dark gallery.

weapons.name: Tablet
weapons.note: She builds battle maps on it. For the rescue she marked the weak points in the Enders' defenses in green and flicked the map to the command deck.

weapons.name: Wristband
weapons.note: It buzzes with messages. On it she read Roger's news of Professor Joe and sent a reply.

weapons.name: Hot pen
weapons.note: A tool she works at her cannon's cells at gear check. She has the cannon open and shut again before Fanny has oiled her second blade.

weapons.name: FIRST PLACE trophy
weapons.note: A gold trophy on her lab's top shelf. The night Fanny took first place, she turned it to face the wall.

weapons.name: Pink box
weapons.note: The chocolate box with a teal ribbon that Fanny gave her as her teammate. It stands on the top shelf beside her trophy.

weapons.name: Seedling
weapons.note: A seedling with three small leaves under a glass dome. It is the only thing in her lab she did not build.

weapons.name: Cannon under the field
weapons.note: Under the Storm Citadel's field its cells went dark one by one and it would not fire. Later it woke on her back, its cells lighting cyan from the bottom up.

rows: Long pink-red twin-tails and a frilled black uniform nobody issued her.
Scientists for generations. A message from home calls her the hope of the family. She leaves their messages unanswered.
Selrick Academy, Combat Division, third year. Her name headed the division's first intake list.
Her needle hit the stop, the best reading of the day. Lesley noted that she never looked back, which is bad in a pair.
Team B3 under Professor Joe, with Roger and later Fanny. Then the Layla-Fanny Team, after she had refused eleven partnership offers in two years.
Professor Joe, Chang'e and Lesley. She sits alone at the front of Chang'e's class and always asks the first question.
Frontline. She takes charge, marks the weak points and goes first on raids so that Fanny is covered.
3:41, top of the board since her first year, until Fanny's 3:39 knocked her to second. Her best rerun of Fanny's run was 3:40.
An abandoned classroom she took against the rules. Her cannon, her drones, her trophy and a seedling live there.
Trains in secret and tells everyone the exams are easy. Counts everything. Watches the sunset and the stars past the dome longer than she means to.
Fanny at first, at everything. She keeps score against Vexana, and neither she nor Guinevere will cross a courtyard to the other.

entries.line: A proud third-year cannon fighter who had topped the VR rankings since her first year.
entries.short: A third-year with pink-red twin-tails and a long cannon. She had topped the VR rankings since her first year and never once been second.
entries.summary: A third-year who built her own cannon, from a long line of scientists, and had never been second until Fanny, a new transfer, beat her time on day one. She raced Fanny at everything until a real breach of the dome showed her the Enders were not target practice, and Professor Joe made them the Layla-Fanny Team. From then on she planned the attacks and went first on raids to cover Fanny, and her plan drew the Mother Matrix's fire so its chest opened for Guinevere. When the Storm Citadel's field killed her cannon, she held the wall in the bay road cut by counting each Ender's strike, told a crying boy Fanny was her teammate, and fought on back to back with her.

entries.name: Lesley

facts.t: She is the Chief Combat Instructor, head of all combat training at Selrick Academy.
She signs Fanny in for the assessment.
She is young and cold, with a dark visor over her left eye.
She reads Fanny's record aloud: transfer, two years with the Shield, asked for the front.
Her one visible eye goes to Fanny's hands.
She says: "One without the Aspirant spirit is like a gun without bullets."
She is the Chief Combat Instructor. She comes in from the giants' front in a white coat scorched at the hem, with a dark visor and a long rifle on her back.
She freezes Selrick's record on the frame of the red-eyed girl holding a scythe over a child.
At the newcomers' arrival she covers the lot from a roof, her rifle on the parapet.
She tells Ruby she has watched the record of the scythe raised over the child.
She lets the newcomers in under watch because she wants the one person who can shut Oro's androids down within reach of her rifle.
She follows Chang'e one full step behind, her eye on the back of the small head; Fanny thinks she walks like a bodyguard.
She never sleeps on her made-up cot. She sleeps sitting up in a hard chair, boots on, her rifle within reach of her right hand.
She is a young woman in a white officer's coat with a gold star, with gold hair streaked with red.
A dark visor covers her left eye. The eye behind it glows teal, and Chang'e built it.
She wakes at once with her hand on the rifle and asks: 'A new product from R&D?'
She keeps her rifle's old hand-worked firing action and wants the new coil fitted on top of it.
She refuses to put Chang'e on the field rotation and gives no reason. She never has.
She is the one who left the caramel pudding at Chang'e's lab door.
She has a familiar dream of screams and the Enders' roar that always ends on a child's voice, and she wakes from it with wet cheeks.
After the dream she always touches her visor and plays the recording of her birthday in her eye.
In 983 she grew up in a ticking house on a street of repair shops, where her father mended clocks.
Her little brother called her Sis and nothing else.
She promised her brother that if an Ender came, she would stand in front.
When the Ender came she stepped in front of her brother and was struck on the left side of her face; that side went dark.
Her whole family died in the attack. She called for each of them and nobody answered.
In the smoke she vowed out loud to kill every last Ender.
She dropped her survivor's tag in the mud and hid on the last truck to the far stations.
The station medic gave her a black patch for the lost eye.
At the station she cleaned rifles, her hands quick with small parts.
She was the only child at the station, and in raids she climbed the wall instead of going to the bunker.
She learned that an Ender's chest opens on its core only when it strikes.
Nobody taught her. She trained by aiming at the grass at dawn and counting: wait, wait, now.
She told the youngest soldier: 'Bullets are the only language the enemy understands.'
She kept from knowing people, so it would not matter when they were gone.
She killed her first Ender with one shot into its core and saved the youngest soldier.
The Shield took her as a soldier while its smallest uniform still covered her hands.
She came back to Terrinia in the upper ranks of the Shield, the youngest anyone there had heard of.
She was sent to keep the research base's two chief scientists and their child alive, and took it like any other mission.
At the base she walked the corridors at midnight and checked every door.
She pulled Chang'e clear of a falling rack in the east corridor.
When Chang'e called her Sis, it was her brother's word.
She told Chang'e she did not have a birthday.
Nobody had seen under her patch since the station medic tied it on, and she feared it would frighten Chang'e.
When the new eye lit, the lab drew itself on her left side in thin teal lines.
She felt warm for the first time in years and stayed bent while Chang'e checked the fit.
She eats supper standing at the door of the family's small dining room, so she can watch the corridor and the table at once.
She notes that there had been four at her own family's house.
She tells Chang'e's father a soldier can carry thirty kilos, or twenty if she has to run far.
Nobody had called her Big Sis in front of people before, and she does not correct it.
On her night round she finds Chang'e asleep at the bench, switches off the soldering iron and carries her to bed.
Her father's bench sounded like a rifle bolt, with clocks on the wall; the night the roof came down every lamp died, but the clocks he wound by hand kept ticking.
She tells Chang'e she always hits her target.
For the first time her hand does not stop halfway, and she rests it on Chang'e's head.
She sights with both eyes open: her real eye and her teal one.
For years she watched Ender cores die from the station wall, and she knows they burn from the middle.
At the rail yard she aims at the edge of an Ender's core instead of its middle, which she had never seen anyone try.
Her shot brings a core piece back whole, which nobody had thought could be done.
An officer tells her the whole core piece makes her the most valuable shot the Shield has, and sends her on a top secret mission.
She has never refused an order in the Shield.
Her brother held her sleeve every night and she promised him every night; he died anyway, and she has promised no one anything since.
She promises Chang'e she will come back.
She will never tell anyone what the mission was.
Back in Terrinia she takes an officer's radio handset and commands the leaderless squads to hold the avenues.
Her rifle barrel grows so hot it burns through her left glove, and she does not let go.
She sees the giant walking toward the base and realizes the fight at the edge is a decoy.
She shoots the Ender that is about to strike Chang'e at the crater.
She holds Chang'e and says she is sorry, and Chang'e pushes her away.
Once she sat in the rain between her own parents, so she knows Chang'e's loss better than anyone.
From a far roof she keeps the lab's lit window in her rifle sights all night, and again the next night.
Months after the fall she is made a commander of the Shield's combat division.
She asks the Shield only for a cold room at the top of an old tower across the water, because its window faces the lab.
She sleeps in a hard chair facing the window, and her dream always ends on Chang'e's voice.
She thinks that ever since that day she vowed to keep Chang'e safe.
She turns her lamp up full and stands in the lit window, so the Ender sees her and turns its open chest toward her.
Her first words to Chang'e since the crater are an order: focus on the fight.
Her round and Chang'e's crescent hit the giant's open chest together.
Later the Academy calls her and Chang'e the First Aspirants.
She tells the Shield's officers that imagination is Chang'e's weapon, and she only aims it.
At the founding she becomes Selrick Academy's Chief Combat Instructor, head of its Combat Division.
For weeks she walks the city's children's homes with stamped sheets and picks children for the Academy.
She never sleeps on her cot; she sleeps upright in the hard chair, boots on, facing the door.
Years later she still cannot tell Chang'e what the mission was.
She keeps Chang'e off the field rotation because in the field she cannot see her, and the last time she was away Chang'e's parents died.
She keeps the old action under the new coil because Chang'e built it.
As Chief Combat Instructor she declares Ruby and Angela Aspirants.
She is a young woman in a white officer's coat with a long rifle on her back and a dark visor over one eye.
She came to the Shield's home with a sheet stamped by the home and read Vexana's record: father, Shield of Dawnbreak, killed in action.
She did not say she was sorry; she told Vexana the Academy tests its first intake this year, and said "Come."
She folded the sheet and walked away without waiting for an answer.
At the entrance assessment she stands at the wall behind the table, watches the queue and leaves the dial to Chang'e.
When a boy runs back toward the gate, she only watches him go.
She asks the questions at the assessment: the child's name and why they are there.
She gives Vexana a long look and sends her to the far door with a tip of her head.
Her face does not change at Guinevere's answer; she only says "Next."
She pins the Academy's first Best Aspirant Duo badges on Guinevere and Vexana, her fingers quick and cool.
Her whole speech at the ceremony is one word: "Undefeated."
At the edge of the stage she smiles, small, and it stays.
Her squads held the giants' front with Guinevere and Vexana on the day the black ships landed.
She gives the speech in the hall in the week the newcomers become Aspirants.
She is first to reach the corridor after the attack, her long rifle on her back and a squad behind her.
She takes Guinevere by the arm and turns her away from the wall.
She tells Guinevere "There's no time to lament."
She hands Guinevere a notebook and pen to write down everything she saw while she still remembers it.
She reads every line of Guinevere's account and folds the pages into her coat.
She pins the VEXANA: MISSING sheet to the board outside the Combat office and walks away without looking at anyone.
She brings Chang'e a cup of water and a pill, and tells her she has slept eleven hours in six days.
She does not argue with Chang'e; she leans on the door frame with folded arms and waits until Chang'e gives in.
She refuses to let a records clerk mark Vexana Killed in action: "No body, no finding. Her file says Missing. It stays Missing."
She tells Guinevere she will give her a squad when she brings a lead.
She tells Guinevere a lit star is a light, not a lead.
She goes into her office and shuts the door.
In Vexana's memory of the ceremony, Lesley smiled at the two partners.
She stands at the command deck's long window with her rifle on her shoulder.
She orders "Sound it," and the alarm goes up through the tower.
Her machine eye lays thin teal lines over the Enders as they land.
She keys the command channel: "All posts. Report."
The last time she saw that violet, she stood on a windowsill while a radio downstairs stopped in the middle of a word. Only the clocks her father wound by hand kept ticking.
She does not know why the channel holds under the storm, but she uses it.
To Chang'e's guess she says, "Logged. Keep reading."
She stands behind Chang'e's chair with one hand on its back, and Chang'e lets it stay.
Years ago she stood on a roof over a burning city while one giant walked through the middle where nobody stood. The blow fell on the base by the water, and she came too late.
She reads the attack as a lure to draw defenders into the streets so the real blow lands at the Academy.
She wants a roof and a line of sight, but stays at the console.
She orders the Shield reserves to hold their wards: "Nobody moves without my word."
When mobile support does not answer, she says "Log it."
She tells Guinevere over the channel, "Knowing when to retreat is an important skill, too."
She sends the frontline on Layla's plan and keeps the deck, in case a second front comes there.
Her rifle has been on Ruby since the day Ruby landed.
In Guinevere's memory, she gave a speech about trust to Layla, Fanny, Ruby and Angela in the hall under the five great stars.
She has stood on enough walls to know that a line shown its best fighter on the other side stops believing it can win.
She has entered "Missing" beside Vexana's name herself every morning since the capture.
She thinks a file says what she can prove, and Vexana's stays Missing.
She orders the wall guns to hold: "Guinevere is on that platform. Nobody fires on it."
When Guinevere's signal is lost, her hand closes on the chair back without her knowing.
She thinks: I'm here this time, I'm right here, and it's a screen.
Seeing a gold glow behind a wall on the street camera, she says, "Her Emblem."
Her thumb goes to the bolt and her machine eye gives her the range to the Matrix, but no rifle could cross it.
She tells Layla that something took the Matrix's shot for Guinevere and to get to her if she can.
When Chang'e says her paper was only a guess, Lesley answers that it is now tested and to log it.
As commander she says Vexana's name for the first time that day.
She watched the Matrix fire on Vexana, then watched Vexana charge it.
She puts Vexana on the line for frontline assault with Guinevere, her voice level.
When told Vexana's file still says Missing, she says 'Change it.'
She concludes that something else is coming through the mouth.
She calls on mobile support to report.
She gives the frontline the Academy district as its ground, with the full shelters at their back, and keeps rear support close behind.
She reports that comms hold but suits do not, and it is not the storm from the records.
She stands behind Chang'e's chair with one hand on its back, as she has all day.
She thinks of the Citadel as the second front, here.
The coil on her rifle had run cooler than the old one since the dawn she fitted it.
She has a machine eye Chang'e built at the old base; it draws the deck in thin teal lines and uses no aspirant power.
The day Chang'e gave her the rifle she thought it would still work in the dark.
She orders the frontline back into the bay road cut to hold one street.
She held streets like that for the Shield before there were any suits.
She once told a room of Shield officers that imagination is Chang'e's weapon, with Chang'e on a crate beside her, and did not know Chang'e kept it.
She used to tell her little brother every night, 'Then I'll stand in front,' while he held her sleeve.
She always said No when Chang'e asked for a place on the rotation.
She pleads, 'Don't make me do this. Chang'e...'
She had given her reason only once: in the field, she cannot see Chang'e.
On the deck she can see Chang'e, and Chang'e is asking her, so she agrees to the plan.
She holds her fire one heartbeat, waiting for Chang'e's call.
She fires over Chang'e's head into the Ender's open core.
She always stops a step away from Chang'e.
This time she kneels and puts her arms around Chang'e and the dented robot both.
She had carried her vow since the night of the crater and thought it once in a tower window across the water, but never said it aloud.
She tells Chang'e, 'Ever since that day, I vowed to keep you safe, Chang'e.'
She tells every Aspirant whose suit went dark, 'As long as we have heart, we will never surrender.'
Her machine eye catches lightning crawling over the bell tower's roof.
Seeing the lights come back she says, 'There's still... hope... ah.'
She agrees the Matrix is gone back only for now.
Since the founding a caramel cup has turned up outside the lab door after every long night; neither she nor Chang'e has ever said a word about it.
When Chang'e says 'You owe me a pudding,' she answers 'Two.'

weapons.name: Lesley's rifle
weapons.note: A long red and gold bolt rifle Chang'e built for her birthday: a spring, a pin and a bolt, with no cell and no cable. It fires by hand, so it still works in the dark.

weapons.name: New coil
weapons.note: Chang'e's coil for the rifle, built to run on aspirant power alone. Lesley fits it on top of the old hand-worked action, which she keeps because Chang'e built it.

weapons.name: Lesley's eye
weapons.note: The machine eye Chang'e built for her empty left socket. It draws what it sees in thin teal lines, gives her range and keeps what it sees. It uses no aspirant power.

weapons.name: Dark visor
weapons.note: Covers her left eye and the teal light behind it. After her recurring dream she touches it and plays the recording of her birthday.

weapons.name: Black patch
weapons.note: The patch the station medic tied over her lost eye. Nobody saw under it until she took it off for Chang'e's eye.

weapons.name: Old Shield rifle
weapons.note: Her rifle before Chang'e's, worked by hand like every Shield rifle. The tape on its stock hung in strips.

weapons.name: White officer's coat
weapons.note: White, with a gold star. She comes in from the giants' front with its hem scorched.

weapons.name: Comm
weapons.note: A comm at her collar with a small green light and two channels, the base's and the Shield's.

weapons.name: Armband
weapons.note: The armband that made her a commander of the Shield's combat division, months after the base fell.

weapons.name: Notebook
weapons.note: A notebook and pen she carries in her coat. She hands them to Guinevere to write down everything she saw while she still remembers it.

Sleeps sitting up in a hard chair, boots on, rifle in reach of her right hand, never on her cot. Leaves a caramel pudding at Chang'e's lab door after long nights.

entries.line: Selrick Academy's young, cold Chief Combat Instructor, with a dark visor over one eye.
entries.short: The Chief Combat Instructor, head of all combat training at Selrick Academy. She is young and cold, with a dark visor over her left eye.
entries.summary: The Chief Combat Instructor of Selrick Academy, a sniper with a long rifle and a teal machine eye. In 983 an Ender took her left eye and her whole family, and she grew up at a far Shield station, sworn to kill every last Ender. Sent to guard a research base, she became Sis to its small genius Chang'e, who built her eye and her rifle, but on the night the base fell she came back from a secret mission too late, and Chang'e's parents died. Years of silence ended when she fired from a lit window to save Chang'e: they became the First Aspirants, and in the Storm Citadel's attack she holds her fire for Chang'e's call and at last says her vow aloud.

entries.name: Lesley's brother

facts.t: He claimed the worst day for a bad nap and got the pie.
He followed Lesley from room to room, held on to her leg, and called her Sis and nothing else.
He squeezed her hand hard as a cart rushed down the hill.
Every night he asked her if Enders were real and what would happen if one came.
He fell asleep holding her sleeve.
He noticed the candle that night was not for a birthday.
His last word, behind her in the dark, was 'Sis?'
Lesley found his hand under a beam; it did not hold on.
He said 'Sis?' as a question, the way Chang'e says it.
He held Lesley's sleeve every night and she promised him every night; she kept it, and he died anyway.
Every night he held Lesley's sleeve while she told him 'Then I'll stand in front.'

entries.line: Lesley's little brother, who called her Sis.
entries.short: Lesley's little brother. He followed her from room to room, called her Sis and nothing else, and fell asleep holding her sleeve.
entries.summary: Lesley's little brother followed her everywhere, held on to her leg and called her Sis and nothing else. Every night he held her sleeve and asked if Enders were real and what would happen if one came, and she told him, "Then I'll stand in front." On the night an Ender broke the house, his last word in the dark was "Sis?", and Lesley found his hand under a beam; it did not hold on. She kept her promise, and he died anyway.

entries.name: Lesley's father

facts.t: He mended small machines, mostly clocks, and hung them on every wall of the shop.
He let Lesley stand on a crate and hold the parts at his bench.
He told a stubborn clock: 'Don't sulk.' Lesley's mother says he says that to all of them.
For Lesley's last birthday he made her a tin bird that hops and clicks its beak.
He turned the radio down when it spoke of Enders.
He began leaving the radio on low at night, saying it was for the weather.
On the night of the attack he told the children to stay put, because the street was worse.
He shouted Lesley's name from the doorway as the roof fell.
He died where the doorway had been.
His bench sounded like a rifle bolt, with clocks on the wall; the clocks he wound by hand kept ticking the night the roof came down.
Lesley once sat in the rain between him and her mother.
He wound clocks by hand. When the violet storm came, only his clocks kept ticking.

entries.line: Lesley's father, who mended clocks in his shop.
entries.short: Lesley's father, who mended small machines, mostly clocks, and hung them on every wall of his shop. He let Lesley hold the parts at his bench.
entries.summary: Lesley's father mended small machines, mostly clocks, hung them on every wall of the shop and told stubborn ones, "Don't sulk." He let Lesley stand on a crate at his bench, made her a tin bird that hops and clicks its beak, and turned the radio down when it spoke of Enders. On the night of the attack he told the children to stay put and shouted Lesley's name from the doorway as the roof fell. He died where the doorway had been, and the clocks he wound by hand kept ticking.

entries.name: Lesley's mother

facts.t: She laughed from the kitchen door at Lesley's father talking to clocks.
She decided who had had the worst day, and that person got the biggest piece.
She kept one candle stub in the kitchen drawer and lit it on birthdays on whatever there was, once a boiled egg.
She told Lesley to wish fast and wish small, because it was a small candle.
She kissed Lesley's head and called her sensible.
She left the hall lamp on so the dark would not come under the door.
On the night of the attack she brought the lit candle upstairs, saying it was for seeing.
She died beside Lesley's father, one hand still out toward the children's bed.
Lesley once sat in the rain between her parents.

entries.name: Mr. Bunny

facts.t: A white ball that floats, with long ears and a black screen for a face.
At the word 'Front' he swings in front of Chang'e and takes a falling tray on his casing.
His screen shows a smile with the eyes shut.
Chang'e built him at the end of the bench as a friend, with a screen face so he could make faces.
Chang'e's father left a better battery beside him.
His shut-eyed smile copies Chang'e's mother's laugh.
He is named for his ears. When Chang'e is sad he comes around in front of her without being told.
Chang'e says he fetches.
His screen frowns when Lesley pokes him.
He lights Chang'e's night work with his screen.
Chang'e fits a small lens to his side so he can film Lesley's birthday.
He records all of the eye gift.
He is a floating robot with a screen for a face; he yawns on it as he follows Chang'e.
He helps push crates from the other side, though it does nothing, because he likes to help.
He fetches whatever Chang'e points at.
Each morning his screen shows the number of days since Lesley left.
Chang'e gives him a homecoming face for Lesley, with one round eye and one teal eye that winks.
During the attack he is left dark on the bench with his casing open.
Switched back on after the fall, he shows the homecoming face, and Chang'e wipes it away.
His lens shows what he sees; night after night he turns to the window where Lesley watches from a rooftop.
A blow sends him spinning away over the rooftops.
At Chang'e's call he comes back as a great white rabbit-head machine taller than the storefronts, his screen as big as a door, and the Enders break against him.
Chang'e thinks that size had never worked in the yard.
At dawn he is his own size again, his screen dimmed.
His sleeping face is two flat lines and a small Z.
When Ruby asks to read his code, his screen goes blank.
Chang'e calls him her best friend.
Chang'e uses him as her excuse to visit Lesley: he was lonely.
His screen dims when nobody needs him.

It floats at Chang'e's shoulder while she teaches.

He drifts down and stops in front of Angela's doll, close enough to touch its face.

A white robot rabbit hangs at young Chang'e's shoulder.
Its screen frowns at Selena when she doubts Chang'e is director.
It bobs after Chang'e as she leaves.
It floats at Chang'e's shoulder on the command deck.
His ears go flat when the floor hums.
He keeps floating at Chang'e's shoulder with his screen on when the field hits.
Chang'e's plan has him take the Ender's hit.
He swings in front of Chang'e's face and takes the claw on his casing, spinning down the console.
He comes back with one ear crooked and a dent across his casing; his screen flickers, then finds its smile with the eyes shut.
He showed Chang'e Lesley on a roof with a rifle, night after night.
He hangs at Chang'e's shoulder with one ear crooked.

entries.name: Obsidia

facts.t: She watches the city from the edge of the Storm Citadel, her ship, which hangs over the bay inside its own black cloud.
Wherever her ship's violet storm reaches, human machines die.
Her strike on the city came after midnight, while the humans slept.
She says to the rain: "We do not destroy; we merely purge the parasites from the host."
To her the host is the planet and the parasites are the people on it.
The Enders walking the ruins are hers. They are living machines that do not think.
Once she did not think either. Something vast and cold made her kind to kill on instinct.
She is the first of her kind to wake: one of them turned and looked at herself, and that was Obsidia.
After she woke, she watched stars collapse.
She helped end a people much like the humans of Terrinia.
Then she slept in the void for ages.
She woke with a question: when nothing is left to purge, what are her kind for?
She sees only two paths for her kind: sleep in the dark again, or war among themselves forever.
The thing that made her had no answer to her question.
So she made something of her own. She grew it in the nest, where her kind sleep until needed.
She carried the thing she made down to the city herself on the night of the strike.
She took a nightgown from a dead woman and dressed the sleeping child with her own hands.
She laid the child on the scorched ground and rose before the rain could wake it.
She knew the child would remember the mud, and nothing before.
Her storm cannot kill a flame.
When the child hugged the woman who found it, Obsidia leaned into the rain. She had not put that in it.
She thinks the humans have taken into their arms a seed that could end them.
She wants to see what will grow from that seed in human warmth and human greed.
After the strike the Storm Citadel climbs back into its cloud, and the street lamps flicker back on behind it.
She says to no one: "Out of pure curiosity, I added one more pawn to the board."
She stands at the edge of the Storm Citadel's highest deck as the door closes behind her ship.
The Citadel answers to her and to no one else; she is its Imperatrix, its empress.
The crossing has worn her: her shell has split in fine lines at the wrists and throat, and she means to go down to the body to be healed.
After the storm night she took the Citadel far out into the sea of stars to watch what grew from the seed, thinking her own hand close by would spoil the result.
She waited there year after year and read the pulse every day.
When Enders raid that world she looks out through their eyes, and they never know.
She closed her own end of the line in the moment she first looked at herself.
She tells the empty deck "It's... quiet..."
She has absolute control of everything aboard, and it brings her no satisfaction, only a nothingness that follows her like a shadow.
Years into the watch she felt Enders die with a light burning in their cores; in all her ages no Ender had died like that.
She wants one of the humans' machines that hold that light.
Late in the year before, she sent her pawn her first recall.
She counts everything, but after a while stopped counting the pawn's silences.
She says "Heh... even their defiance is within my predictions."
Her recalls carry nothing of where she is; one day she might send one that does.
She thinks the pawn will not dare follow, and notices with surprise that she would not mind being wrong.
She is amused that the pawn has rules.
She leaves the pawn's thread open, sure it will not lead the pawn to her.
She pays the pawn first in slack, then in places, never in words.
Through dying Enders' eyes she saw young humans in suits destroy an Ender army at a hole in the dome.
When the pulse changes, the body calls its commander in: it calls her.
She tells the holds "The Matrix is transmitting."
She finds it touching that the children of that world wear uniforms and learn to fight her kind.
To her the purge is only the work; what comes after is the question, and the pawn is her way to find out.
She sees one small light burning in the void that is not an Ender's, and knows its kind.
She sends nothing of the light up the line and marks the place; the violet in her eyes brightens.
She hangs at the top of the body's seam while strands of living violet tissue close fine cracks at her wrists and throat.
She stops the healing with one hand: "That's enough recalibration." One crack at her throat stays open.
She moves through the dark with her feet touching nothing.
She is shaped like a woman, with long blonde hair fading to pink at the ends, a black and magenta gown, a pink star at her chest where an Ender's core would sit, and a black clawed glove on one hand.
Her eyes are violet and blue. She is the first thing in the void to look back at Vexana.
Her eyes stop on Vexana's covered right wrist and their violet brightens, yet she says not one word about the sleeve.
She says the Will shows the end but never what comes after.
She names herself Obsidia and says the ship in the storm is hers.
She says she is the first of the Enders to wake into a self.
She says the body made her as its commander, made to watch a battlefield and shape the pulse for the Enders that cannot think.
She says the body healed her again and again for longer than humans have kept records.
She says she alone woke because she was made to watch and was kept. For ages there was no I, only orders, hunger and the pulse.
She says she woke at the edge of a great door over an ending world, when she noticed that the one watching was herself.
She calls existence a paradox: "To exist is to destroy... a truly intriguing paradox."
She says her end of the Will's line shut the day she woke, so what she sees stays with her.
She says each healing now smooths some of her away, so she takes it only when she must.
She calls herself the flaw: the body's rule says free will must be corrected.
She knows Vexana's name because the Will's orders carry it and she reads them. She says she listens to everything.
She waits a hand's width above the paving of her ship. Vexana does not hear her come.
She calls herself the Will's own: "I am its Will, the ender of civilizations."
Asked why she cut her healing short, she turns her silver-pink weapon's point toward Vexana, then away.
She says she helped end the people whose street hangs in her ship, under the same sky as Vexana's.
She says the body grew the living part of her ship when she woke, and she built the rest from what she ended.
She says she told Vexana all this because she wished to see what a human does with it.
She moves a whole block of the Citadel aside with a lift of her hand.
On the prow she lays her palm on a dead Aspirant suit's core, and a violet hum sinks into it. Only the core answers, with a tick.
She says the scorched suit is the first human machine she has held.
She calls lightning out of the storm with one finger and says: "I am the storm."
She says she sits where no one finds her, unless she calls them.
She says she woke at the edge of a black hole.
She says the Core has never been shown to her and she does not know where it is.
When Vexana declares against the darkness, she asks where that arrogance comes from, and does nothing more.
In the hollow, with her glove on the lead Guard's heart, she watches it wake for Vexana and calls it intriguing technology while three swords hang over her head.
She says she marked the hollow's fold the night her ship came through, but not how.
She read through the eyes in the rows that Vexana went twice to their edge.
She made a row of shells shaped toward human likeness. Some broke and none held a self.
She rests her clawed glove on a small empty dent at the end of the row and says nothing about it.
She asks Vexana what will become of the Enders once humanity has been purged. She says she has never asked a human before.
She says she once set down a seed with her own hands among a people in the rain, the first of her making to hold a perfect human form.
She says her finest making does not answer when she calls, and hopes that when the final stage arrives she will understand her purpose.
Selena has never seen her maker, but never doubted there was one: somebody made the hum in her bones.
She thinks of it as a hunter, then, sure without knowing why, a huntress.
For weeks the fearsome huntress had been crossing the sea of stars, closing in on Selena.
Now the crossing is over, and she waits right behind the Singularity.
Selena thinks nobody travels that far for one runaway, so whatever comes through is coming for the whole city.
Selena realizes someone from the Mother Matrix is coming for her.
Selena reasons that whoever sits at the far end of the pull gives the orders and has a seat she could take.
Selena thinks the huntress made her human face too.
She watches the Singularity through the eyes of a gray Ender standing on the prow of her ship.
Her throne hall lies deep among the hanging blocks of the Storm Citadel, and no way leads into it from outside.
She sits on the throne where a neck would be and feels its low, even hum through the seat.
When she lifts a hand, her weapon comes to her across the hall. Nothing else aboard comes to her hand.
She approves new plate for the Ultimate Enders with the words "Augmentation approved."
Through an Ender's eyes she watches the domed city, the last one left after years of the body's raids.
She counts none of the raids as failed. To her each was the cycle working on a people with nothing to fight it with.
She sees no need to set foot on such an insignificant world herself. She thinks even the storm night was for the seed, and that her hand would only spoil what grew.
She calls going down for the humans "A waste of time."
She has watched peoples on other worlds end, and none of them fought back with what they believed, as these humans do.
She thinks the body cannot answer a people that learns, because it has no mind to learn with, while she has one.
She knows her storm cannot touch the humans' cores, because a core lit by belief runs on no current.
She waited and built a field that could put out aspirant power.
For weeks she tested the field on a dead suit on her prow, until it struck only the core and left plate and metal alone.
The Storm Citadel was sent to crush humanity's resistance once and for all, but when she goes in is hers to choose.
Her plan is to wait behind the mouth with the field ready, and to go in only if the body does not finish the humans.
For years she has known the humans' light only through Enders dying of it. Tomorrow she means to look at it herself.
She calls the coming day the final stage of her experiment. Under every plan lies one want she never wrote down: to see a different ending.
She stopped paying Selena on purpose, thinking that a paid pawn stays where it is and an unpaid one comes looking.
She reads Selena's moves between two roofs as a bearing and says "Good."
In the nest she came back to Selena more often than the work needed and changed her face again and again until it was right.
On the storm night she carried Selena out of the nest and down herself.
Days before the attack she stopped at Selena's empty place in the nest with Vexana beside her, and did not ask herself why.
Her hand comes away from the seat while she thinks of Selena, and she lays it down again.
She says that someday, when this story nears its end, Selena too will return to her.
She will send one last call, carrying where she sits, once Selena shows her own form, and she means Selena to follow it.
She has planned every move her creation could make, and hopes it finds one she has not.
She expected Vexana to turn since she first saw her sleeve, but did not expect it to matter.
She read back along the pulse and learned the Will's plan for Vexana.
She tells no one the Will's plan, not even Vexana, because told, Vexana would do the predictable thing, and untold she might do something else.
She saw the fireworks in Vexana's memories. She asked Vexana about an after, and Vexana answered with an ending.
She lays her palm on the spine and says "The mouth," and the Citadel moves.
She watches through the prow Ender as the Citadel stops behind the mouth, while her storm pours into the city.
Selena thinks of her as the huntress behind the recall's pull.
Among the rows in the nest she said of something she had made: "If it ever slips beyond control, there is only one outcome."
On the prow of the Storm Citadel she told Vexana that a door held open this wide and this long grows a black hole at its center.
She told Vexana, "Nothing made of matter ever comes back out."
She had never even seen the Control Core.
She stands at the top of the steps in her throne hall, deep among the hanging blocks of the Storm Citadel.
She watches the battle through the eyes of the gray Enders on her outer blocks.
She saw a human's belief light a machine of Ender plates that had stayed dead under her own hand in the hollow.
She had told the girl on her prow that nothing made of matter ever comes back out of the black point.
She does not know how the two lights came back out.
On every world she helped end, nothing had wounded the Will's body until two human girls did.
She had known Vexana would turn since the day she looked at that sleeve.
She calls the Matrix's retreat 'merely a prelude to the end.'
A pulse tells her where her pawn is: alive on a tower over the Academy, having obeyed no call and sent no word for days.
She tells her weapon that her finest creation has gone off-script.
She had planned for both outcomes: watch if the body won, go in herself once the mouth was clear if not.
She holds back the last call so her pawn must first show its own shape.
She sets the Storm Citadel moving: 'Let us begin the final purge.'
Through her Enders' eyes she sees every Aspirant in the street burning bright.
She wakes the field by laying two fire-ringed black spheres against her throne.
After seeing her pawn stand before the humans in its own shape, she sends the last call, which carries where she stands.
She thinks the finest thing she made might tell her what comes after, for her kind.
Watching Selena come, she feels a pleasure she has not known in a very long time.
She says to no one, 'Look at how much you've grown, my child.'
She opens the hanging blocks along the line of her call to let Selena through.
She has long hair running from gold into pink, a black and magenta gown, and red gloves that end in claws.
Her face is smooth shell with a cold sheen, and her eyes burn violet; she is not surprised Selena came.
She greets Selena: 'It has been a while, my little doll.'
She tells Selena her name: Obsidia.
She tips Selena's face up with one finger and looks it over like something she carved herself.
She says destruction gives rise to new life, and that this is the meaning of purification.
She says the next thing to destroy is 'a pawn with no surprises left.'
She raises chains of bone from the floor without once looking at them.
She tells Selena, 'Savor your final moments, my dear Selena.'
Seeing Selena's full true form, her face shows something close to pleasure.
She fights unhurried, giving ground down the stairs and keeping Selena at her weapon's length.
She stands on the tilting stairs as if they were level.
When Selena cuts her cheek the shell splits in a thin dark line and no blood comes.
For the first time that day the calm leaves her face, and she gives no more ground.
She smirks as her point-blank shot throws Selena out of the Citadel.
She flies out of the smoke after Selena.
She remembers keeping her post at the edge of a great door among drifting stones while a world went dark, and cities under orange fire after.
Of everything she has watched, she watched longest a small thing curled like a sad girl at the end of a row in the nest, and later under a tarp in the rain.
Inside the gold fire of her change she says, 'You cannot save humanity.'
In her new form she opens her arms and says, 'Come back, my puppet.'

weapons.name: Storm Citadel
weapons.note: Her flying fortress of hanging black blocks. It answers to her alone, and she moves its blocks with a lift of her hand. The body grew its living part; she built the rest from what she ended.

weapons.name: Violet storm
weapons.note: Runs ahead of her ship. Wherever it reaches, human machines die. It cannot kill a flame, and it cannot touch a core lit by belief.

weapons.name: The field
weapons.note: Built while she waited behind the mouth, and tested for weeks on a dead suit. It puts out aspirant power over a whole city and strikes only the core, leaving plate and metal alone.

weapons.name: Black spheres
weapons.note: Two small black spheres ringed with fire. Laid against her throne, they wake the field.

weapons.name: Silver-pink weapon
weapons.note: A long weapon that comes to her hand across the hall. It lashes out at a finger's lift and fires bolts. It went through Selena's side, and a point-blank shot from its gold tip threw her out of the ship.

weapons.name: Lightning
weapons.note: She calls lightning out of the storm with one finger. "I am the storm."

weapons.name: Bone chains
weapons.note: Chains of bone, each ending in a spike, that crawl up out of the floor and pin a foe. She never looks at them.

weapons.name: Her Enders' eyes
weapons.note: She looks out through the eyes of any Ender, on her ship or raiding a world, and they never know.

weapons.name: The recall
weapons.note: A pull she sends down the pulse into Selena's cells to call her back. Her last call carried where she stood.

weapons.name: Clawed gloves
weapons.note: Gloves that end in claws. She lays one on what she studies: a Guard's heart in the hollow, an empty dent at the end of a row in the nest.

weapons.name: Pink star
weapons.note: A pink star that shines at her chest, where an Ender's core would sit.

weapons.name: New form
weapons.note: A taller shape of silver and gold plate with a crown of silver points and magenta light in its joints. Wings of purple and yellow energy open behind it, wider than the storm.

rows: The first Ender to wake into a self. She says she was made as the commander of the Enders that cannot think.
The Mother Matrix, the Will's body, she says. It has healed her for ages, but each healing now smooths some of her away.
The empress; the huntress, to Selena; her maker.
A throne hall deep among the Storm Citadel's hanging blocks, which no way leads into from outside. Her throne is the ship's spine.
A woman's shape with a face of smooth shell. Long hair running from gold into pink, a black and magenta gown, a pink star at her chest, clawed gloves, violet eyes.
The Enders, who do not think, and the Ultimate Enders, whose new plate she approves. She sees through their eyes.
Selena, her finest making, grown in the nest. Before her, a row of shells shaped toward human likeness that never held a self.
At the edge of a great door over an ending world, she says, beside a black hole, when she noticed that the one watching was herself.
She shut her end of it the day she woke, so what she sees stays with her. She still reads the Will's orders.
When nothing is left to purge, what are her kind for? She says the Will shows the end but never what comes after.
She says it has never been shown to her and she does not know where it is.

entries.line: The first Ender to wake, watching from her ship as the city's lights go out.
entries.short: The Ender who watches from her black ship above the bay as the lights of Terrinia go out one by one.
entries.summary: The first Ender to wake into a self, and the Imperatrix of the Storm Citadel, whose storm kills human machines. She says the Mother Matrix made her as its commander, and she asks what her kind are for once nothing is left to purge. In 983 she set down Selena, whom she calls her finest making, among the humans to see what would grow, and years later she brought her ship and a field that puts out aspirant power to Terrinia. Selena cut her throne down and the burning Citadel was drawn into the Singularity, and Obsidia, in a new form of silver and gold, opened her arms to call her puppet back as Selena charged.

entries.name: Professor Joe

facts.t: He speaks in a dry voice.
He is back from a field exercise when Fanny first has his class. He wears a monocle.
He teaches the Combat Division, and Team B3 is his: Layla, Roger and now Fanny.
He opens a gold-covered book, and a life-size VR Ender fills the wall.
He teaches that Enders expose their weak spots only when they launch attacks.
He teaches the three Ender ranks.
He teaches that badly hurt Enders go quiet for weeks in a lull, and a lull always ends.
He shows the Storm Citadel recording from the Academy's oldest records and reads its caption.
When a boom shakes the hall, he says the lull is over and the Enders are awake.
He is at the door with his sword drawn before anyone answers Roger.
At the breach he turns the crowd into a side street, shouting "Everybody fall back now!"
He picks up a crying girl's rabbit, kneels and gives it back, speaking softly in a voice he never uses in class.
He turns his back on a falling slab to cover the girl and her rabbit. It strikes him across the shoulders.
He lies still in the street, one hand open on the stones.
Roger reports that he is awake, with two ribs and the shoulder hurt, and that he wants to know if the girl got out.
On the tenth morning he walks into the drill hall on a cane, his shoulder strapped.
He dissolves Team B3 and names Layla and Fanny the Layla-Fanny Team, his and exclusive.
He says Aspirants fight in pairs because the suits decided it, not the Academy.
He gives the new team one shared score: a kill is a point, a civilian carried clear is ten.
He ticks both names on the pairing sheet with his stylus, two small marks with the same slant.
He says he pairs on hours, not scores, and that Layla and Fanny put in the most hours in his year.
A young Shield soldier with a monocle, he passes Lesley's dial test and becomes one of the first instructors.
Now Professor Joe, still on his cane, sees the third years off at the gate portal every day.
He assigns the fish-market raid: the Layla-Fanny Team to the west end, Guinevere and Vexana to the east.
In his lesson on weak spots, his last slide was a shaking recording from the Academy's oldest records: a ship of black blades over a city in a red sky.
His last slide showed that every machine under the Storm Citadel's storm had died.
He once pointed his cane at the pair's billboard and said, "Those two are undefeated. Ask them why. They can't tell you either."
In his class Layla called an Ender's weak spot obvious: when it attacks.
In his class Fanny saw the Storm Citadel in a shaking film.
He taught that Enders don't strike easily, and when one does, that is how long you get.
On the avenue on the day of the breach he knelt over a girl with a pink rabbit and spoke in a voice he never used in class; then a slab came down on him.

He holds the pads while Fanny punches.

He is in Joe's Team B3 with Layla and Fanny.

He falls on his back under the rearing Ender.
From his pod he says "Enough arguing, guys..." and nobody hears him.

He asks whether "Ultra" means Ultimate, and nobody answers.

He points out Guinevere and Vexana holding the other end of the wall.
He sends Layla word that Joe is awake.
Joe says he has gone to another pair and reports that he falls down less.
