entries.name: Ruby

facts.t: She told this part of her story only once, to the floor of a cell with no window.
As a small child she stands alone in the Council hall hugging a pink doll. Her eyes are wet, and she wipes them before anyone can see.
She is the heir to the Decisionmaker of Planet Oro. She has been told since before she could read that heirs can have no friends and no feelings.
When she thinks nobody is around, she makes her doll bow, low and crooked, the way grown-ups bow to her father.
Playing with her doll, she says: "Okay, nobody's around. Hehe... oh! ...Ahem."
She makes her face go blank, as she had practiced since she could walk.
In her lesson she recites that everything began with a single burst of chaos and that Balance keeps everything in order.
She knows the name Dawnbreak and nothing else about it.
Year after year of lessons, she grows taller, the doll is put away, and her face stays blank whenever anyone looks.
She still laughs sometimes when she is sure the hall is empty. She is not always right.
One evening she watches a dark ship with cyan lights cross the high windows until it is gone.
To her the whole planet is a prison, and she has been locked in it since the day she was born.
Her father rebukes her for laughing again, alone, and tells her she must be strong and unyielding.
She keeps her head down, and the tears run down her face anyway.
She answers her father: "...Yes, Father."
After he leaves, she whispers "But I have a plan..." though she has no plan yet.
The Council's engineers taught her to program. The Council orders her to build a sharper blade for the Balance Keepers.
She builds on a Project Angel body and writes the mind herself, piece by piece.
She sees that she can hide something in the android, as her way out.
Under the walking routines she tucks a few lines nobody asked for, with a lock that opens to her hand alone.
Three tries fail to unlock the Council's plate. She never learns what it does and builds around it.
She names the android: "From now on, I call you Angela."
She built every part of Angela's face by hand, but had never seen it smile.
Nobody had ever smiled at her like Angela does, because nobody was allowed to.
Without moving her lips, she tells herself: "You belong to me, and no one else."
Her face goes smooth when Angela asks about the will of the planet. She explains backlash, says she does not know the other phrase, and tells Angela not to say it aloud.
The Gardens are her secret base.
When Angela calls her a friend she freezes, because heirs cannot have friends.
After a moment she takes Angela's hands, smiling, her heart racing.
When Angela says she does not want to fight, she answers "I know" and tells her not to tell the trainers.
When Angela asks what she wants most, she looks up at the violet sky and does not answer.
She repairs Angela on the Laboratory table after the shield breaks.
She cannot finish explaining what hurt means. Her eyes are wet.
She murmurs that the light on the Council's plate never came on, and she does not know what that means.
When Angela gives her a flower, her eyes fill and a tear falls into Angela's palm.
She whispers to the flower: "What if they find out one day?"
After Angela's sixth return she falls asleep at her bench, the white flower in a glass at her elbow.
Ruby knows the Council's words: 'cleansed' means nobody on Dawnbreak is left outside Balance.
She objects to the plan, telling her father the people of Dawnbreak have done nothing to Oro.
When her objection is overruled she thanks her father and bows to the exact depth.
She keeps her laboratory dark, because a dark room is the nearest thing Oro has to privacy.
She hid forty locked lines of code under Angela's walking routines and wrote the lock first, so nothing can open them without her hand.
When the order comes she says: 'The long-awaited moment has finally come.'
She sees the trojan as perhaps her only chance to leave Oro, since Oro would need Angela's creator to shut Angela down.
Asked what will happen to Angela, she gives no answer and presses the key.
In the hangar she knows what 'save the Rioters' means, and tears come that she does not wipe.
She gives Angela the doll Tetra and does not say that its eye is a camera feeding a monitor on her bench.
When Angela hugs her she thinks, stunned, that they might really be friends.
Her arms come up late and stop in the air behind Angela's back without closing.
She was never allowed to open the plate on Angela's back, and learns from Tetra's feed what it is for.
She blames herself: she built Angela, knew what the order meant, and let her go.
The summons she planned for comes, but she feels no joy.
For years she wanted a ship off Oro; now she stops thinking about leaving and decides to go for Angela.
Her father made sure the heir could fight.
She says 'No... I'm not anyone's puppet.' and gets past the soldier who bars the ramp.
She cuts down a row of androids in one swing to save two fallen students, lightning crawling along her blade.
She uses Code Override on Angela's plate, but the Council's seal denies it.
She stops dodging Angela's late blows and keeps stepping in, even when one cracks her shoulder armor.
She tells Angela she does not want freedom at the cost of her.
She throws her arms around Angela and says: 'I'm never letting go of you!'
She tears the control unit out of Angela's back with her hands.
When Angela goes limp she believes she has killed her.
She stamps on the plate until its seal is gone, and her grief turns into rage.
One of her eyes burns red, and she does not know it.
She repeats 'If it wasn't for all of this...' in a voice that is not quite hers.
With her eye red she knocks aside the boy guarding a barrel and raises her scythe over the child hiding there, seeing only one more piece of 'all of this'.
When Angela calls her name the red goes out of her eye, and it is blue again.
Her scythe stops in the air short of Angela's light, and she lowers it herself.
She says what she wants most is to stay in this free land with Angela.
She asks Angela to wait for her at the end of the world if they are ever separated.
She gives herself up to Oro's soldiers because a fight there would burn what was left of the street.
She is charged with treason against Oro, and the Council is to pass sentence.
In the cell she confesses that she built Angela as her way out, hid a trojan in her, gave her Tetra as a secret camera and used her.
Her code opens the launch bay doors so they can escape.
Free of Oro, she laughs: 'Freedom! Hahaha!' Then she wonders why the alarm stopped.
At the lot she bows with a polished voice, names herself heir to the Decisionmaker of Planet Oro and asks Selrick for refuge.
When Lesley names the scythe raised over the child, she answers 'I lowered it myself.'
She greets Chang'e as Teacher Chang'e, in her perfect voice.
She pulled the Council's control unit out of Angela to keep her safe.
She hid a locked safeguard in Angela's code that opens only to her hand, so she can stop Angela if Oro ever takes her again.
She sweetly asks Chang'e to put her on the list too.
Green lines run from her glove into the doll's back, and she cuts its link to Oro in four seconds.
She asks to read Mr. Bunny's code in return: fair is fair.
Chang'e sees Angela as her best friend.
Lesley had already asked her the entry question on the landing lot.
Her needle on the dial passes the line with room to spare.
A white droid follows her everywhere and watches her with its orange eye.
She earned detention by feeding a ten-minute recording of herself into her droid's camera, over and over, for an hour.
She spent the hour eating a bun in the sun until Lesley found her on the third bite.
She straddles her mop like a horse, races and wins.
She says home is like a golden birdcage, lightly, like a joke; nobody laughs.
She politely wipes around Chang'e's face pressed to the window.
Her cloth stops mid-stroke when Lesley's eye rests on her.
She has told the others Oro lies in another galaxy.
At the ceremony she grounds her scythe and keeps her eyes on the floor in front of Lesley's boots.
Lesley makes her an Aspirant.
She is the girl with the scythe.
In the hall she holds her scythe point-down on the floor in front of Lesley in the week the newcomers become Aspirants.
She came down the ramp of a black ship at a cleared lot by the dome's foot, planted her scythe and bowed.
Guinevere recognizes her bow as the kind a manners tutor teaches; she called herself an heir, and Guinevere thought "Another one."
In the third-year class she sits by the wall, one row behind Selena, and asks whether the Ender Mecha Suit comes in her size.
She comes to the Science Division in the morning for Angela's check.
She lays her gloved hand on the bench and green lines run up the screen.
She tells Angela the hidden code lets her stop Angela if Oro ever takes her again, and that if she deletes it, nothing does.
She leaves the choice to Angela: "You're the one who controls yourself. What to do is yours to decide."
She does not say which answer she wants.
When Angela nods, the lock opens under Ruby's hand and the forty lines are deleted.
She tells Angela "Now you're free. Forever."
When Chang'e says deleting the code is a shame, she says "Not really."
She asks Angela what she wants the most.
She reads Guinevere's star by laying her fingertips beside it, sending green lines into the gold.
She finds the star's glow the same at every reading: it does not fade with distance or point a way, it only says yes.
She and Angela keep the tower's sensor array running in the observation lab at night.
She tells Guinevere the lab is closed at night, in her perfect voice.
At the next bench she looks up: "You didn't even read it."
She smiles at Selena as if Selena pulled a coin out of the air, and says good morning to her every day after. Selena never finds out why.
In Chang'e's lab she has code running.
On the first two nights she and Angela asked Guinevere to leave the lab. After that they kept the tower's sensor array running.
Weeks ago she ran code on a lab bench to make the Emblem of Hope a tracker.
She says the Emblem "only says yes."
She tells Angela, "Keep going," from the console.
She bends over the screen linked to the telescope, one eye behind her visor.
She reads the waveform as likely an Ender, with exceptionally powerful energy from the chest, and thinks it is trying to lure them in.
She warns Guinevere, "I said lure."
She saves the trace and sits with her gloved hand flat over it on the screen.
She is posted to rear support with Angela.
She runs through the hall with the scythe on her shoulder and says dryly on the channel, "Your sector, Commander."
She takes Lesley's order without a word against it.
Her scythe goes through a pane of the shield before anyone asks.
She swings once through a pane and lightning crawls down the blade. The ring on the platform side splits and falls into the water.
She says to Angela, "We escaped from this cage. We can also destroy it!"
In Angela's memory of the avenue, Ruby's eye burned red until Angela called her name.
She once told Angela, "I thought I'd killed you."
Her eye is blue now.
She holds the rail and keeps sending the Enders back with her scythe.
She knocks the last Ender off the rail and leans on it, her scythe on her shoulder.
When the two lights shoot out she says, 'The dawn is finally coming.'
She bumps her shoulder against Angela's.
After Vexana is put on the line, she tells Angela, 'She did that to us. Watched first. Then let us in.'
Fanny remembers soldiers holding rifles up at two girls off a black ship (Ruby and Angela) at the lot by the dome's foot.
She walks the edge of Angela's shield with her scythe crackling.
Her scythe is the one weapon still lit under the field.
She stands over the wounded at the top of the cut.
Her scythe was built by Oro and nothing in it runs on aspirant power, so the field found nothing to put out.
When an Ender throws Angela into a wall, a rage comes up in her.
The rage came once before, in a burning avenue: she cut down everything in front of her, a lamp post and a wall, then raised her scythe over a crying child.
She knows the rage never cared what it hit, and hers is the only live blade in a street full of wounded.
She decides Angela should not have to call her back again.
She makes herself hear the boy's crying to hold on.
She makes one cut into the Ender's core, and no more; the lamp post and wall behind it stand.
Her eyes stay blue.
She tells Angela she made that elbow and can mend it.
She tells the channel, 'What I'm supposed to do, I'll see through to the end, responsibly.'
On Oro every post was chosen for her, inside a golden birdcage; this one she chooses to keep.
She stands between an Ender and Angela and says coldly, 'Don't get in my way!'
She kneels beside Angela with a hand on her shoulder.
She laughs once on the channel when Angela's shield comes back.

entries.line: Heir to the Decisionmaker of Planet Oro, who builds the android Angela.
entries.short: The heir to the Decisionmaker of Planet Oro. Taught that heirs can have no friends and no feelings, she feels the whole planet is a prison.
entries.summary: Ruby, heir to the Decisionmaker of Planet Oro, builds the android Angela for the Council and hides a trojan in her as her way out. When the Council turns Angela on Terrinia, Ruby tears out its control unit and falls into a red-eyed rage, which Angela's cry stops short of a child. They escape Oro and become Aspirants at Selrick, and Ruby deletes the trojan when Angela chooses. In the last battle her Oro-built scythe stays lit under Obsidia's field, and when the rage comes back she makes one cut and her eyes stay blue.

entries.name: Ruby's father

facts.t: He leads the Decisionmakers, who give Oro's orders.
Grown-ups bow to him, low.
He stands outside Ruby's circle of light in the dark Council hall.
He tells Ruby he has heard she laughed again, alone, without raising his voice.
He says Oro has gone unopposed for thousands of years because its rulers do not bend, and Ruby must be strong and unyielding.
His boot comes down on her tears.
He tells her: "You cannot allow yourself to be so weak. Do not disappoint me, Ruby."
He walks out through the far door into white light without looking back.
His desk is black glass with a star map inside it.
He tells Ruby that Dawnbreak is at war with the Enders again and that the Council calls this unrest.
He reports that all three of Oro's powers have voted to cleanse Dawnbreak and bring it into Balance.
He says Dawnbreak's people make weapons from the Enders' dead and will not stay in their place, and he overrules Ruby's objection.
He had never once come to Ruby's laboratory before he stands in its doorway, looking only at her face.
He opens his mouth a little, closes it, and leaves without a word.
He made sure the heir could fight.
He sits alone before the security wall of the secret facility, watching the cell on a screen.
He cannot remember the last time he saw Ruby smile.
He was strict to make Ruby ready, since Oro would be hers one day, and on sleepless nights asks if he robbed her of her childhood. Each time, duty to Oro answers.
The last time he stood in her doorway he went away with the words still in his mouth.
He will not accept that the Council might sentence Ruby to death.
When the Council asks for a status report, he answers 'All normal.'
He puts his hand on the panel and stops the alarm, letting Ruby and Angela escape.

When she and Angela break out of the secret facility, he tells the Council "All normal" and stops the alarm with his hand on the panel, letting them escape.

entries.name: Selena

facts.t: Obsidia made her as something of her own and grew her in the nest.
She looks like a little girl. She is the first of Obsidia's kind with a perfect human form.
Obsidia dressed her, still asleep, in a nightgown taken from a dead woman. The hem fell past her bare feet.
Obsidia laid her on the scorched ground of the city. She would remember the mud, and nothing before.
The rain woke her. She stood up and did not cry or run.
A woman with a lamp found her, knelt and gathered her up.
Her face did not change, but her arms went around the woman's neck and held on.
Obsidia had not put that embrace in her.
The woman laid her at the end of a row of the living under a tarp, where she lay curled alone.
Obsidia thinks of her as a seed that could end the humans.
Obsidia calls her one more pawn added to the board, out of pure curiosity.
At Selrick Academy a blonde girl walks along the top of the wall beside a dragon-shaped machine, late, with a horned crest on her headgear.
She jumps down from the wall and lands running.
She tells the whole courtyard: "I can't stand waking up early, the sun in my eyes, and taking orders!"
A student says she built the dragon machine herself and nobody else can even get it to move.
She calls Chang'e 'Teacher Chang'e'.
She has a lollipop in her cheek and wears her uniform jacket open over a shirt stamped S·L·K.
Silverbolt, a dragon-like machine, waits behind her.
She brings Chang'e a form and asks for one signature.
Her field-test report lists a new stabilizer and one fence, replaced.
She says the fence was in the way.
The family name box on her form is empty.
She calls herself 'Just Selena' and says the form gives in eventually.
She and Chang'e trade sweets as always: a lollipop for two jelly candies.
Nobody but her can run Silverbolt.
She says Silverbolt is shy.
The professors marvel at her feel for mechas.
A blonde girl, older than Chang'e, comes to the base's outer fence most evenings to watch its machines through the wire.
When Chang'e waves at her, she does not wave back.
Chang'e recognizes her on the Science Division's first list as the girl from the salvage stall.
She keeps a trestle table at the city's edge, and she mended an old servo there with a trick Chang'e had never seen.
Asked what she mended it with, she says "Hands."
She sold the servo to Chang'e for every coin in Chang'e's pockets and two jelly candies.
The family-name box beside her name is empty and glows red.
Chang'e takes her for a child with no family, like many in the city.
Chang'e lays her thumb on the box and it turns green, approving her entry.
She is a blonde girl from the Science Division who slips into Chang'e's class late, on foot.
During the lesson she sits by the wall and draws armor in a sketchbook.
Her pen does not stop while Chang'e speaks of the Mother Matrix.
She comes late to the third-year class with a lollipop in her cheek.
When the teacher says she is late again, she says her guardian already called it in, and the note is there.
She lays her head on her arms and naps in class: "I'm taking a little nap. You all just keep going."
She wakes up saying there was a cupcake and it was hers.
She shows an Ender Mecha Suit on her desk screen, made with Ender plating, and says it is her own design.
She says everything comes in any size, "For a price."
When a boy calls the things in her head dangerous, she waves her lollipop and says one day, when the haze clears, they will know the real her.
She passes the lab bench with a lollipop in her cheek, Silverbolt clicking at her heel.
Glancing at Guinevere's star, she says to nobody "Lost things turn up."
She is out of the door before anyone can answer.
Every student in Vexana's year knows she sells Ender wreckage at the crews' yard outside the outer fence, after dark.
She sits on a crate at the crews' yard, her Academy jacket open and a salvage pass clipped to its pocket.
When a big man swings at her over a price, she is never where the fists land.
She warns him: "If you get too smug, you'll get tripped up."
She hooks a tarp rope taut with her heel and trips him into the mud.
Seeing Vexana in Ender plate, she only moves her lollipop and says "Nice hair."
Her calm at seeing a classmate in Ender plate nags at Vexana for a moment.
She had said in class that her plating came in any size, for a price.
She says she would take stipend money, but Missing people don't draw a stipend.
She agrees to trade plating for the places of two whole dead Enders.
While sorting plates she tells Vexana that most people think she is dead, but her partner does not.
She sells it as genuine Ender plating and says the last owner didn't complain.
She says goodbye with "Ahaha, bye-bye!"
She charges three places for each core.
Obsidia planted the seed on that world after the storm night, then went far away to watch what grew.
The line tells Obsidia where her pawn is, that it lives and whether it obeys, and nothing more.
It did not come back when Obsidia sent her first recall late in the year before, or after any recall since.
Obsidia thinks it has learned the humans' ways, and defiance is one of them.
Days after the first silence it opened a thin thread beside her recall, on a storm night, up through the Ender parts of its own machine.
Its first words up the thread were "Not coming back" and "Let's trade."
It reported the Academy's dull routines, last year's suit specifications, how aspirant power drives a suit, and how strong suits run by kind and rank.
Its reports named no person and told nothing about where people could be killed.
Obsidia paid it first in slack, letting the pull in its cells sink to a murmur for a week.
Then she paid it in places: where an Ender had fallen, set in its head before the humans could drag the wreck away.
It sends reports only on storm nights, when lightning hides the thread from human instruments.
Obsidia means it to show her what comes after the purge.
Obsidia says she set down a seed with her own hands among a people in the rain, the first of her making to hold a perfect human form.
Vexana takes it for another world and another people Obsidia ended.
Obsidia calls her the finest of all she has made, and says she does not answer when Obsidia calls.
Vexana thinks even what Obsidia makes says no to her.
Obsidia hopes that when the final stage arrives, she will finally understand her purpose.
Her earliest memory of the world is the scent of mud on a stormy night.
She rebuilt Silverbolt herself, and nobody else can make it move.
When the pull comes with a red alert she says to nobody: "Stop trying to control me."
She woke in the mud of a Terrinia street in 983, in rain, with nothing before it: no bed and no face.
On that first night a deep hum from a black cloud over the water filled her bones and felt like home.
When Karina held her, her arms went around Karina's neck. It felt easy to break, and she held it without squeezing.
Years later she still asked why carbon-based lifeforms were so warm yet so fragile, and why their warmth made the Ender cells in her blood cry out for conquest and also want to cling to it.
On her first night she already knew she was not one of them.
She learned words by watching mouths and kept every one to herself.
Her first spoken word was the name she chose for herself, Selena. She never told anyone where she found it.
As a child she practiced smiles in dark window glass, copying the baker and the woman downstairs, and kept the ones that earned a second sweet.
Storms never frightened her. Each crack of thunder made her bones go calm.
Asked in class how to stop a fire running down a street, she said to knock down the next house first.
Destructive power and dangerous thoughts came naturally to her, and people praised them as talent. To her it was all a game of pretend.
After an Ender passed her by and her cut healed purple, she told Karina she had no cuts.
After reading the Shield's notice she knew what she was, and decided nobody else would know, not even Karina.
On the roof in a storm, two small horns pushed up through her hair. She drew them back in and kept them in after that.
Her hands were always warm after storms, and all that winter she was never ill.
She can feel where current stops inside a machine, the way she feels an Ender's hum. No book taught her that.
As a girl she lifted an iron shutter off a trapped boy's leg that two grown men could not have shifted.
She sold mended salvage from a crate, later a trestle table under a tarp, at the city's edge.
People's praise never meant anything to her. What fascinated her were the cold mecha constructs of Selrick Academy, whose energy felt like what flowed in her own veins.
She joined the Science Division for its suits, tools and Ender wreck, and because nobody hunts for an Ender inside the place built to fight them.
She left the family-name box on her form empty: Selena is the whole name.
Her professors marveled at her feel for Aspirant mechas, never knowing she was a living source of the technology they studied.
No suit core lights for her. She thinks there is nothing in her it wants.
At the Academy she pins on a horned headband and lets her own horns up through her hair in front of it, drawing them in again before home.
She never bites a lollipop. She lets each one melt down to the stick.
Riding Silverbolt in a storm, she shouts: "Nothing matters more to me than my freedom!"
Told she will be a hero, she answers: "Champion of justice? Sounds like a real pain in the shoulders. I think I'll pass."
Only she knows that Silverbolt is, in every sense, a weapon of the Enders.
She ignores the red alerts on purpose, knowing they are a recall from the Enders trying to drag her back to the Mother Matrix.
Selling Academy information to the Enders, her rule is never a name and never a place where people die.
She resolves that if anyone ever points what she sold at the Academy, she will break it herself.
She openly sells Ender technology from wreckage to Vexana, curious to see how another pawn like herself might escape the game.
Passing Guinevere under the billboard, she thinks two words would do it, dead ground, but she rides past and says nothing.
She will not return to the Mother Matrix, and she will not die protecting humanity.
She considers taking the huntress's own seat, then sets the idea aside, deciding nothing.
In dark glass she lets the purple up on her left side only: the right half is the Academy's Selena, the left half is the Ender.
She keeps Karina's last fruit drop wrapped in her pocket instead of letting it melt.
She sold Obsidia last year's numbers as if they were stale. They told Obsidia how hard her field must press.
On the morning before the attack she crossed her city to the Academy. She lived, and she had not obeyed Obsidia.
Late in the year before, an Ender in a burning street heard a human shout her name at her. Obsidia's first recall went down the pulse soon after.
Obsidia stopped paying her on purpose, so she would come looking.
She sent two more reports up the thread unpaid, then went still.
On the next storm night she sat on her tower over the Academy, then on a roof at the far edge of the city, then went back.
In the nest she had no name. She lay curled at the end of a row of shells that never held, in a small place pressed into the body's tissue, while her body grew.
Obsidia changed her face again and again until it was right.
Obsidia carried her out of the nest and down on the storm night.
She has a form of her own that she has not yet shown.
In class she sits in the front row and reads the Academy feed on her phone, held sideways.
Startled by the feed, she drops her pen and papers and cries, "If the world ends now, what about my graduation?!" The class laughs.
Chang'e posts her as mobile support and calls her machine the fastest in her division.
She does not answer when Lesley calls mobile support to report.
She sits on the bell tower tiles with her boots over the drop, and lets the wind try to push her off.
She came up between classes, while everyone else crowded the hologram wall.
She started a new lollipop on the stairs up.
Under the Academy's call runs the recall. For weeks it has burned in her cells, pulling her toward the sky over the bay, and now it pulls from the open mouth.
The recall buzzes on her phone too, red, with no sender. She does not take it out.
She answers neither call.
She smiles at the chaos below.
She tells Silverbolt, "I'm the type who shines in chaos."
She thinks somebody wins today, them or us, whoever us is.
She has already turned down both roads: going back to the Mother Matrix and the huntress, or dying for humanity.
She decides her road is her own and that she will sit this one out until she sees how the pieces fall.
From the tower she watches Guinevere in the courtyard put a hand to her collar.
Fanny sees her on the bell tower, heels against the stone and a lollipop stick at her lips, her dragon-shaped machine beside her. Neither moves.
Fanny takes her for a spotter in the best seat in the city, waiting to see something.
She calls the Mother Matrix 'just big and useless' around her lollipop.
She once sold Vexana a gray Ender shoulder plate one night in the dead ground.
She sold Vexana the plates because she wanted to see how a pawn gets out of the game.
The recall in her cells goes thin while the Matrix reels, then comes back hotter and nearer.
She sits at the edge of the bell tower in her school uniform, making her lollipop last.
She knows the Citadel's hum: every Ender she ever passed carried a small piece of it.
Her bones call the hum 'home', and she answers that so does everybody else.
She calls the one pulling at her the huntress.
Her smile when the Citadel arrives is none of the ones she keeps.
Her rule is never to move first and to let the huntress show her hand.
The field passes through her bone by bone and finds nothing to take.
In class she read out the top row of the Academy's table of suits; every number was higher than the ones she sold.
She judges the field good work and thinks she would have built it the same way.
On the broken wall she once thought she would break it herself if anyone pointed it at the Academy.
For weeks before the charge she had not heard Guinevere laugh.
She had already ruled out going back to the Matrix or a hero's grave; one road was left, her own, up to the huntress's seat.
She knows that saying no means betraying her own kind for good and being hunted without end.
She would rather live as Selena, a name she chose herself, than be someone else's pawn.
She wears the polite smile she learned from humans.
She pushes Silverbolt into overload and its lightning surges into her, closing plate over her arms.
She looks once at the cut where Guinevere lies and steps off the tower.
She drops from the sky between the long-legged Enders and Guinevere, cracking the stones.
Her two small horns grow out of her blonde hair; in class they sat in front of a dark headband, which is gone now.
She tells Guinevere, 'Take a good look. This is the real me.'
When a boy on the Academy stairs called her dangerous, she waved her lollipop and said 'One day, when the haze clears...'
In class she sat in the front row, came in late every morning with her guardian's note, and slept on her arms through lessons.
Under Guinevere's steady look her smile goes, showing a face Guinevere has never seen.
The bell tower is where she always does her thinking.
She follows the recall back to its sender the way she follows a fault through a circuit on the workshop bench.
She does not remember a single minute of the last time she met her maker.
Under Obsidia's finger her blood goes quiet and wants to stay quiet; she notes it and files it.
She tells Obsidia, 'I'll never be your puppet again!'
She has copied every face she has ever met.
She refuses to take the throne: it would be the same board, a better chair.
She tells Obsidia she does not care about purification: 'Give me back my freedom!'
She had walked out of every fight of her life without a scratch until Obsidia's weapon went through her side.
She had never said she would save humanity.
She tells her maker, 'Sorry, ma'am.'
She tells Obsidia, 'But I still prefer life at the academy!'
She charges at Obsidia's open arms.

weapons.name: Silverbolt
weapons.note: A small dragon-shaped mecha she rebuilt from an Academy training frame, every part from her own Ender salvage. No core lights for her, so her purple lit it. Only she can make it move.

weapons.name: Silverbolt's overload
weapons.note: Pushed into overload, its seams go from blue to white and its lightning surges into her, closing Ender plate over her arms. It starts her change.

weapons.name: True form
weapons.note: Her full Ender shape: plate of white, blue and gold and a large pale mane. It is the Ender Mecha Suit she once showed the class as her own design.

weapons.name: Four blades
weapons.note: Four black-and-gold blades that hang in the air around her and swing in with every cut.

weapons.name: Arm blade
weapons.note: A blade of crackling light along one arm. With it she cut Obsidia's throne through at the base, and later cut Obsidia's cheek.

weapons.name: Claws and fangs
weapons.note: In her own shape she has red eyes, pointed ears, fangs and black claws. Her claws tore apart the point of a bone chain at her throat.

weapons.name: Lightning
weapons.note: Lightning bursts out of her. It broke Obsidia's bone chains, split the clouds open toward the Storm Citadel, and carries her up the sky.

weapons.name: Horned headband
weapons.note: A dark headband shaped like a horned crest. At the Academy she wears it in front of her real horns so they pass for part of it.

weapons.name: Lollipop
weapons.note: Nearly always melting in her cheek. She never bites one, except once, on the bell tower before she goes up to the Storm Citadel.

weapons.name: Fruit drop
weapons.note: A fruit drop from Karina in a twist of paper. She keeps it wrapped in her pocket instead of letting it melt.

weapons.name: Phone
weapons.note: Shows the Academy feed, and buzzes red with alerts that have no sender: the Enders' recall. She swipes them away.

weapons.name: Salvage stall
weapons.note: A crate, later a trestle table under a tarp at the city's edge, where she sells mended salvage.

rows: An Ender, the first of Obsidia's making to hold a perfect human form. Ender cells run in her blood, and she keeps it secret from everyone.
Obsidia, who grew her in the nest, changed her face again and again until it was right, and carried her down on the storm night.
Karina, the woman with the lamp who found her in the rain on her first night. Selena grew up in Karina's flat in Terrinia.
Selena, a name she chose for herself. It was her first spoken word. The family-name box on her forms stays empty.
Science Division of Selrick Academy. In the attack Chang'e posts her as mobile support, and she answers no call.
Blonde, with two small horns she lets up through her hair in front of a horned headband. Uniform jacket open over an S·L·K shirt.
Her cuts heal purple, and storms calm her bones. She feels where current stops inside a machine, and as a girl lifted a shutter two grown men could not.
Mends and sells salvage and Ender wreckage at the city's edge. She sold Obsidia Academy information, never a name and never a place where people die.
Chang'e, her teacher, who marks her reports and trades sweets with her. Ruby says good morning to her every day.
Late every morning with her guardian's note. Naps in class. Lets every lollipop melt to the stick. Does her thinking on the bell tower.
Her freedom. She will not go back to the Mother Matrix, will not die for humanity, and will not take Obsidia's seat: same board, better chair.
