entries.line: A blonde Academy student who hates orders and built a dragon-shaped machine.
entries.short: A blonde student at Selrick Academy who hates early mornings and orders. She built Silverbolt, a dragon-shaped machine nobody else can make move.
entries.summary: A girl Obsidia grew in the nest and left in the mud of Terrinia in 983, the first of her kind with a perfect human form. Karina found her and raised her, and she hid the Ender in her blood, named herself Selena, rebuilt Silverbolt from salvage and joined the Science Division, where nobody hunts for an Ender. She ignored every recall and sold Academy numbers to Obsidia and Ender plating to Vexana, but never a name or a place where people die. When Obsidia's field put out the Aspirants, she showed her real face, rode her lightning up into the Storm Citadel, cut the throne down instead of taking it, and charged her maker rather than go back as her puppet.

entries.name: the Academy gate guard

facts.t: When Guinevere asks at the gate for post on rest days, the guard says "Nothing today."
A guard calls Guinevere to the gate when Hester comes.

rel.t: The guard keeps the Academy gate.

entries.line: The guard who keeps the Academy gate.
entries.short: The guard at the Academy gate. When Guinevere asks for post on rest days, the answer is "Nothing today."
entries.summary: The guard who keeps the gate of Selrick Academy. Every rest day Guinevere asks at the gate for post from home, and every time the guard says "Nothing today." Four days before her final trial, a guard calls her to the gate, where Hester waits outside the bars.

entries.name: the attendance clerk

facts.t: He frowns at his tablet at the attendance desk when Selena comes in late.
He says her guardian called with a fever, and that she looks fine.
Selena says it broke.

entries.line: The clerk at the Academy's attendance desk.
entries.short: The clerk at the attendance desk. He frowns when Selena comes in late after a night out.
entries.summary: The clerk at the Academy's attendance desk. When Selena comes in late after a storm run, he frowns at his tablet and tells her that her guardian called first thing about a fever. He looks her up and down and says she looks fine. "It broke," says Selena.

entries.name: the baker

facts.t: Selena copies his smile.
Selena tells Karina her new smile came from the baker.
Selena gives him his own smile on the way home, and he waves.

entries.line: A baker in Terrinia whose smile Selena copies as a child.
entries.short: A baker in Terrinia. As a small child Selena practices his smile in the dark window glass.
entries.summary: A baker in Terrinia. As a small child Selena practices smiles in the window glass, and his is one of the first she tries. She tells Karina her new smile came from the baker, and Karina says it looks better on her. Later, walking home past the bakery, Selena gives him his own smile, and he waves.

entries.name: the big man at the crews' yard

facts.t: He stands at the trestle table shouting at Selena over a crate of plating: "Half price, or I take it!"
He swings at her twice and misses, the second time hitting the post.
He pins a hand beside her head and grins that she has nowhere left to lean.
He trips on the tarp rope, falls in the mud, and stamps off swearing toward the gate.
Vexana waited in the dark for him to leave before she stepped into Selena's lamp.

rel.t: She trips him into the mud when he tries to bully her on price.

entries.line: A big buyer who tries to force Selena's price with his fists.
entries.short: A big man at the crews' yard. He shouts at Selena over a crate of plating and tries to force her price.
entries.summary: A big man who buys salvage at the crews' yard. One night he shouts at Selena over a crate of plating: "Half price, or I take it!" He swings at her twice and misses, the second time hitting a post, then pins a hand beside her head. He trips on the tarp rope, falls in the mud and stamps off swearing. Vexana waits in the dark for him to leave before she steps into Selena's lamp.

entries.name: the boy at the gate

facts.t: He looks twice at Selena's horns: "Nice. Where'd you get those?" She says she grew them, and he laughs.

entries.line: A student at the gate who notices Selena's horns.
entries.short: A student at the Academy gate. He looks twice at Selena's horns and asks where she got them.
entries.summary: A student at the Academy gate. The first morning Selena lets her own horns show, behind a horned headband, he is the only one who looks twice. "Nice. Where'd you get those?" She says she grew them. He laughs and goes on.

entries.name: the boy from the drill line

facts.t: He skinned his palm in drills, and Guinevere had a band-aid on it before he could say no.
He laughed with her when she said Baroque money paid for the band-aid too.
On Team-Up Day he saw Guinevere coming, went pink and grabbed the boy beside him as his partner.

rel.t: He is a cadet in Guinevere's drill line.

entries.line: A cadet in Guinevere's drill line.
entries.short: A cadet in Guinevere's drill line. When he skins his palm, she has a band-aid on it before he can say no.
entries.summary: A cadet in Guinevere's drill line. When he skins his palm, she has a band-aid on it before he can say no, and tells him Baroque money paid for that too. He laughs with her. On Team-Up Day he sees her coming to ask him, goes pink and grabs the boy beside him as his partner.

entries.name: the boy in the second row

facts.t: He asks "Balance?" during Chang'e's lesson.
He asks what the Control Core is.
He asks what a black hole is.

rel.t: He is in Chang'e's class.

entries.line: A student in Chang'e's class who keeps asking questions.
entries.short: A boy in the second row of Chang'e's class. He asks what her words mean.
entries.summary: A boy in the second row of Chang'e's class. During her lesson on the Will of the Planet he keeps asking what the words mean: "Balance?" Then what the Control Core is. Then what a black hole is.

entries.name: the boy on the stairs
aka: the boy on the Academy stairs

facts.t: He leans over the stair rail and calls "Selena! The things in your head. Dangerous!" meaning it as praise.
He calls Selena dangerous. She promises him he will meet the real her one day.
The whole stairwell laughs.
He once called Selena dangerous on the Academy stairs, and everybody laughed.

entries.line: A student who calls Selena dangerous on the Academy stairs.
entries.short: A student on the Academy stairs. He calls Selena dangerous, meaning it as praise.
entries.summary: A student at the Academy. Leaning over the stair rail, he calls out that the things in Selena's head are dangerous, and he means it as praise. Selena promises him he will come to know the real her one day, and the whole stairwell laughs. Much later, when Selena shows her real self, nobody laughs.

entries.name: the boy under the shutter

facts.t: After a raid he lies in the street with a fallen shop's iron shutter across his leg, crying in the rain.
Selena lifts the shutter and whispers: "Shh. It won't hurt anymore."
He limps off shouting toward the rescue lamps, which turn toward him.

rel.t: She lifted the shutter off his leg.

entries.line: A small boy pinned under an iron shutter after a raid.
entries.short: A small boy pinned under a shop's iron shutter after a raid, crying in the rain.
entries.summary: A small boy caught after a raid, with a fallen shop's iron shutter across his leg, crying in the rain. Selena lifts the shutter, which two grown men could not have shifted, and whispers: "Shh. It won't hurt anymore." She turns him toward the rescue lamps and tells him to shout. He limps off shouting, and the lamps turn toward him.

entries.name: the boy with a hook

facts.t: He looks Selena over: "You're new. Hooks are extra." She uses her hands.

rel.t: A scavenger.

entries.line: A young scavenger in the base's ruins.
entries.short: A young scavenger in the ruins of the base. He tells Selena that hooks are extra.
entries.summary: A young scavenger who picks through the ruins of the research base after its fall. He looks Selena over when she joins them: "You're new. Hooks are extra." She uses her hands instead.

entries.name: the boy with the red tie

facts.t: A boy in a Selrick uniform with a red tie stands in front of a barrel, hands empty and shaking.
He begs Ruby: 'Please, it's only a kid.'
Ruby knocks him aside with the flat of the scythe, and the barrel he guarded rolls away.
He shouts at Ruby from the ground, and she does not hear him.

rel.t: He wears a Selrick uniform.
The boy stood guard over it.

entries.line: A Selrick student guarding a hiding child with empty hands.
entries.short: A boy in a Selrick uniform with a red tie. He stands in front of a barrel, hands empty and shaking, and does not move.
entries.summary: A boy in a Selrick uniform with a red tie. During the attack on Terrinia he stands in front of a barrel, hands empty and shaking, where a small child hides. He begs Ruby: "Please, it's only a kid." She knocks him aside with the flat of her scythe, and the barrel rolls away. He shouts at her from the ground, and she does not hear him.

entries.name: the boy with the skinned knee

facts.t: He skins his knee on the school steps, howls, and picks at the scab for a week.
Selena compares her purple-healed cut with his week-long knee.

entries.line: A boy in Selena's childhood class.
entries.short: A boy in Selena's class who skins his knee on the school steps and picks at the scab for a week.
entries.summary: A boy in Selena's class when she was small. He skins his knee on the school steps, howls, and picks at the scab for a week. Selena watches it until it is gone. Her own scrapes are always gone before she thinks to look, and she later compares a cut that healed purple with his week-long knee.

entries.name: the camera droid

facts.t: At the foot of the stage it asks Guinevere and Vexana to stand closer.
It asks for more shots, saying someone blinked.
It asks for a back-to-back picture for the courtyard.
It prints the hand-in-hand picture, one copy each, in a thin black frame.
It sent the photo to both their phones.

entries.line: The droid that takes the Best Aspirant Duo photographs.
entries.short: A camera droid at the foot of the stage. It asks Guinevere and Vexana to stand closer.
entries.summary: A droid that takes photographs at the Best Aspirant Duo ceremony. It asks Guinevere and Vexana to stand closer, asks for more shots because someone blinked, and asks for one back to back for the courtyard. It prints the hand-in-hand picture, one copy each, in a thin black frame, and sends the photo to both their phones.

entries.name: the child in the barrel

facts.t: A small child hides in a barrel at the avenue's end, then crouches in the dust and cries.
It looks up at Ruby, face wet, as she raises the scythe.
Angela's ring of light lifts it out of the blade's path.
It is unhurt.
Lesley brings up the scythe raised over it when Ruby asks for refuge.

rel.t: The boy stood guard over it.
She rescues the child from Ruby's scythe.

entries.line: A small child hiding in a barrel in burning Terrinia.
entries.short: A small child hiding in a barrel at the end of an avenue in burning Terrinia, where a boy in a red tie stood guard in front of it.
entries.summary: A small child who hides in a barrel at the end of an avenue in burning Terrinia, while a Selrick boy in a red tie stands guard in front of it. When Ruby knocks the boy aside, the child crouches in the dust and cries, and looks up at her, face wet, as she raises the scythe. Angela's ring of light lifts it out of the blade's path, and it is unhurt. Lesley brings up that raised scythe when Ruby asks for refuge.

entries.name: the Combat Division boy

facts.t: Leaning over the rope at the year's showing, he tells Selena she will be a hero with Silverbolt.
He laughs at her answer.

rel.t: A boy from the Combat Division.

entries.line: A Combat Division student who calls Selena a hero.
entries.short: A boy from the Combat Division. At the year's showing he tells Selena she will be a hero with Silverbolt.
entries.summary: A boy from the Combat Division. At the year's showing he leans over the rope around Silverbolt and tells Selena she will be a hero with that thing. Selena says being a champion of justice sounds like a pain in the shoulders, and she will pass. He laughs.

entries.name: the counseling woman

facts.t: In a room with soft chairs and a window full of plants, she pours two cups of tea.
She asks Guinevere to sit down and tell her about Vexana.
Guinevere leaves at once, and the tea stays full on the table.

rel.t: She works in the counseling section.

entries.line: An older woman in the Academy's counseling section.
entries.short: An older woman in the counseling section. She pours tea and asks Guinevere to tell her about Vexana.
entries.summary: An older woman who works in the Academy's counseling section. In a room with soft chairs and a window full of plants, she pours two cups of tea and asks Guinevere to sit down and tell her about Vexana. Guinevere sits, says "She's alive," and leaves at once. The tea stays full on the table.

entries.name: the courier

facts.t: A courier brings Ruby the Council's order to build a sharper blade for the Balance Keepers.

rel.t: The courier carries the Council's order.

entries.line: A messenger who brings Ruby the Council's order.
entries.short: A courier who brings Ruby the Council's order: build a sharper blade for the Balance Keepers.
entries.summary: A courier on Oro, who brings Ruby the Council's order to build a blade sharper than any the Balance Keepers have. That order is how Angela comes to be made.

entries.name: the examiner

facts.t: He takes Selena's paper without a word about the red box and calls the next name.

entries.line: The examiner at Selena's Science Division entry.
entries.short: The examiner at the Science Division entry, who takes Selena's paper without a word about her empty name box.
entries.summary: The examiner at the Science Division's entry test. Selena leaves the family-name box on her form empty, and it glows red. She waits for questions or a shut door. The examiner takes her paper without a word and calls the next name.

entries.name: the girl at the cake counter

facts.t: She tells Guinevere that one of everything on the top row is eleven cakes.

rel.t: She works behind its counter.

entries.line: The girl behind the counter of the girls' house cake shop.
entries.short: The girl behind the counter at the cake shop. She tells Guinevere one of everything on the top row is eleven cakes.
entries.summary: The girl who works behind the counter of the girls' house, a cake shop down the hill from the Academy. When Guinevere orders one of everything on the top row, she points out that it is eleven cakes. Guinevere orders eleven.

entries.name: the girl at the next desk

facts.t: She asks whether Selena's drawing is a suit design. Selena says something like that.

entries.line: Selena's classmate at the next desk.
entries.short: A girl at the desk next to Selena's. She asks whether Selena's drawing is a suit design.
entries.summary: A classmate at the desk next to Selena's. As Selena draws a suit of armor on her desk screen over months, the girl asks whether it is a suit design. Selena says something like that. She is drawing the shape she feels folded under her own skin.

entries.name: the girl in the red dress
aka: the girl with the pink rabbit
a little girl on her hip

facts.t: A little girl in a red dress stands crying in the middle of the pavement, her pink rabbit at her feet. People run around her.
Joe picks up her rabbit, kneels and puts it back in her arms.
Joe covers her and the rabbit from a falling slab.
A woman sweeps her up.
When the gold giant appears, a child's voice asks: "Mommy, what's that?"
She walks out of the crowd alone into the avenue, her face turned up to the giant.
Fanny scoops her onto her hip, and the rabbit falls.
As Fanny carries her she says: "I'm flying!"
Fanny sets her down behind a van in a side street and tells her to stay.
Fanny says she got out: her mother was running to her.
Fanny once carried a little girl on her hip and told her that flying felt great.
On the avenue on the day of the breach, Joe knelt over a girl with a pink rabbit and spoke to her softly.

weapons.name: Pink rabbit
weapons.note: Her toy. Joe kneels to give it back, and it falls when Fanny lifts her.

rows: A red dress, with a pink rabbit

rel.t: The pink rabbit is hers.
He takes a falling slab across his back to cover her.
She carries the girl out of the giant's path.
Her mother runs to her.
Fanny carried her.
He knelt over her on the avenue.

entries.line: A little girl with a pink rabbit, caught in the street at the breach.
entries.short: A little girl in a red dress crying in the street at the breach, her pink rabbit at her feet. Professor Joe covers her from a falling slab.
entries.summary: A little girl in a red dress who stands crying on the pavement at the breach while people run around her. Professor Joe gives back her pink rabbit and covers her from a falling slab, which strikes him instead. When the gold giant comes she walks out into the avenue alone, and Fanny scoops her onto her hip just before its beam burns the place where she stood; "I'm flying!" she says. Fanny leaves her behind a van, and her mother runs to her.

entries.name: the girl with two braids

facts.t: At the Shield's home she sat down by Vexana at breakfast and offered her a blue ribbon so they would match.
When Vexana said no, her face fell and she took her bowl to another table.
Years later Guinevere's "Now we match" reminds Vexana of her.

rel.t: She lived at the home.

entries.line: A girl at the Shield's home who offers Vexana a ribbon.
entries.short: A girl with two braids at the Shield's home. She offers Vexana a blue ribbon so they would match.
entries.summary: A girl with two braids at the Shield's home for soldiers' children. At breakfast she sits by Vexana and offers her a blue ribbon so they would match. Vexana says no, and the girl takes her bowl to another table. Years later, when Guinevere says "Now we match," Vexana remembers her.

entries.name: the girl's mother

facts.t: Fanny leaves the rabbit facing the avenue where a mother coming back would see it.
Fanny says the girl's mother was running to her when Fanny left her behind the van.

rows: The girl in the red dress

rel.t: Her mother runs to her.

entries.line: The mother of the girl in the red dress.
entries.short: The mother of the girl in the red dress. Fanny leaves the girl's pink rabbit where a mother coming back would see it.
entries.summary: The mother of the girl in the red dress, caught in the attack at the breach. After the fighting, Fanny sets the girl's pink rabbit on a broken wall, facing the avenue, where a mother coming back would see it. Fanny later says the mother was running to the girl when Fanny left her behind a van.

entries.name: the gray-haired professor

facts.t: He sets a dead pump on Selena's bench and stands back to watch.
Leaning in the doorway of Chang'e's lab, he calls Silverbolt's refusal fine tuning: tuned to one pilot, like the director's gear.

rel.t: One of the professors.

entries.line: A gray-haired professor of the Science Division.
entries.short: A Science Division professor. He sets a dead pump on Selena's bench and stands back to watch.
entries.summary: A gray-haired professor in the Science Division. On Selena's first days he sets a dead pump on her bench and stands back to watch. Later, leaning in the doorway of Chang'e's lab, he calls Silverbolt's refusal to move for anyone else fine tuning: tuned to one pilot, like the director's own gear.

entries.name: the grumbling classmate

facts.t: Picking glass from his sleeve after a test rig blew, he grumbled that Selena always walks away without a scratch.

entries.line: A Science Division classmate who grumbles about Selena.
entries.short: A classmate who grumbles that Selena always walks away without a scratch.
entries.summary: A classmate of Selena's in the Science Division. Picking glass out of his sleeve after a test rig blew, he grumbles that she always walks away without a scratch. He does not know how true that is.

entries.name: the gunner

facts.t: In the east gun pit, his face goes bright with the light of an Ender's open core.
He fires into the opening and kills the Ender.
That night he chalks a stroke on the armory door.

rel.t: He serves at the station.

entries.line: A gunner at Lesley's Shield station.
entries.short: A gunner in the east gun pit. He fires into an Ender's open core and kills it.
entries.summary: A gunner at the Shield station where Lesley grew up. In the first raid she sees, an Ender's chest opens over the east gun pit and the light of its core fills his face. He fires into the opening and kills it. That night he chalks a stroke on the armory door, where the station keeps its count. Watching him, Lesley learns that the chest opens only when it strikes.

entries.name: the House servant

facts.t: A servant brings Guinevere tea and says the master knows she is there.
The servant takes away the cold pot and brings a fresh one.
The servant tells her the master took his lunch at his desk.

rel.t: A servant of the House.

entries.line: A servant of House Baroque who brings Guinevere tea.
entries.short: A servant of House Baroque who brings Guinevere tea and says the master knows she is there.
entries.summary: A servant of House Baroque. While Guinevere waits all day on the bench outside her father's office, the servant brings her tea and says the master knows she is there. The tea goes cold, and the servant brings a fresh pot. Asked whether her father has eaten, the servant says the master took his lunch at his desk.

entries.name: the library droid

facts.t: It sits at the library's front desk and turns its one lens to Vexana.
Asked for anything on the void, it lists three papers on its screen.
It prints Chang'e's paper for Vexana.

rel.t: It works at the front desk.

entries.line: The one-lensed droid at the library's front desk.
entries.short: The droid at the library's front desk. It turns its one lens to Vexana when she comes in.
entries.summary: The droid that sits at the front desk of the Academy library. When Vexana asks for anything on the void, it lists three papers on its screen. The third is Chang'e's, on aspirant power and the black hole, and the droid prints it for her.

entries.name: the man at the fence

facts.t: He tells the crowd the flyers are the instructors, Shield soldiers in the new suits.

entries.line: An onlooker at the Academy's opening day.
entries.short: A man at the fence on opening day. He says the flyers are the instructors: Shield soldiers in the new suits.
entries.summary: A man in the crowd at the fence on the morning Selrick Academy opens its gate. As figures in suits rise on wings of light and fly over the city, he tells everyone they are the instructors, Shield soldiers in the new suits. No suit had flown over the city before that day.

entries.name: the man under the sign

facts.t: In Fanny's VR assessment a man shouts from under a fallen sign. A voice says simulated civilians are not scored.
Fanny pulls him clear first, which costs eleven seconds.
Layla reruns the assessment leaving him under his sign. Fanny's record reads CIVILIAN RECOVERED, +0:11.

rel.t: She pulls the simulated civilian clear first.
Fanny pulls him clear.

entries.line: A simulated civilian in Fanny's VR assessment.
entries.short: A simulated man trapped under a sign in Fanny's VR test. Civilians are not scored, but Fanny pulls him clear first.
entries.summary: A simulated civilian in Fanny's VR assessment. He shouts from under a fallen sign, and a voice says simulated civilians are not scored. Fanny pulls him clear first anyway, which costs her eleven seconds. Layla reruns the test five times leaving him there, and Fanny's record still reads CIVILIAN RECOVERED, +0:11.

entries.name: the manners tutor

facts.t: A manners tutor spent years teaching Guinevere how to bow.

rel.t: The tutor taught Guinevere her bow.

entries.line: The tutor who taught Guinevere how to bow.
entries.short: Guinevere's manners tutor, who spent years teaching her how to bow.
entries.summary: One of Guinevere's tutors at House Baroque. She talked all day about a lady's refinement, which meant how you hold your back, and spent years teaching Guinevere how to bow. Guinevere knows that bow at once when Ruby plants her scythe and bows at the lot.

entries.name: the medic

facts.t: A medic tapes Layla's cheek and wraps her left forearm in gauze after the battle.
After the fish-market raid a medic tapes Guinevere's wrist.
After the raid the medic told Guinevere to rest.
The medic allowed Guinevere's bag work with her left hand only.

rel.t: Tapes her wrist.

entries.line: A medic who patches up the fighters after a battle.
entries.short: A medic who tapes Layla's cheek and wraps her forearm after the battle.
entries.summary: A medic who tends the fighters after the fighting. After the battle at the breach, a medic tapes Layla's cheek and wraps her left forearm in gauze. After the fish-market raid a medic tapes Guinevere's wrist, tells her to rest, and allows her bag work with her left hand only.

entries.name: the night-shift researcher

facts.t: Someone found flour and sugar for his birthday cake, and the lab sang to him over the benches, badly.
Chang'e brings Lesley a slice because it is his birthday.

rel.t: He works the night shift at the base.

entries.line: A researcher at the base whose birthday cake Chang'e shares.
entries.short: A night-shift researcher at the base. The lab finds flour and sugar for his birthday cake and sings to him, badly.
entries.summary: A researcher on the night shift at the research base. For his birthday someone finds flour and sugar, and the whole lab sings to him over the benches, badly. Chang'e carries a slice out to Lesley, because it is his birthday, so she gets cake.

entries.name: the officer who posted Lesley

facts.t: He has Lesley's file open on his desk.
He sends her, as the best young shot they have, to keep the research base's two chief scientists and their child alive.
He posted Lesley to the base, and he comes out in person because he will not give these orders over the comm.
He tells her Headquarters calls the whole core piece a miracle and sends her on a top secret mission.
He orders no radio and no letters, because the Shield thinks the Enders can hear its signals.
He says another soldier will take her gate.

rel.t: He is a Shield officer.
A Shield officer.
He gives Lesley her orders.
She accepts his order to go on the mission.

entries.line: The Shield officer who posts Lesley to the research base.
entries.short: A Shield officer. He sends Lesley, the best young shot they have, to guard the research base's scientists and their child.
entries.summary: A Shield officer with Lesley's file on his desk. He sends her, as the best young shot they have, to keep the research base's two chief scientists and their child alive. After she brings in an Ender core piece whole, he comes out in person, because he will not give these orders over the comm. He sends her on a top secret mission with no radio and no letters, since the Shield thinks the Enders can hear its signals, and says another soldier will take her gate.

entries.name: the officer with gray in his beard

facts.t: He has gray in his beard and a rank armband on his sleeve, and nobody on the channel listens to him.
He knows Lesley by the rail yard shot.
He hands Lesley his radio handset, and the squads answer her.
Months later he brings Lesley the armband that makes her a commander of the Shield's combat division.
He tells her the squads asked for her because she held the avenues.
He leads the Shield's officers who come to see Chang'e's suits.
He points out that no Shield soldier could lift an arm in the suits.
He asks who will keep the suits running.

rows: Gray in his beard and a rank armband on his sleeve
Giving Lesley command on the night the base fell

rel.t: A Shield officer.
He hands her his radio handset.

entries.line: A Shield officer with gray in his beard and a rank armband.
entries.short: A Shield officer with gray in his beard whom nobody on the channel listens to. He hands Lesley his radio, and the squads answer her.
entries.summary: A Shield officer with gray in his beard and a rank armband on his sleeve. On the night the base fell nobody on the channel listened to him, so he handed Lesley his radio handset, and the squads answered her. Months later he brought her the armband that made her a commander of the Shield's combat division, because the squads had asked for her. He leads the officers who come to see Chang'e's suits and asks the hard questions: who could lift an arm in them, and who will keep them running.

entries.name: the old Shield sergeant

facts.t: This old Shield sergeant taught Hester to fight before the House hired her.

rel.t: She learned to fight from this sergeant.
A Shield sergeant.

entries.line: The old Shield sergeant who taught Hester to fight.
entries.short: An old Shield sergeant who taught Hester to fight before House Baroque hired her.
entries.summary: An old sergeant of the Shield of Dawnbreak, who taught Hester to fight before House Baroque hired her. Hester later passes his lessons on to Guinevere at the sandbag: elbow in, hip first, hands home.

entries.name: the oldest of the scientists

facts.t: He reads Chang'e's report and stops at the line where she crossed out belief.
He copies the word aspirant power into his own report.
He frowns that Chang'e's plan is a school, not a regiment.

rel.t: The oldest of them.

entries.line: The oldest of Terrinia's scientists.
entries.short: The oldest of the city's scientists. He stops at the line in Chang'e's report where she crossed out belief.
entries.summary: The oldest of Terrinia's scientists. Reading Chang'e's report on the first suits, he stops at the line where she crossed out belief and wrote aspirant power. She tells him belief sits still and this reaches, and he copies the word into his own report. When Chang'e lays out her plan to teach young fighters in pairs, he frowns that it is a school, not a regiment.

entries.name: the quartermaster

facts.t: He warns Lesley the tower room is cold and nobody wants it.

rel.t: The Shield's quartermaster.

entries.line: The Shield quartermaster who gives Lesley her tower room.
entries.short: The Shield's quartermaster, who warns Lesley that the tower room is cold and nobody wants it.
entries.summary: The quartermaster of the Shield of Dawnbreak. When Lesley asks for a room at the top of an old tower across the water, the quartermaster warns her it is cold up there and nobody wants it. She says it has a window.

entries.name: the records clerk
aka: a clerk from the records office

facts.t: He stands under the board outside the Combat office with a form in his hand.
He says there has been no trace of Vexana since the corridor, and after this long the form says Killed in action.
When Lesley refuses, he takes his form back and goes.

rel.t: He comes from the records office.

entries.line: A clerk who comes to change Vexana's file.
entries.short: A clerk from the records office. He brings a form to change Vexana's file from Missing to Killed in action.
entries.summary: A clerk from the Academy's records office. Weeks after Vexana is taken, he stands under the board outside the Combat office with a form. There has been no trace since the corridor, he says, and after this long the form says Killed in action. Lesley refuses: no body, no finding. He takes his form back and goes.

entries.name: the researcher
aka: the researcher who gave her the big bench

facts.t: He tells Chang'e the big bench is for grown-ups and sends her back to her corner.
When Lesley appears silently in the doorway, he finds work at the far end of the lab.
After seeing the first light, he tells Chang'e the big bench is hers.
On the night the base fell he carries Chang'e in from the yard and puts his own coat round her.
He brings her soup and suggests a children's home in the city; after her answer he never says home again.
He tells her finishing the frame will not bring her parents back.
When the Enders return he blocks her way and says her mother would want her in the shelter.
He never left the base, and Chang'e makes him the first of the Science Division's professors.

rows: Researcher at the base, later the first professor of the Science Division

rel.t: One of the night shift.
He looks after her after the fall.
She makes him the first Science Division professor.
Its first professor.

entries.line: A researcher at the base who keeps the big bench for grown-ups.
entries.short: A researcher at the base. He tells Chang'e the big bench is for grown-ups and sends her back to her corner.
entries.summary: A researcher at the base who once sent Chang'e back to her corner, saying the big bench was for grown-ups, and who gave it to her after he saw the frame's first light. On the night the base fell he carried her in from the yard in his own coat. He brought her soup and stopped saying home after her answer, though he warned that finishing the frame would not bring her parents back. He never left the base, and Chang'e made him the first of the Science Division's professors.

entries.name: the schoolteacher

facts.t: She tells Selena to get under the table in a storm, because everyone else is.
When Selena says to knock down the next house to stop a fire, she smiles: that is what the fire crews do. "Clever girl."

entries.line: Selena's teacher at her childhood school.
entries.short: Selena's teacher when she was small. She tells Selena to get under the table in a storm, because everyone else is.
entries.summary: Selena's teacher at school when she was a child. When a storm comes, she tells Selena to get under the table, because everyone else is. Another day, when Selena says the way to stop a street fire is to knock down the next house first, the class gasps and the teacher smiles: that is what the fire crews do. "Clever girl."

entries.name: the scorched suit's pilot

facts.t: A pilot's belief once lit the scorched suit's core.
Vexana says she did not know the pilot.
Obsidia answers that Vexana's hand did, since it had closed.

entries.line: The pilot whose belief once lit a scorched Academy suit.
entries.short: The pilot of the scorched Academy suit that Obsidia holds on her ship. A pilot's belief once lit its core.
entries.summary: The pilot of an Aspirant suit that ends up scorched black, one arm gone, on the prow of Obsidia's ship. A pilot's belief once lit its core. Vexana had watched two feeders drag the suit from a ditch in the dead ground, its last hand still a fist. When Obsidia asks if she knew the pilot, Vexana says no. Obsidia answers that her hand did, because it had closed.

entries.name: the sergeant at the fence

facts.t: He pulls Guinevere down by the collar as she climbs the outer ward's fence at night.
He is gray at the temples with a rifle on his back, and works out who Guinevere is from her pink hair and red bows.
He tells her "No pass, no entry, miss."
When she says she will find Vexana, he tells her to do it with a pass.
He walks her back under the lamp and writes her name in his book.
He reports her at a closed fence, at night.

weapons.name: Rifle
weapons.note: Carried on his back.

rows: Gray at the temples, a rifle on his back

rel.t: He is a Shield sergeant.

entries.line: A Shield sergeant who stops Guinevere at the outer fence.
entries.short: A Shield sergeant at the outer ward's fence. He pulls Guinevere down as she climbs it at night.
entries.summary: A Shield sergeant, gray at the temples, with a rifle on his back. One night he pulls Guinevere down by the collar as she climbs the outer ward's fence, and works out who she is from her pink hair and red bows. "No pass, no entry, miss." When she says she will find Vexana, he tells her to do it with a pass, walks her back under the lamp and writes her name in his book. His report reaches her father.

entries.name: the sergeant at the lot

facts.t: A sergeant asks Fanny on whose word she vouches for the newcomers.
At the lot by the dome's foot he asked Fanny 'On whose word?' when she vouched for the two girls off a black ship.

rel.t: He is one of the soldiers at the lot.
He is a sergeant among the soldiers.

entries.line: A Shield sergeant at the lot where the black ship lands.
entries.short: A Shield sergeant at the lot, who asks Fanny on whose word she vouches for the newcomers.
entries.summary: A Shield sergeant in the line of soldiers at the cleared lot by the dome's foot. When a black ship lands and Fanny vouches for the two girls who walk down its ramp, the sergeant asks: "On whose word?" Fanny answers: "Mine." She remembers that moment much later, on the platforms.

entries.name: the sergeant at the rail yard

facts.t: He stares at the whole core piece and says Ender cores always burn.

rel.t: Sergeant of the squad Lesley saved.

entries.line: The sergeant of the squad Lesley saves at the rail yard.
entries.short: The sergeant of a Shield squad at the old rail yard. He stares at the whole core piece Lesley brings down.
entries.summary: The sergeant of a Shield squad pinned behind a wagon at the old rail yard. Lesley draws the Ender off them and shoots its core at the edge, so one piece splits away whole. He stares at it and says Ender cores always burn. Nobody had thought it could be done.

entries.name: the shelter clerk

facts.t: He sits at a table by the shelter door with a box of cards. Ink stains his hand to the wrist.
He writes on a card: girl, no name, and guesses her age.
He says half the children there have not said a word, from shock.
He tells Karina she cannot keep signing the log.
He has a list of names for children without one and tries Anna and Rose.
After a week he stops asking.

rel.t: He names Karina and watches her keep the child.

entries.line: The clerk who writes a card for a nameless girl.
entries.short: A clerk at a shelter after a strike. He writes on a card: girl, no name, and guesses her age.
entries.summary: A clerk at a table by a shelter door, with a box of cards and ink to the wrist. He writes on a card for a silent child: girl, no name, and guesses her age. He says half the children there have not said a word, from shock. He tells Karina she cannot keep signing the log, and tries names on the girl, Anna and Rose. After a week he stops asking, and Karina keeps her. The girl is Selena.

entries.name: the Shield clerk

facts.t: He asks Lesley her date of birth when the Shield takes her as a soldier.
It was the one time Lesley gave anyone her birthday.

rel.t: He enlists her.

entries.line: The clerk who enlists Lesley in the Shield.
entries.short: The Shield clerk who asks Lesley her date of birth when she joins as a soldier.
entries.summary: A clerk of the Shield of Dawnbreak. When the Shield takes Lesley as a soldier, the clerk asks her date of birth. She gives it and does not think of it again. It is the one time she gave anyone her birthday.

entries.name: the Shield soldier on the hill

facts.t: He knelt and wound a field dressing around Lesley's head, over the left eye.
He tied a paper tag to her wrist and told her to wait at the bottom of the hill.
He told her the Enders come in groups from out down the road beyond the city.

rel.t: He is a Shield soldier.

entries.line: The Shield soldier who bandages Lesley's eye.
entries.short: A Shield soldier. He winds a dressing over Lesley's left eye, tags her wrist and sends her down the hill.
entries.summary: A soldier of the Shield of Dawnbreak, who comes up the hill after the rain thins. He kneels and winds a field dressing around Lesley's head, over the left eye, ties a paper tag to her wrist and tells her to wait at the bottom of the hill. When she asks where the Enders come from, he points down the road out of the city: out there, in groups.

entries.name: the small boy

facts.t: He cries in a shelter doorway up the cut.
He comes down the street looking for someone and finds the wall instead.
He takes a fistful of the back of Layla's uniform and holds on.
He asks Layla whether Fanny is her friend.
A soldier with his arm in a sling walks him back up the street.
Ruby makes herself hear his crying to keep hold of herself.

rel.t: She lets the crying boy hide behind her.
She comforts the crying boy.
He takes the boy back to safety.

entries.line: A small boy crying in a shelter doorway during the battle.
entries.short: A small boy crying in a shelter doorway up the cut while the battle goes on below.
entries.summary: A small boy who cries in a shelter doorway up the cut during the battle. He comes down the street looking for someone and finds Layla holding it instead, takes a fistful of the back of her uniform and holds on. He asks Layla whether Fanny is her friend. A soldier with his arm in a sling walks him back up the street, and Ruby makes herself hear his crying to keep hold of herself.

entries.name: the small girl at the shelter

facts.t: A man runs past Chang'e with a small girl on his hip, and a woman beside them holds her hand; the girl has her eyes shut.
They reach the shelter's doors with ten steps to spare.
At dawn she rides out of the shelter on her father's hip with her eyes open.

rel.t: Chang'e guards the doors she ran through.

entries.line: A small girl carried into the seawall shelter.
entries.short: A small girl on her father's hip, eyes shut, running for the seawall shelter as the Enders come.
entries.summary: A small girl carried down the avenue on her father's hip, her mother holding her hand, her eyes shut. They reach the seawall shelter's doors with ten steps to spare, and Chang'e takes her place in front of those doors. At dawn the girl rides out of the shelter on her father's hip with her eyes open.

entries.name: the soldier under the slab

facts.t: A slab of fallen wall pins his legs until Angela lifts it off.
He drags himself clear.
When an Ender drops at him, Angela throws herself over him.

rel.t: She shields the soldier from a claw with her own back.

entries.line: A wounded soldier pinned under fallen wall.
entries.short: A soldier pinned by a slab of fallen wall. Angela lifts it off his legs with her bare hands.
entries.summary: A wounded soldier in the bay road cut. A slab of fallen wall pins his legs until Angela lifts it off with her bare hands, and he drags himself clear. When an Ender drops at him from a roof, Angela throws herself over him and takes the claw on her back.

entries.name: the soldier who brought the toolbox

facts.t: On Vexana's second day at the home he brought her father's toolbox and set it by her cot.
He told her the Ender never got past her father while he stood.
He brought Vexana's father's toolbox to the home, set it by her cot, and said "That Ender never got past him. Not while he stood."
A soldier sat beside Vexana's cot and told her the Ender never got past her father, not while he stood.

rel.t: He carried the toolbox to Vexana.

entries.line: A soldier from the city wall who came to Vexana's cot.
entries.short: A soldier from the city wall. On Vexana's second day at the home he brought her father's toolbox and set it by her cot.
entries.summary: A soldier from the city wall who came to the Shield's home on Vexana's second day there. He set her father's toolbox beside her cot and told her, "That Ender never got past him. Not while he stood." Years later Vexana still remembers his words beside her cot.

entries.name: the soldier who carried Vexana
aka: the soldier who carried Vexana off

facts.t: During the attack he caught Vexana from behind, threw her over his shoulder and ran.
When she shouted for her father, he only ran faster.
He carried the young Vexana off down the street while her father stayed to fight.

rel.t: He carried her away from the Ender.
He carried her away from the Ender.

entries.line: The soldier who carried the young Vexana away.
entries.short: A soldier who catches the young Vexana from behind, throws her over his shoulder and runs.
entries.summary: A Shield soldier in the attack on the wall. When an Ender comes at the young Vexana and her father steps between them, this soldier catches her from behind, throws her over his shoulder and runs. She shouts for her father, and he only runs faster. Over his shoulder she watches her father's back as he stays to fight.

entries.name: the soldier with the sling

facts.t: A soldier with his arm in a sling takes the small boy's hand and walks him back up the street.

rel.t: He takes the boy back to safety.

entries.line: A wounded soldier who walks a small boy to safety.
entries.short: A soldier with his arm in a sling. He takes the small boy's hand and walks him back up the street.
entries.summary: A wounded soldier in the bay road cut, his arm in a sling. During a lull in the fighting he takes the small boy's hand and walks him back up the street, away from the wall.

entries.name: the stallholder

facts.t: At the arcade's fabric stall the stallholder says everybody likes the pink felt.
The stallholder wraps Vexana's felt in brown paper.

entries.line: The keeper of the fabric stall in the arcade.
entries.short: The keeper of the arcade's fabric stall, who says everybody likes the pink felt.
entries.summary: The keeper of the fabric stall in the middle of the arcade, which sells felt in squares of every color. The stallholder says everybody likes the pink, and wraps Vexana's felt in brown paper. Vexana later sews a small pink head and a black one from it.

entries.name: the station medic

facts.t: He swaps Lesley's field dressing for a black patch.
Nobody saw under the patch after he tied it on.

rel.t: He serves at the station.

entries.line: The medic at the Shield station who gives Lesley her patch.
entries.short: The medic at the Shield station, who swaps Lesley's field dressing for a black patch.
entries.summary: The medic at the far Shield station where Lesley is taken as a child, who swaps her field dressing for a black patch over her left eye. Nobody sees under that patch again until Chang'e asks her to take it off.

entries.name: the station sergeant

facts.t: A heavy man with a burned hand who finds Lesley hiding at the station.
He has a boy Lesley's size in the city who still cannot tie his boots, and says the station is no place for either of them.
When she stays, he tells her that if she is staying, she works.
He lets her fire one round a week at a fence post with the gunners.
The first time she climbs the wall in a raid he carries her down; after that he only looks.
In time he gives her five rounds a week.
He orders the soldiers to fall back when an Ender crosses the wall.
After her kill he holds out the chalk so she can make her own stroke.

rows: Gives the orders at the Shield station
A heavy man with a burned hand
A boy Lesley's size in the city who still cannot tie his boots

rel.t: He is a Shield sergeant.
He carries her down from the wall in her first raid.
He gives the orders there.

entries.line: A heavy Shield sergeant with a burned hand.
entries.short: A heavy Shield sergeant with a burned hand who finds Lesley hiding at the station. If she is staying, he tells her, she works.
entries.summary: A heavy man with a burned hand who gives the orders at the Shield station where Lesley hides. He has a boy her size in the city and says the station is no place for either of them, but when she stays he puts her to work and lets her fire one round a week at a fence post, and in time five. The first time she climbed the wall in a raid he carried her down; after that he only looked. After her first kill he held out the chalk so she could make her own stroke.

entries.name: the third-year teacher

facts.t: The teacher waits at the classroom door with folded arms when Layla and Fanny arrive late.
Fanny asked the teacher what to bring to detention.
The teacher of the third-year class tells Selena she is late again.
The teacher checks a tablet, sighs, and finds Selena's late note there.
The teacher goes on with the lesson while Selena sleeps.
The teacher has not written anything on the board yet when the paper plane flies.
At the screen the teacher goes down a table of this year's suits.
The teacher asks Selena to read out the top row.

rel.t: Layla's class teacher.
Fanny's class teacher.
Selena is in this class.

entries.line: The class teacher of Layla, Fanny and Selena.
entries.short: Layla and Fanny's class teacher, who waits at the door with folded arms when they arrive late.
entries.summary: The teacher of the third-year class, which holds Layla, Fanny and Selena. The teacher waits at the door with folded arms when Layla and Fanny run in late, and tells Selena she is late again, then finds her late note on a tablet, sighs and lets her sleep through the lesson. In the last weeks the teacher goes down a table of this year's suits on the screen and asks Selena to read out the top row.

entries.name: the truck driver

facts.t: He drives Lesley back toward Terrinia and expects to be home by one.
He brakes hard on the last hill when he sees the city's edge burning.

rel.t: He drives a Shield truck.

entries.line: The Shield driver who brings Lesley back toward Terrinia.
entries.short: A Shield truck driver taking Lesley back toward Terrinia. He expects to be home by one.
entries.summary: A Shield driver who carries Lesley back toward Terrinia at the end of her secret mission. He calls back through the cab window that they will be home by one. Past midnight, on the last hill, he brakes hard: the city's edge is burning.

entries.name: the warden

facts.t: The warden hauls at one of the seawall shelter's iron doors, ready to shut it.
The warden shouts at Chang'e to get in.

rel.t: Keeps its doors.

entries.line: The warden of the seawall shelter's iron doors.
entries.short: The warden of the seawall shelter, hauling at one of its iron doors, ready to shut it as the Enders come.
entries.summary: The warden who keeps the iron doors of the seawall shelter. As the Enders come down the avenue, the warden hauls at one door, ready to shut it, and shouts at Chang'e to get in. She stays outside and takes her place in front of the doors instead, and they bang shut behind her.

entries.name: the waterfront merchant

facts.t: He pays Selena for one word.
She tells him tomorrow.
He moves his stock out of his warehouse that afternoon. The next night its roof comes in.

rel.t: His warehouse is on the waterfront.

entries.line: A waterfront merchant who pays Selena for a warning.
entries.short: A merchant on the waterfront who pays Selena for one word: when.
entries.summary: A merchant whose warehouse stands on the waterfront. Selena can feel the Enders' hum gather in her bones a day before a raid, and he pays her for one word. She tells him: tomorrow. He moves his stock out that afternoon, and the next night the warehouse roof comes in.

entries.name: the woman downstairs

facts.t: When the sirens come close, Selena is to go down with her.
Selena copies the smile she wears for the landlord.
She calls Selena a talent for mending radios.
In the raid she leads Selena by the hand toward the shelter, and her hand lets go when the line breaks.

entries.line: Karina's downstairs neighbor, who minds Selena in raids.
entries.short: The woman downstairs from Karina's flat. When the sirens come close, Selena is to go down with her.
entries.summary: Karina's neighbor in the flat downstairs. When the sirens come close, Selena is to go down with her, and Selena copies the smile she wears for the landlord. She calls Selena a talent for mending radios. One rainy night in a raid she leads Selena by the hand toward the shelter, and when the line breaks, her hand lets go.

entries.name: the workshop man

facts.t: He paid Selena for four plates and walked off with five.
The next week she charged him for five when he bought four.
He paid, and every workshop on his street heard about the fifth plate.

entries.line: A workshop man who cheats Selena once.
entries.short: A man from the outskirts' workshops who pays Selena for four plates and walks off with five.
entries.summary: A buyer from the workshops on the outskirts. He pays Selena for four salvage plates and walks off with five. The next week he wants four more, and she counts them out and holds out her hand for the price of five. "Miscounted," she says. He pays, and every workshop on his street hears about the fifth plate.

entries.name: the youngest soldier

facts.t: He stands the dawn watch beside Lesley, counting out loud the days to his leave.
He asks her why she never talks.
He asks her to play cards, and she goes back to the rifles.
He slips at the foot of the ladder and an Ender turns to him.
Lesley's shot kills the Ender and its arm strikes the mud beside him.
With twelve days left before he goes, he asks her again for one game.

rel.t: He serves at the station.
She shoots the Ender that turns on him.

entries.line: The youngest Shield soldier at the station, counting the days to his leave.
entries.short: The youngest soldier at the station. He stands the dawn watch beside Lesley, counting out loud the days to his leave.
entries.summary: The youngest soldier at the Shield station, who stands the dawn watch beside Lesley and counts out loud the days to his leave. He asks her why she never talks and asks her to play cards, and she goes back to the rifles. When he slips at the foot of the ladder and an Ender turns to him, Lesley's shot kills it and its arm strikes the mud beside him. With twelve days left before he goes, he asks her again for one game.

entries.name: Tigreal

facts.t: He is Fanny's elder brother, an incredible fighter she respects above anyone else.
Since she was a child, Fanny has longed to join him on the battlefield.
Fanny feels she could never quite reach his level.
Fanny says her brother would have held the street alone.
Fanny says she does not care what Tigreal would have done.

rel.t: Tigreal is her elder brother.
He belongs to Fanny's family.
Tigreal is her brother.

entries.line: Fanny's elder brother, a fighter she looks up to.
entries.short: Fanny's elder brother, an incredible fighter she respects above anyone else. She has longed to fight beside him since she was a child.
entries.summary: Tigreal is Fanny's elder brother, an incredible fighter she respects above anyone else. Since she was a child she has longed to join him on the battlefield, and she feels she could never quite reach his level. During the battle Fanny says her brother would have held the street alone, and then that she does not care what Tigreal would have done.

entries.name: Vexana

facts.t: She is on the courtyard billboard: a girl with long black hair, named VEXANA, back to back with Guinevere.
She stands next to Guinevere and catches Fanny staring.
She tells Fanny that if you ask Guinevere how she trains, she will talk for an hour.
At the breach she and Guinevere hang in the air with wings spread, drones circling them in step.
She hangs above Guinevere with a staff.
Her magic hits whatever reaches for Guinevere's back first. Neither of them looks around to check.
Joe says she and Guinevere are undefeated, and they cannot explain why either.
At the newcomers' arrival she stands beside Guinevere with her staff.
She is on the Combat Division's first intake list.
She waits by the hall door in school uniform with folded arms, a chibi keychain of a pink-haired Guinevere at her belt.
She lets Guinevere tow her out by the sleeve.
She has black hair, violet eyes and a small mole beside her mouth.
She gives Layla her name only in case it is needed.
She and Layla have shared classes for two years without either speaking first.
She follows Guinevere into the portal without a word.
She keeps to the roof below Guinevere, where she sees the tear and the street, and her staff finishes whatever Guinevere knocks down.
Her bolt frees Guinevere's boot from a claw.
When Guinevere's wings fail, she lies flat on the tiles and catches her by the wrist.
She counts under her breath while Guinevere recovers, and says "Four."
Her hand shakes afterward, and she grips her staff until it stops.
She saw Guinevere tiring a minute before and said nothing.
On an earlier raid she told Guinevere to come down and rest, and Guinevere flew higher; so now she waits at the roof's edge instead.
For the rest of the raid she stands a step nearer and fires over Guinevere's shoulder.
She picks up Guinevere's broken drone and takes it back through the portal ahead of the others, saying nothing.
She phones Guinevere at the usual hour to tell her to go to bed, and hangs up.
On the morning of the entrance assessment a black-haired girl with a cloth bag goes past Guinevere at the gate, eyes front.
Every night on the phone she tells Guinevere "Good."
Her room at the Academy is nearly bare: a tin of oil, a jar of spare screws, two tactics books stacked square and her father's old toolbox. Guinevere has never been inside; Vexana always goes to her.
Her mother died of an illness before Vexana could remember her, so she grew up alone with her father.
As a child she lived with her father in a row of Shield houses in the shadow of the city wall.
As a child she learned to hand her father the right tool without being told which.
During a real Ender attack she slipped out of the shelter to find her father, because she only wanted to be with him.
When an Ender raised its claw at her in the street, her feet would not move.
A soldier carried her away over his shoulder while her father stood against the Ender, and she watched the smoke close over him.
After her father died she was sent to the Shield's home for soldiers' children with one bag.
She blames herself for his death: she did not stay back, he came back for her, and she thinks it should have been her.
After his death she kept every rule, and nobody at the home ever had to tell her anything twice.
She refused a friendly girl's ribbon, believing that people who stand near you die for you, so nobody should stand near her.
She trained alone at dawn with a wooden drill pole, telling herself she owed her father and would pay it back in Enders.
Lesley found her at the home and told her to come to the Academy's first intake.
When she first saw Guinevere at the Academy gate she thought of her as a lamp, someone so bright she had never been in the dark.
At the entrance assessment her needle passed the line, and she told Lesley she came "To destroy the Enders."
During a real siren in the shelter she sat alone on the bench by the door, hands flat on her knees, eyes on the door.
Through the preparatory year she trained every night in the training hall gallery without a sound, ate alone and answered in one word.
She wears white gloves; under them her palms are ridged and hard from the drill pole.
On the night Guinevere bled on the heavy bag, she came down from the gallery and left a roll of cloth tape on Guinevere's jacket.
She has black hair and violet eyes with a hard light far back in them.
On Team-Up Day she told Guinevere "You are strong, Guinevere," though she had never said her name aloud before.
She refused to be Guinevere's partner because she liked her and could not bear to watch someone die for her again.
In the raid at the dome's foot she followed Guinevere a street back, and her arrow came one breath too late to stop the claw.
After fighting back to back with Guinevere, she broke her own rule and decided: "I like her. That's why it has to be yes."
She follows a written plan exactly; when Guinevere says she can do more than fifty, she answers "It says fifty."
Whenever the training hall stays lit late, she phones Guinevere and tells her to go to bed.
She will not talk about who taught her to mend things or about her family.
In the team test, kneeling to mend her staff, she saw Guinevere standing where her father had stood, and made her hands keep working.
She had never spent any of her Academy stipend; it lay in the bottom tray of the toolbox, still in its paper bands.
She thinks of every gift as a debt, and fears owing Guinevere as she owes her father a life.
She returned all of Guinevere's gifts and told her "I am not something you buy."
Nobody had ever made her anything before Guinevere made the Emblems of Hope.
Each night she puts her star and the pink keychain in the white box, and each morning she puts them back on.
On the night of the fireworks she let herself smile without pressing it flat.
On the day of the tree she told Guinevere "My father liked the stars," the first time she spoke of him.
Before the day of the tree she had never seen her own face smile.
Afraid Guinevere would be first through any way into the void, she resolved to find it first, and read Chang'e's paper alone in the library.
She found Guinevere's lost drone in a gutter, mended it and set it on Guinevere's charger at night without being heard.
She knows Chang'e's paper by heart and believes two Aspirants would shine brighter than one.
She fights back to back with Guinevere in the fifth raid in nine days, and counts the raids from the siren on the dormitory roof.
She thinks the Enders go for the strongest, and sees more of them turn toward Guinevere than toward anyone.
Since the fish market she keeps a step nearer Guinevere's back.
She steps into a claw meant for Guinevere's open left side; it tears her left glove and cuts her arm, and she fires her orb into the Ender's bare core.
She has dressed her own cuts since she was small, and hides the bandage under a spare pair of gloves and her sleeve.
She thinks her father came back for her and paid for it, and that this debt she pays herself.
She does fifty forms every morning.
Guinevere hears her laugh for the first time after their drawn match: short and rusty.
She kept Guinevere's own words: "Rules are for keeping safe what matters."
Every morning since the ceremony she has set Guinevere's slipping left bow straight before the run.
Since the summer she has sewn two felt dolls, a pink-haired Guinevere and a black-haired Vexana, to give at the fireworks.
When the training hall stays lit late she phones Guinevere and tells her "Go to bed."
She always shuts doors. On the morning of the watch she runs out with her staff and the pink-haired keychain at her belt.
In the Investigation Room corridor she shoves Guinevere clear of a claw coming out of a door in the wall, and the claw closes on her hand instead.
As the claw drags her toward the dark she thinks it is all right, as long as Guinevere is safe.
She shouts "Stay back!" at Guinevere as the door pulls her in.
She has violet eyes and a small mole by her mouth.
In the void the Ender drags her a long way and then lets go; she thinks it was sent to take her, not to kill her.
As a child she slipped out of the shelter by the wall to find her father, because she was afraid to be alone, and an Ender found her first.
Her father's last words to her were "Stay back," said as he stood between her and the Ender.
Since the shelter she has felt she owed a life; after saving Guinevere she thinks it is paid.
She folds her wings and lets herself fall through the void, until the Emblem of Hope warms at her collar.
In her memory under the tree she pats Guinevere's hair for the first time, still learning how hard.
She fires at the Will of the Planet; the shot vanishes into its face and not one plate moves.
She asks the Will whether this is the only way to protect Guinevere. It does not answer.
One wish has sat under everything she does since her father died: that it had been her instead.
She decides to take the Will's orders, walk among its Enders as one of them, and keep close to its body.
She plans to pour all her aspirant power into the Mother Matrix's open core when it opens its chest to fire, knowing it would end her too.
She thinks she cannot stop it from the Academy's side, but might from the Enders' side.
Offered a door home onto the dead ground, she steps back and returns to the void.
In the void purple-black armor cut like an Ender's shell closes over her clothes, with a purple cloak, horns and star-shaped blades.
She moves the Emblem from her collar to the inside of her right sleeve, against her wrist, and hides it there.
Her hair, black all her life, turns blue-lavender, darkening to magenta at the ends.
The void slows her body: she is rarely hungry and sleeps little, curled beside her folded uniform.
In the hollow she trains: violet wings, the great arrow that comes down from above at her call, charged shots and the black orb.
She pays Selena for Ender plating in places: where wreckage lies, before the crews find it.
She stays away so that the star is the one true thing Guinevere gets from her.
She builds a machine from Ender plates in the hollow, beating their edges with a hammer until they catch.
As a child she handed her father tools in a gun pit on the city wall without being told which.
She does not mean to come back down from the Mother Matrix.
A door brings her back from the dome's edge at gray dawn, and she goes to the hollow.
She wears a star at her right wrist under her sleeve. It is always lit, and she still checks it.
The cold point behind her breastbone orders her to the body: "The body. Now."
The Will had never sent her near its body before, and she fears it knows about the star.
She leaves her four Guards dark so the Will will not see them.
Seeing the body's face, she thinks it is the Mother Matrix and that Chang'e's readings were right.
She studies the body's chest seam the way she studies an Ender's chest before it fires.
When Obsidia looks at her wrist, her power gathers in her staff on its own and the black orb hums.
She fears that if she dies, Guinevere's star goes dark and Guinevere will believe she is dead, as the Academy does.
She tells Obsidia only the end the vision showed her: "The will of the stars has spoken: this world will one day meet its end."
She tells Obsidia she hears orders, and says: "Enders die. We see to it."
She works out that the Will sees only what its Enders see, so to it she is a girl in its shape doing as she is told.
She reasons that if a made thing can turn on its maker, then "predetermined" is only a word.
She never gave Obsidia her name, yet Obsidia knows it.
She stays under the body, looks up at the long seam with its magenta glow, and thinks: There.
She goes to the Storm Citadel between errands on her own, with no order, hoping its commander knows where the Core is.
Under the human sky she once sat by a shady tree with Guinevere's head in her lap.
She remembers her father on the wall before dawn, oiling the guns so the street behind him could sleep, and one lit window across the city long past midnight.
She thinks the crack opened after their win at the breach, and blames herself: "We did that. I did."
Her legs once gave out halfway up the wall stair at home, and her father carried her the rest of the way.
She decides the Will does not hate humans, so it cannot be begged, and so it has to be broken.
Twice she has gone to the rows to search, keeping to their edge. She has found no Core.
She sees the body and the Storm Citadel as her two enemies.
She recognizes the scorched suit on the prow and thinks she let the feeders take it.
She plans to strike when the body comes through the gate whole and close.
With the Core not found, she plans to strike the body's chest alone when it opens to fire, expecting nothing of her to be left after.
She tells Obsidia: "As long as the Aspirant voice echoes, I will resist the darkness."
She had said the word Aspirant in the dark before, alone, but never to anyone.
She knows she has just told the Will's commander which side she is on.
In the hollow she always bares the star at her wrist.
She carried home every plate of her four Guards in a sack and beat every joint until it caught.
On errand nights she eats a little from tins in dead kitchens. In the void she is hardly ever hungry.
She keeps a step behind Obsidia among the rows so that she looks like an instrument at its commander's heel.
Her father's toolbox, set beside her cot in the Shield's home, was all of him that came back to her.
She tells Obsidia that someone once told her they would be like fireworks, shining at their brightest.
She thinks that for her it will be fireworks, then dark, but not for the one who said it.
Her left hand goes to the pin under her right sleeve when Obsidia speaks of a pawn's termination. She takes it away.
Seen by Selena after she went missing: her black hair has turned blue-lavender with magenta tips, real horns rise from it, and she wears an Ender's robe and carries a staff with a black orb.
She waited in the dark for the big man to leave before stepping into Selena's lamp. Selena thinks an Ender would not have waited.
When Selena tells her that her partner does not think she is dead, her face does not move, and her left hand goes halfway to her right sleeve.
In the capture the Will reached through a door in an Academy corridor for the girl with her back to it, the other girl stepped in front of her, and Vexana was the one taken.
In the vision the Will told her: "Vexana of The Aspirants, you have reached the end of your future."
The Will went through her memories: fireworks at the edge of a dome, a tree with a head in her lap, a girl with pink hair laughing.
In all her weeks with the Enders, no human saw her face. Obsidia thinks the Will was saving it.
She came home through the Will's doors carrying Ender plate and cracked cores.
She keeps her star pinned inside her sleeve and stays at the edge of the rows, believing the Will sees only what its Enders see.
She wakes in the void curled beside her folded school uniform, with her four Guards standing dark over her.
Seeing the body move toward the crack, she says "The end is drawing near."
She leaves her uniform folded, because in the vision she wore it and Guinevere fell anyway.
A cold point under her breastbone stirs when the Will gives her an order.
She hopes Guinevere will be the one to clear her room, read the card, and go next year anyway, not alone.
Her plan is to go in front of the Mother Matrix inside her lead Guard and pour all her power into its chest when it opens to fire.
She has known what the plan will cost since she knelt before the Will, and has never changed her mind.
She tells the rain, "If night is fated to swallow day, I will vanish before the dawn."
She tells the lit window of the lab, "I will become the sun that lights the dark night, and protect her."
The Will's orders come to her as a voice inside her: a place and a time, never a why.
The Enders move with her as if she led them. That is the Will's mark on her.
For weeks she watched from the ruined tower beyond the beep's reach. On the day of the attack she took the nearest roof, knowing what her star would do.
Seeing Guinevere cry and smile below, she says very low, "Betray her... But to protect her..."
She wants Guinevere to come alone and early, so she can be put down first, hurt and out of the fight, but alive.
She wears heeled boots, white stockings and a long robe, and moves slowly, as if she owns the place.
Her hair is now blue-lavender fading to magenta at the ends. She has violet eyes and a small mole beside her mouth.
She tells Guinevere in a low, flat voice, "You haven't changed at all."
She screams "Enough!" as Guinevere calls up to her, then comes down to face her with an army at her back.
She tells Guinevere, "Give up, Guinevere. Hope is an illusion. Its 'Will' is absolute."
The beam that broke over her Guard burned her left arm raw to the elbow.
She walks into the middle of the road so every Ender sees her and follows her away from Guinevere.
She says to nobody, "The pain, the hate, I will bear it all."
She realizes the Will never needed her loyal, only used.
She gathers the last of her power to strike the open chest, for humanity and for Guinevere.
In the fight over the gap she turned her staff aside at the last meter, with every Ender watching.
To save Guinevere she forced a door of the void open herself for the first time, and something tore.
She tells Guinevere, "Go. I've seen the end that awaits us. There is no other choice..."
She had meant to leave everything behind and never tell Guinevere why.
She takes Guinevere's hand with her burned hand. It hurts, and she does not let go.
She says, "You pulled me out of the dark once."
She cries "Hope never dies!" though not long before she had told Guinevere hope was an illusion.
She says "This is the final farewell," and means it.
Caught by the black hole after the strike, she says "Plan B" without being asked.
The dark takes her and Guinevere both.
Inside the black hole her fingers come away in flecks of pale light, and her burned arm goes first.
She remembers that Chang'e's paper said the body goes first.
The star under her right sleeve is the only warm thing on her, and it keeps growing colder.
She tells Guinevere that she brought color to her world, and that before they met her world was darker than the void.
She says her ignorance and foolishness led to her father's death: he was a soldier to the end and died saving her.
Under the tree she had told Guinevere only that her father liked the stars.
She says her father told her to stay back at the shelter door; she did not, so he came back for her. She says she shouted the same words, 'Stay back!', at Guinevere in the corridor.
She says that after his death atonement and destroying the Enders became her only purpose, and she chose to be alone for fear of losing someone again.
She says Guinevere saw her hiding in the shadows, reached out without hesitation and chose to be her partner.
She says Guinevere took her to the summer fireworks, the girls' house and the amusement park.
She says she kept everything from those days in a box: ticket stubs, a paper fan, even the napkin from a doughnut.
She says she wore the pink-haired keychain into the corridor instead of keeping it in the box.
She calls the Emblem of Hope Guinevere gave her her most treasured possession.
She says the Will of the Planet showed her a 'future' that Guinevere must never know.
She asks Guinevere's forgiveness and says she would again choose to betray her in order to protect her.
Warmth comes through the star at her wrist and her body stops fading.
She had read the page of Chang'e's paper about the black hole twice in the library.
When her body begins to recover she thinks of Plan B.
She laughs in the dark when Guinevere says she once phoned in the middle of the night to tell her to go to bed.
Meeting Guinevere again in the light she says, 'Beneath the shooting star, we have met again, Guinevere.'
Before the strike on the Matrix her voice came over Guinevere's open line: 'This is the final farewell.'
She returns with her left sleeve gone to the elbow; the arm under it, burned raw before the charge, is whole again.
She flies down to three dark giants in the rubble and lights their eyes with her palm without saying a word.
She tells Fanny the giants are hers and answer to her.
She has no comm of her own, so Guinevere gives her hers.
When Lesley puts her on the frontline she grounds her staff, brings her heels together and answers 'Understood, Commander.'
She reaches over and sets Guinevere's left bow straight.
She tells Guinevere quietly that she saw the end and no longer knows if it was the only one.
She flies on violet wings beside Guinevere and sends her three giants into the road.
She recognizes the field's hum and orders everyone to land at once, without explaining why.
When the field reaches her, her violet wings fold into nothing and she drops onto the road on her feet.
Selena sees her kneel over Guinevere in an Ender's robe, blue-lavender hair down her back.
Under the field the orb of her staff gives no light.
She gets between an Ender and Guinevere with her dark staff and is knocked into a doorway.
Weeks among the Enders taught her how they move; she holds her staff across her body like a pole and reads which one will swing.
With both stars dark, her fingers still find Guinevere's wrist between Enders.
When her star lights again, violet wings open at her back.
She had once walked the Storm Citadel's hanging streets.
She says the portal is torn, not closed.
She had not planned on a next year, yet a card on her desk still says 'Same place. Next year.' in her small square letters.

weapons.name: The practice staff

weapons.name: The brass collar

weapons.name: White gloves

weapons.name: The wooden drill pole

weapons.name: Toolbox
weapons.note: Her father's old soldier's toolbox, smelling of gun oil, with his small screwdriver inside. A soldier brought it to her at the home. She carries it everywhere in a cloth bag.

weapons.name: Chibi keychain
weapons.note: A little doll keychain of pink-haired Guinevere at her belt. Guinevere wears its twin.

weapons.name: Emblems of Hope
weapons.note: The gold star Guinevere made for her and pinned at her collar, one seam a hair crooked. It glows when their powers are in sync and beeps when the two come near after being apart.

weapons.name: The white box
weapons.note: A cake box where she keeps her summer keepsakes: ticket stubs, a paper fan, even the napkin from a doughnut. Each night her star and keychain go in it too.

weapons.name: Vexana's Ender armor
weapons.note: Purple-black plates cut like an Ender's shell, a purple cloak, two horns and star blades at her shoulders. It closed over her in the void; her hair turned blue-lavender and her staff's orb black.

weapons.name: Hammer
weapons.note: She beat the edges of Ender plates with it until they caught, to build her machines in the void.

weapons.name: Eternal Guards
weapons.note: Four machines she built from Ender plate and cracked cores, to stand over Guinevere when she could not. They run on her power and wake under her palm. Three giants carry swords longer than a house.

weapons.name: Lead Guard
weapons.note: The first Guard: purple plate edged in gold, yellow eyes and a magenta heart on its chest. Behind the heart is room for her, and inside it she sees through its eyes.
