entries.name: checks

facts.t: Chang'e checks Angela the way she checks a machine: joint torque, sensor reach, cooling.
Chang'e rules that anything that can receive can be told what to do, so Angela stays on checks.
What Chang'e cannot open goes on her list.
She writes WEEKLY beside the safeguard's lock.
Chang'e admits keeping Angela on checks is the same as Lesley keeping her off the rotation.

entries.line: The Science Division's regular checks on Angela.
entries.short: Chang'e's inspections of Angela. Anything that can receive can be told what to do, so Angela stays on checks.
entries.summary: The checks the Science Division keeps Angela on. Chang'e checks her the way she checks a machine: joint torque, sensor reach, cooling. She rules that anything that can receive can be told what to do, so Angela stays on checks, and what Chang'e cannot open goes on her list; beside the lock of Ruby's safeguard she writes WEEKLY. Later she admits it is the same as Lesley keeping her off the rotation.

entries.name: Chief Combat Instructor

facts.t: Lesley's title at Selrick.
The narration names Lesley the Chief Combat Instructor.
Lesley becomes the Academy's Chief Combat Instructor, head of its Combat Division.

rel.t: It is Lesley's title.

entries.line: Lesley's title: head of the Academy's combat training.
entries.short: Lesley's title at Selrick Academy. The Chief Combat Instructor is head of all combat training.
entries.summary: The Chief Combat Instructor is head of all combat training at Selrick Academy and of its Combat Division. Lesley took the title when the Academy began, and she holds it still.

entries.name: Chief Scientist

facts.t: Chang'e is the youngest Chief Scientist in Terrinia.
Terrinia's research base had two chief scientists.
The base's two chief scientists brought Chang'e there and raised her.
The city's scientists make Chang'e Chief Scientist, the youngest Terrinia has ever had.
It had been her parents' title; the old door plate said CHIEF SCIENTISTS, and the new one drops the last S.

rel.t: It is Chang'e's title.

entries.line: Chang'e's title, the youngest in Terrinia to hold it.
entries.short: Chang'e's title. She is the youngest Chief Scientist in Terrinia.
entries.summary: Terrinia's research base had two chief scientists: Chang'e's parents, who brought her there and raised her. The old door plate said CHIEF SCIENTISTS. After the fall the city's scientists made Chang'e Chief Scientist, the youngest Terrinia has ever had, and the new plate dropped the last S.

entries.name: cleansing

facts.t: All three of Oro's powers vote that Dawnbreak will be cleansed.
In the Council's words, cleansed means nobody on Dawnbreak would be left outside Balance.
Ruby explains it as removing everyone who will not live by the Council's Balance.

rel.t: The Council voted to cleanse Dawnbreak.
It comes after the cleansing.
Ruby calls the androids the start of the Council's plan.

entries.line: Oro's Council word for leaving no one outside Balance.
entries.short: The Council's word for a planet's fate. Cleansed means nobody on it is left outside Balance.
entries.summary: Cleansing is a word of Oro's Council. All three of Oro's powers voted that Dawnbreak would be cleansed: nobody on it would be left outside Balance. Ruby says it plainly: it means removing everyone who will not live by the Council's Balance. After the cleansing, Oro would annex the planet.

entries.name: Code Override

facts.t: Code Override rewrites a machine's orders. Green lines run from Ruby's glove and land on their target.
On Angela's plate the lines reach the Council's seal and stop, and the air says DENIED in red.
While the control unit drives Angela, its orders outrank anything Ruby writes.
In the cell Ruby says her code cannot reach the lock, because nothing gets a signal out.
With her hand on Angela's shoulder, green lines run down Angela's arm into the lock, and it clicks open.
Ruby's code opens the launch bay doors.

rel.t: It is Ruby's power, used from her glove.

entries.line: Ruby's power to rewrite a machine's orders.
entries.short: Ruby's power. Green lines run from her glove onto a machine and rewrite its orders.
entries.summary: Code Override rewrites a machine's orders. Green lines run from Ruby's glove and land on their target. On Angela's plate the lines reached the Council's seal and stopped, and the air said DENIED in red: while the control unit drove Angela, its orders outranked anything Ruby wrote. In the cell nothing got a signal out, until Ruby laid her hand on Angela's shoulder and the lines ran down Angela's arm into the lock, which clicked open. Her code also opened the launch bay doors.

entries.name: curfew

facts.t: After the curfew bell nobody goes out of the Academy grounds, and the summer fireworks start after it.
Vexana warns they will be caught if they break it.

entries.line: The Academy rule that keeps everyone inside after the bell.
entries.short: After the curfew bell, nobody goes out of the Academy grounds.
entries.summary: After the curfew bell, nobody goes out of the Academy grounds, and the summer fireworks only start after it. Vexana keeps every rule, so when Guinevere asks her out to see the fireworks, she warns they will be caught. Guinevere answers that rules are for keeping safe what matters, not for locking you up.

entries.name: debts

facts.t: After her father's death Vexana thinks she owes him and will pay it back in Enders.
She thinks a coat is a debt, and so is everything anyone gives you.
She thinks she owes her father a life, and cannot owe Guinevere too.
She decides the felt is no debt, since it is for someone else.
She keeps ticket stubs, a fan and a napkin because nobody could call those debts.

entries.line: What Vexana believes she owes, and must pay back.
entries.short: Vexana's belief that every gift is a debt. She thinks she owes her father a life, and pays it back in Enders.
entries.summary: Vexana thinks everything anyone gives you is a debt, even a coat. After her father's death she decided she owed him a life and would pay it back in Enders, so she cannot owe Guinevere too. Felt meant for someone else is no debt. She keeps ticket stubs, a fan and a napkin, because nobody could call those debts.

entries.name: Destruction

facts.t: Obsidia says destruction is hers to command.
Obsidia tells Selena she does not understand the true power of Destruction.
Obsidia had always stood above destruction.
Obsidia says destruction and faith share the same origin.

entries.line: Obsidia's word for the power she commands.
entries.short: Obsidia's creed. She says destruction is hers to command.
entries.summary: Obsidia says destruction is hers to command, and she has always stood above it. She tells Selena that she does not understand the true power of Destruction. Destruction and faith, Obsidia says, share the same origin.

entries.name: detention

facts.t: Students caught skipping class can be kept in detention all day.
Detention is cleaning the Academy hall.
It is Fanny's first.
Angela comes though nobody sentenced her.
The bell ends it.

entries.line: The Academy's punishment for students who skip class.
entries.short: The punishment for skipping class: cleaning the Academy hall, sometimes all day.
entries.summary: Students caught skipping class can be kept in detention all day. Detention means cleaning the Academy hall. It is Fanny's first. Angela comes too, though nobody sentenced her, and the bell ends it.

entries.name: drills

facts.t: The wall houses held drills; at the drill bell soldiers went to their guns and families to the shelter.
To young Vexana drills were a game in which nothing bad ever happened.
One evening the bell rang and it was not a drill.
The Shield's home held drills too, but nobody came to find her after.

entries.line: Practice alarms at the Shield's wall houses.
entries.short: Practice alarms at the wall houses. At the drill bell soldiers go to their guns and families to the shelter.
entries.summary: The Shield's houses by the city wall held drills. At the drill bell Vexana's father went up to his gun, she ran to the shelter, and when the all-clear sounded he came to find her. To young Vexana it was a game in which nothing bad ever happened, until one evening the bell rang and it was not a drill. At the Shield's home she kept still through every drill, but nobody came to find her after.

entries.name: electromagnetic interference

facts.t: Wherever the Storm Citadel's violet storm reaches, human machines die.
After the Citadel climbs away, the street lamps flicker back on.
The recording's caption says the Storm Citadel can unleash devastating electromagnetic interference over large areas.
Interference means every machine under its storm dies.

rel.t: It unleashes interference over large areas.
It is the Storm Citadel's weapon.

entries.line: The Storm Citadel's power that kills machines under its storm.
entries.short: The Storm Citadel's weapon. Every machine under its storm dies.
entries.summary: Electromagnetic interference is the Storm Citadel's weapon. Wherever its violet storm reaches, human machines die, and when the Citadel climbs away, the street lamps flicker back on. The Academy's oldest film says it can unleash it over large areas. A suit's core lit by belief runs on no current, so the storm cannot touch it.

entries.name: Ender ranks

facts.t: Joe teaches three ranks: Ultimate Enders, the deadliest, which release the other two; then Super Enders; then plain Enders.
Joe says the small ones kill the most, because there are the most.
None of Joe's three ranks had been gold.
Layla runs through the three ranks when the gold giant appears, and remembers that the siren said Ultra.

rel.t: Joe sorts them into three ranks.
The middle of Joe's three ranks.
The highest of Joe's three ranks.

entries.line: Joe's three ranks of Enders, from plain to deadliest.
entries.short: Joe's three ranks: Ultimate Enders, the deadliest, which release the others; then Super Enders; then plain Enders, which kill the most.
entries.summary: Joe teaches three ranks of Enders. Ultimate Enders are the deadliest and release the other two. Then come Super Enders, then plain Enders. The small ones kill the most, because there are the most. None of the three ranks was gold. When a gold giant broke the dome, Layla went through them anyway and remembered the siren had said Ultra.

entries.name: Ender signal

facts.t: Academy screens read a signal off every Ender near the dome, shown as rows of jagged lines.
Chang'e says the signals all stopping at once shows something switches the Enders off.

entries.line: The jagged readings Academy screens take off every Ender near the dome.
entries.short: A reading Academy screens take off every Ender near the dome, shown as rows of jagged lines. When a lull begins, they all stop at once.
entries.summary: Academy screens read a signal off every Ender near the dome and show it as rows of jagged lines. When a lull begins, every signal stops in the same moment. Chang'e says this shows that something switches all the Enders off at once. Selena knows the screens too: a signal sent up through Ender parts would spike on them in clear weather, so she sends hers only in storms, when the lightning buries it.

entries.name: errands

facts.t: Obsidia tells Vexana to go back to her errands.
Vexana goes to the Citadel between errands, with no order.
On errand nights Vexana eats from tins in dead kitchens.

rel.t: The Will sends her on them.

entries.line: The tasks the Will sends Vexana on in the dark.
entries.short: The tasks the Will of the Planet gives Vexana in the dark. Its orders come from a cold point under her breastbone.
entries.summary: The tasks the Will sends Vexana on while she lives in the dark. Each order comes out of a cold point under her breastbone, such as the rail yards north of the dome at dusk. On errand nights she eats from tins in dead kitchens. When Obsidia meets her under the body, she tells Vexana to go back to her errands. Later Vexana goes to the Storm Citadel between errands, on her own, with no order.

entries.name: fine tuning

facts.t: The gray-haired professor says Silverbolt is fine tuned to one pilot, and that the director's gear is the same.

entries.line: How a machine is tuned to answer one pilot only.
entries.short: A machine tuned to one pilot answers no one else. Silverbolt is fine tuned, and so is the director's gear.
entries.summary: Some machines are fine tuned: made to answer one pilot only. When Chang'e climbs onto Silverbolt and tells it to walk, not even its tail twitches. The gray-haired professor explains that Silverbolt is fine tuned to one pilot, and that the director's gear is the same.

entries.name: First Aspirants

facts.t: Later the Academy calls Lesley and Chang'e the First Aspirants.

entries.line: The title the Academy later gives Lesley and Chang'e.
entries.short: The name the Academy later gives Lesley and Chang'e, after the night the two of them bring down three giant Enders over Terrinia.
entries.summary: An honorary title. Years after the research base fell, Lesley and Chang'e fought side by side in Terrinia. They brought down a giant Ender over the avenue, and before dawn two more of the big ones. Later the Academy called the two of them the First Aspirants.

entries.name: free will

facts.t: Obsidia says the body made the Enders and mends her by one rule: free will is a flaw that must be corrected.
Obsidia says she is the flaw.
Vexana thinks that if a made thing can turn on its maker, "predetermined" is only a word.

entries.line: What the Enders' maker treats as a flaw to be corrected.
entries.short: Obsidia says the body made the Enders and mends her by one rule: free will is a flaw that must be corrected. She calls herself the flaw.
entries.summary: Obsidia says the body made the Enders, and mends her by one rule: free will is a flaw that must be corrected. Each healing sets a made thing back to what it was made for, so she stops it before it is done. "I am the flaw," she says. Vexana watches her stop her maker with one hand, and thinks that if a made thing can turn on its maker, "predetermined" is only a word.

entries.name: Go to bed

facts.t: What Vexana says when she phones Guinevere because the training hall is still lit late.
Vexana says the late call counts as an emergency.
Guinevere stops pretending to be asleep and bargains for more punches.
Vexana phones even when the hall is dark.
Vexana plans to phone Guinevere later and tell her to go to bed.

entries.line: What Vexana says when she phones Guinevere late at night.
entries.short: What Vexana says when she phones Guinevere at two in the morning, because the training hall is still lit.
entries.summary: In their first weeks as partners, Vexana phones Guinevere at two in the morning because the training hall is still lit, and says only "Go to bed." The number was for emergencies. Vexana says it was one. After that she phones whenever the hall stays lit late, and Guinevere stops pretending to be asleep and bargains for ten more. One night the hall is dark, and Vexana phones anyway.

entries.name: heir to the Decisionmaker
aka: heir to the Decisionmaker of Planet Oro

facts.t: Ruby is the heir to the Decisionmaker of Planet Oro. Heirs can have no friends and no feelings.
Her tutor addresses her as "Heir."
The rule that nobody on Oro may grow strong enough to upset the order includes the heir.
Heirs can have no feelings, but Ruby's tears run anyway.
The Council's order says the heir will build the new blade.
Heirs cannot have friends, so Ruby freezes when Angela calls her one.
Ruby's lock means Oro would have to send for the heir.
Oro's soldiers address Ruby as 'Heir'.
The treason charge names Ruby heir to the Decisionmaker.
Ruby introduces herself as heir to the Decisionmaker of Planet Oro.

rows: Her father, who leads Oro's Decisionmakers

rel.t: It is Ruby's title.

entries.line: Ruby's title on Planet Oro: heir to the Decisionmaker.
entries.short: Ruby's title: heir to the Decisionmaker of Planet Oro. Heirs can have no friends and no feelings.
entries.summary: Ruby is the heir to the Decisionmaker of Planet Oro, and has been told since before she could read that heirs can have no friends and no feelings. Her tutor and Oro's soldiers call her "Heir," and Oro's rule that nobody may grow strong enough to upset the order includes her. The Council orders the heir to build its new blade, and when Angela calls her a friend, she freezes. Charged with treason, she still names herself heir when she asks Selrick for refuge.

entries.name: Hester's count

facts.t: Vexana counts under her breath while Guinevere recovers, reaching four.
Guinevere counts one, two, three in bed after the raid.
Hester counts "One. Two. Three." when Guinevere falls, and Guinevere stands on three.
Soon Guinevere counts with her.
On the storm night Hester counted the steps aloud so the baby would not cry.
When nobody comes, Guinevere counts herself up.

rel.t: Hester's habit.

entries.line: Counting to three to get up after a fall.
entries.short: Hester, of the House's guard, counted "One. Two. Three." whenever little Guinevere fell, and Guinevere stood up on three.
entries.summary: When little Guinevere fell, Hester of the House's guard knelt and counted "One. Two. Three," and Guinevere stood on three. Soon Guinevere counted with her. On the storm night Hester, then the newest guard, carried the baby to the cellar and counted the steps aloud so she would not cry. When nobody comes, Guinevere counts herself up, and years later she still counts under her breath in bed. When Guinevere claims she can regain her elegance in three seconds, Vexana counts, and says four.

entries.name: host

facts.t: Obsidia says every civilization tries to transcend its own host.
Obsidia says the host is the planet. A people that outgrows it uses it up and reaches for other worlds. A purge leaves the host alive to begin again.
Obsidia says after the last people she helped end, the Enders slept until the host grew a new people.

entries.line: Obsidia's word for the planet a people lives on.
entries.short: Obsidia's word for a people's planet. She says a people that outgrows its host uses it up, while a purge leaves the host alive.
entries.summary: Obsidia's word for the planet a people lives on. She says every civilization tries to transcend its own host: a people that outgrows it uses it up, reaches for other worlds and leaves a dead world behind. A purge, she says, leaves the host alive to begin again. After the last people she helped end, the Enders slept until the host grew a new one.

entries.name: Imperatrix

facts.t: Obsidia is the Storm Citadel's Imperatrix, its empress.

entries.line: Obsidia's title as ruler of the Storm Citadel.
entries.short: Obsidia's title. She is the Storm Citadel's Imperatrix, its empress, and the ship answers to her and to no one else.
entries.summary: Imperatrix means empress. It is Obsidia's title as ruler of the Storm Citadel, the largest ship of her kind, which answers to her and to no one else.

entries.name: Karina's rule
aka: You don't put down someone you carried out

facts.t: Karina says: "You don't put down someone you carried out."
The clerk says it is no rule. Karina says it is hers, and duty.
Selena has kept those words since the second night.
Selena thinks Karina never asked because if she knew, she might have to put her down.

rel.t: It is Karina's own rule.

entries.line: Karina's rule for the people she carries out of the ruins.
entries.short: Karina's own rule, said over the shelter's log: "You don't put down someone you carried out." She calls it duty.
entries.summary: Karina is on the rescue team that carries the living out of the ruins. On the second night after the storm, she signs the nameless girl she carried out into her care again, and when the clerk objects she says, "You don't put down someone you carried out." He says it is no rule. She says it is hers, and duty. Selena keeps those words for years, and comes to think Karina never asked what she is because then she might have to put her down.

entries.name: lag

facts.t: On Tetra's feed Angela's arm comes up a beat late, every time.
Angela lags because the trojan jams the Council's link a little: she answers each order late, like a screen that freezes.
Every one of Angela's blows comes a beat late, so Ruby could dodge them all.
Selrick's record shows the small android firing at students a beat late.

rel.t: The trojan causes it.

entries.line: Why Angela answers every order a beat late.
entries.short: Angela answers each order a beat late. Ruby's trojan jams the Council's link to her a little, like a screen that freezes.
entries.summary: On the feed from Tetra, the doll camera Angela carries, her arm comes up a beat late, every time. Ruby sees why: her trojan has woken but cannot break the Council's hold, so it only jams the link a little, and Angela answers each order late, like a screen that freezes. When Angela fights Ruby, every blow comes a beat late, so Ruby could dodge them all. Selrick's record later shows the small android firing at students a beat late.

entries.name: Layla's count

facts.t: From an Ender's arm lift to its chest split is always three; Layla timed it on the first ones.
She calls 'Three! Two! Now!' along the wall.
The soldiers fire on her count, and Fanny strikes on it.
She counts silently when back to back with Fanny.
Her cannon fires on her own count.

entries.line: Layla's count of three from an Ender's raised arm to its open chest.
entries.short: Layla's count: from an Ender's arm lift to the split of its chest plates is always three. She calls it along the wall.
entries.summary: At the bay road wall, Layla timed the first Enders: from the lift of an Ender's arm to the split of its chest plates is always a count of three. She calls "Three! Two! Now!" along the wall, and the Shield's soldiers begin to fire on her count. Fanny strikes on it too. Back to back with Fanny, she counts in silence and drops on now, so Fanny's blade can sweep over her into the open chest. Later her cannon fires on her own count.

entries.name: Lesley's dream

facts.t: Screams, crying, metal scraping on metal and the endless roar of the Enders, with Lesley running the wrong way through a crowd.
It always ends on a child's voice.
The voice says: 'Go away! Leave me alone!'
It never reaches back as far as the house she grew up in.
It replays the night the base fell and always ends on a child's voice.
In the dream, years later, Chang'e's quiet "Leave me alone" becomes a shout.
It ends on "Go away! Leave me alone!"
After it Lesley always touches her visor.

rel.t: Lesley's nightmare.

entries.line: Lesley's recurring nightmare, which always ends on a child's voice.
entries.short: Lesley's recurring nightmare: screams, the Enders' roar, and running the wrong way through a crowd. It always ends on a child's voice.
entries.summary: Lesley's recurring nightmare replays the night the base fell: screams, crying, metal scraping on metal, the endless roar of the Enders, and Lesley running the wrong way through a crowd. It never reaches back as far as the house she grew up in. It always ends on a child's voice: "Go away! Leave me alone!" That night Chang'e said it so low Lesley hardly heard it. In the dream it became a shout. After the dream, Lesley always touches her visor.

entries.name: lull

facts.t: Joe says that when Enders are hurt badly they go quiet for weeks. This is called a lull, and a lull always ends.
When a boom shakes the hall, Joe says the lull is over.
At sunset the swarm draws back. It has only gone quiet.
A lull is the weeks the Enders go quiet; when one begins, every Ender signal stops in the same moment.
Badly hurt Enders go quiet for a while; Vexana thinks every win only buys a lull, and a lull always ends.
Vexana thinks of the lulls when Obsidia says the Will goes dark for a while after Enders die in numbers.

entries.line: The weeks the Enders go quiet after they are badly hurt.
entries.short: Joe's word for the weeks the Enders go quiet after they are badly hurt. A lull always ends.
entries.summary: When Enders are hurt badly, they go quiet for weeks. Joe calls it a lull, and says a lull always ends. When one begins, every Ender signal on the Academy's screens stops in the same moment. Vexana thinks every win only buys a lull. Obsidia says that when Enders die in numbers the Will goes dark for a while, then stirs again and sends more.

entries.name: Missing

facts.t: A student says Missing is what they write first.
The records form says that after long enough with no trace, a file says Killed in action.
Lesley rules no body, no finding: Vexana's file stays Missing.
Missing people do not draw a stipend.
Vexana learns Missing is the word for her now.

entries.line: The status written on a file when someone vanishes with no trace.
entries.short: The status on a file when someone is lost with no trace. A student says Missing is what they write first.
entries.summary: Missing is the status on a file when someone is lost with no trace. After Vexana vanishes, a sheet on the board reads VEXANA: MISSING, and a student says Missing is what they write first. Weeks later a records clerk says that after this long, the form says Killed in action. Lesley rules no body, no finding, and Vexana's file stays Missing. At the crews' yard, Vexana learns from Selena that Missing is the word for her now, and that Missing people draw no stipend.

entries.name: mobile support

facts.t: Chang'e posts Selena to mobile support.
Mobile support goes wherever the fight bends.
Its light on the panel keeps blinking when nobody answers.
Fanny takes it for a spotter's post in the best seat in the city.
Lesley calls on mobile support to report, and Selena lets the call go by.
Its light on Chang'e's console keeps blinking.
Its light still blinks after the field dies.

rel.t: Selena is mobile support.
Lesley calls her as mobile support.

entries.line: Selena's post in the battle: wherever the fight bends.
entries.short: Selena's battle post, set by Chang'e. Mobile support goes wherever the fight bends.
entries.summary: Chang'e posts Selena to mobile support, because Silverbolt is the fastest machine in her division. Mobile support goes wherever the fight bends. Selena sits on the bell tower and lets every call to report go by, and the light for mobile support on Chang'e's console keeps blinking all day, even after the ship's field dies. Fanny takes her for a spotter in the best seat in the city.

entries.name: Nobody goes alone

facts.t: The instructor's order to the singles at the dome's foot.
Because of it, Vexana followed Guinevere when she ran.

entries.line: The order given to the single cadets in a raid.
entries.short: The instructor's order to the cadets without partners at the dome's foot: take the side streets, and nobody goes alone.
entries.summary: An instructor's order to the singles, the cadets without partners, when the reserve is sent to the dome's foot: Singles, the side streets. Nobody goes alone. When Guinevere ran up a side street toward the Enders by herself, Vexana followed her because of it, a street's length back, near enough to shoot.

entries.name: Obsidia's experiment

facts.t: Obsidia calls the day of the attack the final stage of her experiment. Under every plan lies one want: to see a different ending.

entries.line: Obsidia's long plan, and the want under it.
entries.short: Obsidia calls the day of the attack the final stage of her experiment. Under every plan lies one want: to see a different ending.
entries.summary: Obsidia calls the day of the attack the final stage of her experiment. If the body finishes the humans, she will watch the old ending hold. If not, she will go in herself. The pawn she made is her way to find out what comes after a purge. Under every plan lies one want she never wrote into any: to see a different ending.

entries.name: Outstanding Student

facts.t: After the year's showing, Selena's file gains the line Outstanding Student.

entries.line: An honor written into an Academy student's file.
entries.short: A line added to a student's Academy file. Selena's file gains it after the year's showing.
entries.summary: An honor written into a student's file at the Academy. After the year's showing, where Silverbolt stood on a plinth behind a rope, Selena's file gained the line Outstanding Student. Only Selena knew that Silverbolt was, in every sense, a weapon of the Enders.

entries.name: Partners tell each other first

facts.t: Guinevere's stake in the match: if she wins, Vexana tells her first, every cut, every paper.
After the drawn match both make the rule: partners tell each other first, both of them.
It heads Guinevere's new month plan in gold.
Guinevere shouts her thanks when Vexana tells her first that her arm aches.
Vexana decides a present does not count.
Vexana promised it on the training-hall floor, but decides she cannot tell this.

rel.t: Guinevere and Vexana made it together.

entries.line: Guinevere and Vexana's rule of telling each other first.
entries.short: A rule Guinevere and Vexana make after a drawn match: partners tell each other first, both of them.
entries.summary: Guinevere stakes it on a one-armed match: if she wins, Vexana tells her first, every cut, every paper. The match ends in a draw, so they both make the rule: partners tell each other first. It heads Guinevere's new month plan in gold, and when Vexana tells her first that her arm aches, Guinevere shouts her thanks. Vexana decides a present does not count. After the corridor she remembers her promise and decides she cannot tell this.

entries.name: pawn

facts.t: Obsidia says the Will lets a pawn move freely for a while. If it slips beyond control, there is only one outcome.
Vexana names the outcome: termination. Obsidia inclines her head.
Vexana thinks: free for a while, until the day it finds out.
Selena sells to Vexana to see how another pawn like herself might escape the game.
Selena's body knows the rule: a pawn could run loose for a while, but if it got away for good it was finished.
Obsidia thinks even the storm night was for the seed, and that afterward her hand would only spoil what grew.
Selena thinks of Vexana as another pawn getting out of the game.
Obsidia calls Selena her pawn.
Obsidia says her finest creation has gone off-script.
Selena would rather live as Selena than remain someone else's pawn.
Obsidia greets Selena as 'my little doll.'
Asking what to destroy next is the line a good pawn would say.
Obsidia says the next thing to destroy is a pawn with no surprises left.
Selena says she will never be Obsidia's puppet again.
Obsidia calls her 'my puppet.'

rel.t: Obsidia says the storm night was for it.

entries.line: Obsidia's word for the one of hers living among the humans.
entries.short: Obsidia's word for the one of hers among the humans. The Will lets a pawn move freely for a while. If it slips beyond control, there is one outcome.
entries.summary: Obsidia's word for Selena, the thing she made and set loose among the humans. She says the Will lets a pawn move freely for a while, but if it ever slips beyond control there is only one outcome: termination. Selena's body knows that rule, and she sells to Vexana to see how another pawn might escape the game. Obsidia calls her her finest creation, gone off-script. In the throne hall she greets her as her little doll, and Selena says she will never be her puppet again.

entries.name: payment in places

facts.t: Vexana pays Selena in places: where wreckage lies, before the crews find it.
A place buys a set of plates; another place buys the other knee.
Cores cost three places each.
Obsidia pays her pawn in places: where an Ender fell, set in its head before the humans can drag the wreck away.
The Enders pay Selena with a place set in her head, where a downed Ender lies.
Vexana pays Selena in places, whole Enders where no crew has been. Selena thinks that beats money.
Selena prices cores at three places each.
After each report a ditch with a downed Ender would come into her head, and by nightfall the plates were sold.
When the payments stop, her head stays empty at the sink.

entries.line: Wreck sites used as money: where a downed Ender lies.
entries.short: How Vexana pays Selena for salvage: she tells her where wreckage lies, before the crews find it.
entries.summary: A place is a wreck site: where a downed Ender lies, before any crew has found it. Vexana pays Selena in places for Ender plates and cores, at three places a core. Obsidia pays Selena the same way for her reports, setting the place of a fallen Ender in her head, and by nightfall the plates are sold. Selena thinks it beats money. When Obsidia stops paying, Selena's head stays empty at the sink.

entries.name: Plan A and Plan B

facts.t: Guinevere's Plan A is that she smashes the Core and they win; Plan B is that they come home.
Vexana says "Plan B" when Guinevere insists.
Guinevere sings "Two of us, shining out of the dark and home!" and says Vexana has given her a song.
When a siren sounds she says "Plan A first."
Guinevere says, "Plan A first."
On the green-railed roof Guinevere laid it out: she smashes the Core and they win.
Plan B is that they come home. Guinevere made Vexana say "Plan B" out loud.
They never found the Core, so the open chest is the one blow left.
Vexana says, "This is Plan A," and gives no more.
Guinevere notices that Vexana did not say Plan B.
As the black hole takes them, Vexana says "Plan B" without being asked.
Guinevere's light flares up gold at the words.
Vexana thinks 'Plan B' when warmth stops her body fading.

entries.line: Guinevere's two plans: win, or come home.
entries.short: Guinevere's two plans. Plan A: she smashes the Core and they win. Plan B: they come home. She makes Vexana say it.
entries.summary: On the green-railed roof, Guinevere lays out her two plans. Plan A, she smashes the Core and they win. Plan B, they come home. She makes Vexana say "Plan B" out loud, sings about it, and when a siren sounds says "Plan A first." On the day of the attack the Core is never found, and Vexana says only "This is Plan A." Guinevere notices she did not say Plan B. As the black hole takes them, Vexana says it without being asked, and Guinevere's light flares gold.

entries.name: preparatory course

facts.t: It is the Combat Division's year of training before any real fight.
It ends with a final combat trial scored by the instructors.
It ends on Team-Up Day.

rows: The final combat trial, then Team-Up Day

rel.t: It is the Combat Division's course.

entries.line: The Combat Division's year of training before any real fight.
entries.short: The Combat Division's year of training before any real fight. Cadets whose needle passes the line at the assessment go there.
entries.summary: A cadet whose needle passes the line at the entrance assessment goes on to the Combat Division's preparatory course: a year of training before any real fight. The rest go to the Support Division. The course ends with a final combat trial scored by the instructors, which never goes on the rankings board, and then Team-Up Day, when cadets ask each other to be partners.

entries.name: protectors of all humanity

facts.t: Layla and Fanny say together: "We've gotta get stronger. After all, we're the protectors of all humanity."
Neither had planned it.

entries.line: The words Layla and Fanny say together on a ruined rooftop.
entries.short: What Layla and Fanny say together, without planning to: "We've gotta get stronger. After all, we're the protectors of all humanity."
entries.summary: On a ruined rooftop, the night of their battle outside the dome, Layla and Fanny say it together: "We've gotta get stronger. After all, we're the protectors of all humanity." Neither had planned it. Then they drop into the dark street and go back to training.

entries.name: purge protocol

facts.t: A voice from everywhere orders, "Vexana. Execute purge protocol."
To purge a place is to wipe it clean.
Guinevere takes it as an order to kill her.
Vexana sees it as a trap: kill her partner, or show her side. Either way the Will wins.
Vexana wanted the Will to think the purge was done.

rel.t: Obsidia reads that the Will planned one order with Guinevere in front of Vexana.

entries.line: The order the Will gives Vexana in front of Guinevere.
entries.short: An order from a voice everywhere: "Vexana. Execute purge protocol." To purge a place is to wipe it clean.
entries.summary: On the day of the attack, a voice from everywhere orders, "Vexana. Execute purge protocol." To purge a place is to wipe it clean, and Guinevere takes it as an order to kill her. Vexana sees it as the Will's trap: kill her partner, or show her side, and either way the Will wins. She wanted the Will to think the purge was done, so it would go on trusting her until the Matrix stood whole and close.

entries.name: purification

facts.t: Obsidia says destruction gives rise to new life, and that is the meaning of purification.
Obsidia says purification is not the end but where everything begins.
Selena says she does not care about it.

entries.line: Obsidia's word for destruction that makes way for new life.
entries.short: Obsidia's word for destruction. She says destruction gives rise to new life, and that is the meaning of purification.
entries.summary: Obsidia's name for destruction. In the throne hall she tells Selena that destruction gives rise to new life, and that is the meaning of purification. Later, on the leaning stairs of her burning ship, she says purification is not the end but where everything begins. Selena answers that she does not care about it, and demands her freedom back.

entries.name: raids

facts.t: Cores come back to the lab in a raid crate.
Lesley leads her first raid in command as a Shield commander.
After the base fell the raids thin, then stop for a long time.
Guinevere and Vexana fight raids together as cadets.
House Baroque lends money to rebuild each ward after a raid.

entries.line: Ender attacks on the city, and the fights against them.
entries.short: Ender attacks and the fights against them. After a raid, Ender cores come back to the lab in a crate.
entries.summary: Raids are the Enders' attacks and the fights against them. After one, cores come back to the lab in a raid crate. Lesley led her first raid in command as a Shield commander. After the base fell the raids thinned, then stopped for a long time. Later Guinevere and Vexana fought raids together as cadets, and House Baroque lent money to rebuild each ward after one.

entries.name: recalibration

facts.t: Strands of living violet tissue from the body's seam close cracks in Obsidia's shell.
Obsidia stops it before it is done: "That's enough recalibration."
Obsidia says it mends more than the shell: it sets a made thing back to what it was made for.
Obsidia says each healing now smooths some of her away, so she takes it only when she must.

rel.t: The body does it.

entries.line: The body's healing, which sets a made thing back to what it was made for.
entries.short: The body's healing. Living violet strands close cracks in Obsidia's shell, and set a made thing back to what it was made for.
entries.summary: Strands of living violet tissue come from the body's seam and close the cracks in Obsidia's shell. Obsidia stops them before they are done: "That's enough recalibration." She says it mends more than the shell: it sets a made thing back to what it was made for. Before she woke it cost her nothing. Now each healing smooths some of her away, so she takes it only when she must.

entries.name: registration rule

facts.t: Chang'e's rule: no change to a registered mecha without a field-test report and her mark.
It covers any change, especially paint.
Selena files a report for the name, because a name is a change.

rel.t: Chang'e's rule.

entries.line: Chang'e's rule for any change to a registered mecha.
entries.short: Chang'e's rule: no change to a registered mecha without a field-test report and her mark. Any change, even paint.
entries.summary: When a training frame comes to Selena's bench, registered to her, Chang'e gives her the rule: no change to a registered mecha without a field-test report and Chang'e's mark. It covers any change, paint included. After her first run on the rebuilt frame, Selena files a report for its name, because a name is a change: Frame Nine, Name: Silverbolt. Chang'e reads it twice and makes her mark.

entries.name: regulation

facts.t: Lesley refuses Chang'e's rifle lamp because it is not regulation.
Chang'e decides she will make it regulation.
Lesley refuses the heated gloves for the same reason.
Asked what is under the cloth on her bench, Chang'e answers: 'Nothing regulation.'
Lesley hands back anything that is not regulation, such as a lamp and gloves.
Chang'e makes the rifle regulation so Lesley cannot hand it back.
Chang'e tells Lesley the rifle is regulation.

rel.t: The Shield's rules.

entries.line: The Shield's standard, and Lesley's reason for handing gifts back.
entries.short: Lesley hands back anything that is not Shield regulation, like the rifle lamp and heated gloves Chang'e built for her.
entries.summary: Regulation is the Shield's standard. Lesley hands back Chang'e's rifle lamp and heated gloves because they are not regulation, and Chang'e decides she will make it regulation. Asked what is under the cloth on her bench, she answers, "Nothing regulation." She reads the Shield's rulebook cover to cover, learns that a Shield rifle is worked by hand and needs nothing else, and builds one. "It's regulation," she tells Lesley, and Lesley does not hand it back.

entries.name: Ruby's rage

facts.t: Something comes up in Ruby when Angela is hurt.
When it came before, everything went quiet and hot, and she cut down everything in front of her.
It makes crying sound far away.
It never cared what it hit.
In the avenue it took Angela's shout to bring Ruby back.
This time Ruby holds it to one cut.

rel.t: It is Ruby's own rage.

entries.line: The blind fury that comes up in Ruby when Angela is hurt.
entries.short: A fury that comes up in Ruby when Angela is hurt. Everything goes quiet and hot, and she cuts down everything in front of her.
entries.summary: Something comes up in Ruby when Angela is hurt. The first time, in a burning avenue, everything went quiet and hot. She cut down everything in front of her, the lamp post and the wall too, and raised her scythe over a crying child, and it took Angela's shout to bring her back. The rage makes crying sound far away, and it never cared what it hit. At the bay road it comes again, and this time Ruby makes herself hear the crying and holds it to one cut, into the core.

entries.name: Selena's graduation

facts.t: Selena joked about it in class; Karina still wants to see it.
That morning Selena's papers flew as she cried 'what about my graduation?!'
Selena thinks somebody down there still wants to see her graduate.

entries.line: Selena's graduation from the Academy, still to come.
entries.short: Selena's graduation from the Academy, still ahead. She jokes about it in class, and Karina still wants to see it.
entries.summary: Selena's graduation from the Academy, still to come. She joked about it in class, and one morning her papers flew as she cried: what about my graduation?! Karina still wants to see it. High over the city, Selena thinks that somebody down there still wants to see her graduate.

entries.name: Selena's thread

facts.t: A thin thread opened beside Obsidia's recall, running up through the Ender parts of the pawn's own machine.
Obsidia could close it with a thought but leaves it open.
Reports come up it only on storm nights, when lightning hides it from human instruments.
Selena reasons that the pull is a line, and lines run both ways.
Pushing through Silverbolt's core, she opens a thin thread beside the pull, hers alone, that tells her nothing of where it ends.
In clear weather a signal sent this way would spike on Chang'e's screens, but in a storm the lightning buries it.
Her own thread never told her where it ended.
It has been silent for days since Obsidia stopped paying.
Two more reports came up it unpaid, then it went still.

rel.t: It opened the thread to Obsidia.
She opened it.
Selena sends her reports up it.

entries.line: A thin secret line from Obsidia's pawn back up to her.
entries.short: A thin thread Obsidia's pawn opened beside her recall. Reports come up it only on storm nights, when lightning hides it.
entries.summary: A thin line Selena opened beside the recall. Lines run both ways, she reasoned, so she pushed through Silverbolt's core and the Ender plates on it until a thread of her own gave. It tells her nothing of where it ends. She sends reports up it only on storm nights, when lightning hides it from Chang'e's screens. Obsidia could close it with a thought but leaves it open, and pays for each report. When she stops paying, two more reports come up unpaid, then it goes still.

entries.name: sergeant's throw

facts.t: Fanny lays Layla flat with her sergeant's throw.
She offers to teach it, saying it saves a lot of time.
Layla had filed the throw, with the promise to teach it, as an insult.

rel.t: It is a throw from Fanny's Shield training.

entries.line: The Shield throw Fanny uses to lay Layla flat.
entries.short: A throw from Fanny's Shield training. She lays Layla flat with it, then offers to teach it: it saves a lot of time.
entries.summary: A throw Fanny learned in the Shield. When Layla needles her, Fanny lays her flat with it and offers to teach it, saying it saves a lot of time. Layla filed the throw, and the promise to teach it, as an insult. Later she sees that it was an offer.

entries.name: Sis

facts.t: Lesley's brother called her Sis and never anything else.
It was the last word he said, as a question.
Chang'e's mother says a girl who protects you, if she isn't your mom, is a big sister.
Chang'e shortens 'big sister' to 'Big Sis', then to 'Sis', for when there is no time.
When Chang'e calls Lesley Sis after the rack falls, it is her brother's word.
Chang'e asks 'Sis? Does it work?' the same way Lesley's brother said it.

rel.t: It is what Chang'e and Lesley's brother call her.

entries.line: What Lesley's little brother called her.
entries.short: What Lesley's little brother called her. She was Sis to him, and he never called her anything else.
entries.summary: Lesley's little brother called her Sis and nothing else. It was the last word he said, as a question, behind her in the dark. Later Chang'e asks her mother what to call a girl who protects you, if she isn't your mom. "A big sister," her mother says, so Chang'e shortens it to Big Sis, then to Sis, for when there is no time. When Chang'e first calls her Sis, Lesley goes still: it is her brother's word.

entries.name: Stay back

facts.t: The two words Vexana's father said whenever the drill bell rang.
He said them as he left her at the shelter on the night of the attack.
He said them a last time, standing between her and the Ender.
They come into Vexana's head when she starts down the gallery stair toward Guinevere, and she stops.

entries.line: The two words Vexana's father said whenever the drill bell rang.
entries.short: The two words Vexana's father said whenever the drill bell rang, before he went up to his gun.
entries.summary: Vexana's father served a Shield gun on the wall. Whenever the drill bell rang he said two words, "Stay back," and went up to his gun while she ran to the shelter. One evening every gun on the wall fired at once. That night he said them as he left her at the shelter door, and a last time standing between her and the Ender. Years later, as she starts down the gallery stair toward Guinevere, the words come back, and she stops.

entries.name: stipend

facts.t: The Academy pays every cadet a small stipend; Vexana's lay unspent in paper bands in her toolbox.
She broke the first band to buy the felt.
She paid for a second pot of tea from the same band.
Selena would take stipend money, but Missing people do not draw a stipend.

entries.line: The small allowance the Academy pays each cadet.
entries.short: A small allowance the Academy pays every cadet. Vexana's lies unspent in paper bands in her toolbox.
entries.summary: The Academy pays every cadet a small stipend. Vexana's lay unspent in paper bands in her toolbox, until she broke the first band to buy felt for Guinevere. She paid for a second pot of tea from the same band. Later Selena says she would take stipend money, but Missing people do not draw a stipend.

entries.name: technical bug

facts.t: Ruby expects Oro's officers to call the trojan's fault a technical bug that only the one who wrote the code could mend.
Soldiers tell Ruby the Council reports a technical bug in its secret weapon that its engineers cannot find, and only her creator can fix.

rel.t: It is how the trojan's effect is meant to look to Oro.

entries.line: The cover story for the trojan in Angela.
entries.short: What Ruby expects Oro's officers to call the trojan's fault: a technical bug only the one who wrote the code can mend.
entries.summary: Ruby hides a trojan in Angela that will wake on the Dawnbreak mission. She expects Oro's officers to see a fault they cannot locate and call it a technical bug, one only the code's writer could mend. It goes that way: soldiers tell Ruby the Council reports a technical bug in its secret weapon that its engineers cannot find, and only her creator can fix it.

entries.name: the alley thing

facts.t: In her assessment Fanny fights the soldiers' way, her back to a narrow alley, so the Enders must come one or two at a time.
Fanny offers to show Layla the alley thing because it saves time.
Fanny drills in the drill hall's one narrow doorway, so anything that comes at her has to take turns.
Layla finds it so simple it makes her angry.
In the test match Layla turns it around: the drones come down one narrow line, so one full charge could take the whole row.
Fanny laughs that Layla did hear her about the alley thing.
Outside the dome there is no narrow place to hold.
The wall stands across the narrowest place with one gap; nobody swings until an Ender does, then steel goes into the core.
Layla once spied on it from a dark gallery and then pretended she had never heard of it.

rel.t: Fanny fights this way, the soldiers' way she learned with the Shield.

entries.line: Fanny's way of fighting with her back to a narrow place.
entries.short: Fanny's tactic: fight with your back to a narrow alley, so the Enders must come at you one or two at a time.
entries.summary: In her assessment Fanny fights the soldiers' way, her back to a narrow alley, so the Enders have to come one or two at a time. Layla spies on her drilling in the drill hall's one narrow doorway, and finds it so simple it makes her angry. In the test match Layla turns it around: the drones come down one narrow line, so one full charge could take the row. At the bay road Fanny builds the wall across the narrowest place, with one gap, and steel goes into each core as it opens.

entries.name: The Aspirants always stand united

facts.t: Guinevere remembers that even Fanny said it, and her star lights.
Fanny said it with her blades raised at Vexana.
Guinevere tells Fanny she held on to it inside the black hole.

entries.line: The words every Aspirant shouted together on the platforms.
entries.short: The Aspirants' shout. Everyone said it on the platforms, even Fanny, and the thought of it lights Guinevere's star.
entries.summary: On the platforms, after Guinevere's call to the Aspirants, everyone said it together: "The Aspirants always stand united!" Fanny said it too, with her blades still raised at Vexana. Inside the black hole, with her star almost dark, Guinevere remembers that even Fanny said it, and the star lights. Afterward she tells Fanny she held on to it in there.

entries.name: the cycle

facts.t: Obsidia asks how many times humanity has walked the same path.
Obsidia says the children of the few survivors built again and remembered nothing.
Obsidia says the world's life began under falling stones, and that destruction is merely the beginning of a new cycle.
Obsidia says that after a people is ended the Enders sleep for ages until the host grows a new people.
To Obsidia every raid was the cycle working on a people with nothing to fight it with.
If the body finishes the humans, Obsidia will watch the old ending hold.
She wants to see a different ending.

entries.line: Obsidia's view of history: destruction, then a new beginning.
entries.short: Obsidia's view of history: peoples rise, are ended and begin again. She says destruction is merely the beginning of a new cycle.
entries.summary: Obsidia asks how many times humanity has walked the same path. She says the world's life began under falling stones, that the children of a purge's few survivors built again and remembered nothing, and that destruction is merely the beginning of a new cycle. After each people ends, the Enders sleep until the host grows a new one. To her every raid on the humans was the cycle at work. If the body finishes them, she will watch the old ending hold, but she wants a different ending.

entries.name: the end of the world

facts.t: Ruby asks Angela, if they are separated, to wait for her at the end of the world.
Angela promises she will, and asks Ruby to wait for her too.

entries.line: Where Ruby and Angela promise to wait for each other.
entries.short: Where Ruby asks Angela to wait for her if they are separated. Angela promises, and asks Ruby to wait for her too.
entries.summary: After they bring down a giant Ender together, shield and scythe, Ruby asks Angela to wait for her at the end of the world if they are separated. Angela promises she will, and asks Ruby to wait for her too. Moments later soldiers come down the avenue to take them.

entries.name: the Ender hum

facts.t: On the storm night something deep and huge hums in Selena's bones, coming from above.
When the black cloud is gone, the hum goes out of her bones.
When the Ender finds her in the raid, the hum of the first night comes back.
The giant's hum reaches her across the whole city, ringing in her bones like a bell.
All her life Enders had hummed in her bones. The recall is the hum with a hook in it.
Before a raid she feels the Enders' hum gather a day early.
At the breach the black Enders' hum reached her across the city.
She knows somebody made the hum in her bones.
It comes up through the tiles into Selena's bones before she sees anything.
Every Ender carries a small piece of it; the Citadel carries the whole.
It is the hum Selena heard on the night of the mud.
Selena's bones call it home.
Each small ship hums a small sharp note under the deep one.
In the throne hall the ship's note and the field's lower note come from one place.

entries.line: The deep hum Selena feels in her bones near Enders.
entries.short: The deep hum of the Enders that Selena feels in her bones. Every Ender carries a small piece of it. The Storm Citadel carries the whole.
entries.summary: Selena has felt the Enders hum in her bones all her life. On the storm night it came down from a black cloud over the bay, felt like home, and went out of her when the cloud left. Giants ring in her bones across the city, and she feels the hum gather a day before a raid. Every Ender carries a small piece of it, and the Storm Citadel carries the whole. She knows somebody made it. In the throne hall the ship's note and the field's lower note come from one place.

entries.name: the first rule of Enders

facts.t: Joe teaches that Enders expose their weak spots only when they launch attacks, and that brief moment is all the time you get.
Layla answers that you hit it when it attacks.
Team B3 drills the weak spot in VR.
By Joe's rule the breach Ender's chest opens only when it strikes, so its neck is the only other opening.
Layla applies Joe's rule to the gold giant: its chest opens when it fires.
An Ender's chest plates split for the strike.
Every Academy student learns that Enders open their weak spot only when they strike: the chest plates split and the core shows.
Joe taught a lesson on weak spots.
An Ender's chest opens as it strikes, and a shot into it kills.
Vexana calls it the first rule of Enders: when one fires, its plates split and the core is bare.
Vexana says of the Matrix, "It opens when it fires. Only then."
In Joe's class Layla called the weak spot obvious: when it attacks.

entries.line: Enders show their weak spot only when they strike.
entries.short: Joe's lesson: Enders show their weak spot only when they attack. The chest plates split, the core glows, and that moment is all you get.
entries.summary: Every Academy student learns it from Joe: Enders expose their weak spot only when they launch an attack. The chest plates split, the core shows, and that brief moment is all the time you get. Layla calls it obvious, and uses it on the breach Ender and the gold giant. Vexana calls it the first rule of Enders, and means to meet the Mother Matrix with it: "It opens when it fires. Only then."

entries.name: the flying ban

facts.t: Flying is banned on school grounds, except in the white training corridor.
Flying is banned on school grounds.

rel.t: It is an Academy rule.
An Academy rule.

entries.line: The Academy rule against flying on school grounds.
entries.short: Flying is banned on school grounds, except in the white training corridor.
entries.summary: Flying is banned on the grounds of Selrick Academy. The one exception is the white training corridor, where Fanny meets the drones in the air in her suit.

entries.name: the four conditions

facts.t: Chang'e holds up four fingers.
The android comes to Chang'e's lab for an examination, the heir takes the entrance assessment, an AI droid follows them everywhere, and they sit in the third-year class beside the two who vouched.
Ruby accepts them.
An AI droid takes its place one step behind Ruby.

rel.t: It is one of the conditions.
Chang'e sets them.

entries.line: Chang'e's four terms for letting Ruby and Angela stay.
entries.short: Chang'e's four terms for Ruby and Angela's refuge: a lab exam, the entrance assessment, a droid escort and seats beside Layla and Fanny.
entries.summary: When Lesley lets Ruby and Angela in under watch, Chang'e holds up four fingers. The android comes to her lab for an examination. The heir takes the entrance assessment. An AI droid follows them everywhere. And they sit in the third-year class beside the two who vouched for them, Layla and Fanny. Ruby accepts, and a slim white droid with one orange eye takes its place one step behind her.

entries.name: the leftward drift

facts.t: At full charge Layla's cannon pulled left, a hand's width at two hundred meters.
Each test ends in ERROR on Layla's console, one more line in a log going back months.
In the test match the full-charge shot pulls left and passes Fanny's shoulder by a hand's width.
The log reads FULL CHARGE, 200 M, a drift in centimeters, ERROR. Fanny counts a hundred and nineteen lines, all LEFT, nine to eleven centimeters.
The last red line is dated the night of the test match. Then three green lines read LEFT 0.3 CM, OK, the last from the night before the breach.
Before those, the cannon had never been right more than two times in a row.
Layla explains that the two halves of the charge came up at different speeds and the shot leaned toward the faster half.
Fanny realizes Layla put her on the right because the drift is left, where a miss could not reach her.

rows: Nine to eleven centimeters left at two hundred meters
The two halves of the charge came up at different speeds

rel.t: It is the fault in Layla's cannon.

entries.line: The fault that pulls Layla's full-charge shot to the left.
entries.short: A fault in Layla's cannon: at full charge the shot pulls left, a hand's width at two hundred meters. Each test ends in ERROR.
entries.summary: At full charge Layla's cannon pulled left, a hand's width at two hundred meters, and each test ended in ERROR. The log went back months: a hundred and nineteen red lines, all LEFT, nine to eleven centimeters. In the test match the drift sent her shot past Fanny's shoulder. Layla found the cause: the two halves of the charge came up at different speeds, and the shot leaned toward the faster half. She made the faster half wait, and kept Fanny on her right, where a miss could not reach her.

entries.name: the line

facts.t: It showed Obsidia that Selena crossed her city to the Academy that morning.
On the next storm night it put Selena on her tower over the Academy, then on a roof at the far edge of the city, then back.

entries.line: Obsidia's trace of where Selena goes.
entries.short: A trace that shows Obsidia where her pawn, Selena, goes in the city.
entries.summary: A trace that lets Obsidia follow where Selena goes. One morning it showed her Selena crossing the city to the humans' Academy, alive and not obeying. On the next storm night it put Selena on her tower over the Academy, then on a roof at the far edge of the city, then back. Obsidia knew a bearing when she saw one.

entries.name: the march

facts.t: An old march Vexana's father always hummed while he worked, always stopping in the same place.
He said he would finish it when the war did.
Vexana hums it under her blanket at the home and stops where he stopped; nobody knows the rest.

entries.line: An old march Vexana's father hummed and never finished.
entries.short: An old march Vexana's father hummed while he worked, always stopping in the same place. He would finish it when the war did.

Obsidia says then the commander is called out of the long sleep and small doors open near the people for the Enders.

official.text: Planet Dawnbreak is a planet in Universe A5-01. It was born in the Galaxy A-19 of the Saintess Constellation billions of years ago. In its early ages, it is full of nitrogen and its surface diurnal temperature variation is extreme, no life form can survive. Eons of asteroid and meteor impact greatly enrich the resources on the planet and bring plankton to the world. The planktons change the structure of the atmosphere bit by bit and after billions of years, all kinds of lifeforms emerge.

entries.summary: Oro is Ruby's home world, at A-20 in another galaxy, under a violet sky. Its will is Balance: after a terrible war with the Enders long ago, nobody there may grow strong enough to upset the order, and its three powers rule through the Council. To Ruby it is a prison, a golden birdcage where every post was chosen for her, so she flees it with Angela. Oro built her scythe, and she fears it may take Angela again.

official.text: Planet Oro is a planet in Universe A5-01. It was born in the Galaxy A-20 of the Aquila Constellation billions of years ago. The will of A-20 is "Balance", the same as the universe. It was a nitrogen gas planet in its early years. After billions of years of microbial action, it is now habitable planet.

entries.short: Humanity's last city, where the survivors of the Ender attacks drew back. Its dome of light, the Defensive Bubble, keeps the Enders out.
entries.summary: Terrinia is Dawnbreak's last city, humanity's final bastion, sheltered by the Defensive Bubble, a dome of light, its streets running down to the bay. In 983 Obsidia's strike put out its lights street by street. Raid after raid tears the dome, and the city holds the research base, later Selrick Academy, and House Baroque on a hill above it. In the great attack nearly half the city becomes rubble, but nothing of the burning Citadel falls on it.

official.text: To fight back against destruction, humanity reverse-engineered the wreckage of The Enders, developing mecha driven by humanity's hope and training the "Aspirants" capable of facing The Ender's head-on. Terrinia became humanity's final bastion.
