When a dummy swings, its chest opens, and Guinevere puts her fist into the open chest.
In the team test they come down all six rails at once, and a pair is out the moment a steel arm touches either of them.
At the end of the test every dummy hung dead on its rail.

entries.line: Steel training dummies built like Enders, run on rails.
entries.short: Steel dummies built like Enders that run at cadets on rails. When one swings, its chest plates open like a real Ender's.
entries.summary: Steel dummies built like Enders, used in the Academy's trials. They run at the cadets on rails, and when one swings, its chest plates open as a real Ender's do. At her trial Guinevere went under a dummy's arm and put her fist into its open chest. In the team test they came down all six rails at once, and a pair was out the moment a steel arm touched either of them. By the end of that test every dummy hung dead on its rail.

entries.name: strawberry-jam doughnut

facts.t: Guinevere says nothing can resist one, not even robots.
She tore one in two and gave Vexana half.

entries.line: A strawberry-jam doughnut from the cake shop.
entries.short: A strawberry-jam doughnut. Guinevere says nothing can resist one, not even robots, and splits it with Vexana.
entries.summary: A strawberry-jam doughnut at the cake shop. Guinevere held one up to her mended drone, which circled it twice, and said nothing can resist one, not even robots. Then she tore it in two and gave Vexana half in its paper napkin. Vexana kept the napkin.

entries.name: S·L·K

facts.t: The mark stamped on the students' matching jackets.
Ruby saw it on the students' jackets and comes asking refuge of their school.
It is the mark of Selrick, stamped on Selena's shirt.
The scorched suit's shoulder plate is stamped S·L·K.

rel.t: It is the Academy's mark.

entries.line: The mark stamped on Selrick students' jackets.
entries.short: The mark of Selrick, stamped on the students' jackets and shirts.
entries.summary: S·L·K is the mark of Selrick, stamped on the students' matching jackets and shirts. Ruby saw it on their jackets and came to their school to ask for refuge. It is also stamped on the shoulder plate of a scorched Aspirant suit that lies on the prow of the Storm Citadel.

entries.name: tactics books

facts.t: Two tactics books stand stacked square in Vexana's room.
She reads one at the corridor window.

entries.line: Two tactics books in Vexana's room.
entries.short: Two tactics books, stacked square in Vexana's nearly bare room.
entries.summary: Vexana owns two tactics books. They stand stacked square in her nearly bare room, beside a tin of oil and a jar of spare screws. One morning she stands reading one at the corridor window, turning pages as if she had been there for hours.

entries.name: team radio

facts.t: It sits on the shelf in Karina's flat and is never off. All night it hisses street names and counts.
Karina sleeps through its hissing, still in her coat.
On the day before it reports the cliff watch doubled, no change at the point over the bay, and all teams on standby.

rel.t: The team's radio.

entries.line: The rescue team's radio on Karina's shelf.
entries.short: The rescue team's radio on the shelf in Karina's flat. It is never off, and all night it hisses street names and counts.
entries.summary: The rescue team's radio sits on the shelf in Karina's flat and is never switched off. All night it hisses street names and counts, and Karina sleeps through it, still in her coat. On the day before the attack it reports the cliff watch doubled, no change at the point over the bay, and all teams on standby.

entries.name: team's log

facts.t: Karina signs the team's log to keep the child for one night.
The clerk tells her she cannot keep doing that.
After a week Karina stops signing it.

rel.t: The team's log.

entries.line: The rescue team's record book.
entries.short: The rescue team's log. Karina signs it to keep a child she carried out with her for one night.
entries.summary: The record book of the rescue team. When nobody comes for the child she carried out, Karina signs it to keep her for one night, then signs again the next evening. The clerk tells her she cannot keep doing that. After a week nobody has claimed the child, the clerk stops asking, and Karina stops signing.

entries.name: telescope

facts.t: A long telescope stands at the glass, pointed at nothing.
Guinevere moves it across the sky one small piece at a time until dawn.
From the ruined tower Vexana sees it turning, and knows someone is searching the sky one piece at a time.
It points out over the bay, toward where the crack hangs.
It creeps along the sky behind the glass of the observation lab.
It started after Vexana was taken.
It has turned a little farther.
It stands in the glass lab with a lamp beside it.
Through it Guinevere sees the far light burn magenta and flash.
It is linked to a screen at Ruby's console.

rel.t: It stands in the observation lab.
It stands in the lab.
It stands in the glass lab.

entries.line: A long telescope at the glass of the observation lab.
entries.short: A long telescope at the glass of the observation lab. Guinevere moves it across the sky one small piece at a time until dawn.
entries.summary: A long telescope stands at the glass of the observation lab. After Vexana was taken, Guinevere began moving it across the sky one small piece at a time. From the ruined tower Vexana sees it turning and knows someone is searching the sky. It points out over the bay toward the crack, and through it Guinevere sees the far light burn magenta and flash. It is linked to a screen at Ruby's console.

entries.name: test press

facts.t: It climbs past the mark, and Selena's knee joint holds.

entries.line: A testing press in Chang'e's lab.
entries.short: A testing press in Chang'e's lab. Chang'e and Selena bet on whether a knee joint of Selena's will crack in it.
entries.summary: A testing press in Chang'e's lab. Chang'e bet that a knee joint Selena made would crack in it, and Selena bet two puddings it would not. The press climbed past the mark and the joint held. Selena held out both hands: she had won again.

entries.name: Tetra

facts.t: A doll no longer than a hand: a copy of Angela in white, with pink hair, rabbit ears and a four-pointed star.
Its left eye is a camera lens, and whatever it sees lights a monitor on Ruby's bench.
Angela carries it pressed to her chest onto the ship.
Its feed runs one way only, so Ruby cannot speak to Angela through it.
Through its feed Ruby saw the androids wake at once in the ship's hold.
When Angela saves the child, Tetra rises from beside her and hangs above the ring of light, shining pink.
Ruby confesses she never told Angela it was a camera.
Angela keeps it after learning what it is.
Angela carries it in the crook of her arm.
Its left eye is a camera with a live link to Oro, so Chang'e wants it kept for checks.
Angela folds both arms around it and refuses.
Ruby cuts its link through her glove, and a tiny light goes out.
Ruby says it only sees for Angela now.
The tablet reads LINK: NONE after four seconds; Chang'e once spent a week cutting a link like that.
At the ceremony it is clipped at Angela's hip.
Angela carries it in the crook of her arm.
Angela keeps the little doll clipped at her hip.
Chang'e tells Mr. Bunny it is a new friend for him.
It is at Angela's shoulder when she reports at the hall panel.
It rides at Angela's shoulder in the fight, its camera eye turning with the battle.

rows: A copy of Angela in white, with pink hair, rabbit ears and a four-pointed star
Its left eye, once linked to Oro

rel.t: Its camera feeds the monitor in Ruby's laboratory.
Angela holds on to it even after learning it watched her.
She carries Tetra and keeps it.
Her doll.
It only sees for her now.
She keeps the doll clipped at her hip.
Chang'e calls it Mr. Bunny's new friend.
Tetra rides at her shoulder.
It rides at Angela's shoulder.

entries.line: A hand-sized doll of Angela that Angela carries.
entries.short: A doll no longer than a hand, a copy of Angela with pink hair and rabbit ears. Its left eye is a camera that feeds a monitor on Ruby's bench.
entries.summary: Tetra is a doll no longer than a hand, a copy of Angela in white with pink hair, rabbit ears and a four-pointed star. Its left eye is a camera, and Ruby never told Angela that its feed lit a monitor on her bench. Angela kept it after she learned. At the Academy Chang'e wanted it kept for checks, but Angela refused, and Ruby cut its link to Oro so it only sees for Angela now. It rides at her shoulder in the fight.

official.text: A gift for Angela from Ruby. Angela takes it with her wherever she is.

entries.name: the Academy's lists

facts.t: Hester says Guinevere's father reads them every morning.
She does not say which list: the rankings, or the one with the dead.

rel.t: The Academy publishes them.

entries.line: The lists Selrick Academy publishes.
entries.short: The lists Selrick Academy puts out: the rankings, and the one with the dead.
entries.summary: Selrick Academy publishes its lists. Hester tells Guinevere that her father reads them every morning. She does not say which list: the rankings, or the one with the dead.

entries.name: the armband

facts.t: The gray-bearded officer wears a rank armband on his sleeve.
He brings Lesley an armband that makes her a commander of the Shield's combat division.
She puts it on, though she thinks she held the wrong place.

rel.t: Lesley wears it.

entries.line: A Shield rank armband.
entries.short: A rank armband of the Shield, worn on the sleeve of the gray-bearded officer.
entries.summary: A rank armband of the Shield of Dawnbreak. The gray-bearded officer wears one on his sleeve. Months after the base falls, he brings one to Lesley: it makes her a commander of the Shield's combat division, because the squads asked for her. She thinks she held the wrong place, and puts it on.

entries.name: the armory door

facts.t: The station keeps its count of dead Enders there in chalk strokes.
Lesley makes her own stroke after her first kill.
It stayed behind when the station closed. A long row of strokes on it was hers.

rel.t: It is the door of the station's armory.

entries.line: The armory door of a far Shield station, chalked with strokes.
entries.short: The armory door at a far Shield station. The station keeps its count of dead Enders on it in chalk strokes.
entries.summary: The door of the armory at a far station of the Shield. The station keeps its count of dead Enders on it in chalk strokes. After her first kill, the sergeant held out the chalk and Lesley made her own stroke. When the station closed, the door stayed behind, and a long row of the strokes on it was hers.

entries.name: the barricade in the cut

facts.t: Fanny, Layla and a few soldiers drag a door and a shop sign across the street.
It is made of a door, a shop sign and a car tipped on its side, across the narrowest place, with one gap wide enough for one Ender at a time.
A dead Ender in front of the gap forces the rest to climb over it one at a time.
Four dead long-legged Enders make a heap in front of the gap.
Fanny built it the way suitless soldiers taught her.
The soldiers lay their rifles across the stack.
Its weak end, where the shop sign meets a house front, slides.

rows: Fanny, Layla and a few soldiers

rel.t: It stands across the cut.

entries.line: A street barricade dragged across the cut.
entries.short: A barricade of a door, a shop sign and a tipped car across the narrowest place in the cut, with a gap wide enough for one Ender at a time.
entries.summary: Fanny, Layla and a few soldiers build the barricade across the narrowest place in the cut, from a door, a shop sign and a car tipped on its side. Fanny built it the way suitless soldiers taught her, with one gap just wide enough for one Ender at a time. Dead Enders heap up in front of the gap, so the rest must climb over one at a time. The soldiers lay their rifles across the stack, but its weak end, where the sign meets a house front, slides.

entries.name: the base's alarm

facts.t: When it goes, every lamp in the lab turns red.
It is tested every week, so Lesley knows its note.
The red lamps die with it.
Years later it goes again when the Enders return.
Lesley says it started when she was halfway to the base.

rel.t: The base's own alarm.

entries.line: The siren of the research base.
entries.short: The research base's alarm. When it goes, every lamp in the lab turns red.
entries.summary: The research base's own alarm. It is tested every week, so Lesley knows its note. On the night the giant came it started while she was halfway back to the base, and every lamp in the lab turned red. The red lamps died with it. Years later it went again, when the Enders returned.

entries.name: the big bench

facts.t: A researcher says it is for grown-ups.
Chang'e falls asleep at it with her soldering iron in her hand.
After the first light the researcher tells Chang'e it is hers.

rel.t: A bench in the lab.

entries.line: The big workbench in Chang'e's lab.
entries.short: The big bench in the lab. A researcher tells young Chang'e it is for grown-ups.
entries.summary: The big workbench in the research base's lab. A researcher once found Chang'e at it, standing on a box, and sent her back to her corner: the bench was for grown-ups. She fell asleep at it anyway with her soldering iron in her hand. After the first light, the same researcher told her the big bench was hers.

entries.name: the birthday candle

facts.t: One candle stub kept in the kitchen drawer and lit on birthdays on whatever there was.
The family blew it out quickly so it would last.
On the night of the attack Lesley's mother lit it for seeing.
It went out when the wall fell.

entries.line: One candle stub, lit for every birthday in Lesley's house.
entries.short: The one candle stub Lesley's mother keeps in the kitchen drawer, lit on birthdays on whatever there is.
entries.summary: Lesley's mother kept one candle stub in the kitchen drawer. On a birthday she lit it on whatever there was, once a boiled egg, and the family blew it out quickly so it would last. On the night of the attack she lit it again, not for a birthday but for seeing. It went out when the wall fell.

entries.name: the birthday recording

facts.t: A recording from years ago that opens in Lesley's eye when she touches her visor.
In it Chang'e, barely up to Lesley's waist, sets an eye with a teal light in Lesley's palm.
It ends with two small warm hands pressing Lesley's cheeks.
Chang'e tells Mr. Bunny to film everything on Sis's birthday, from the start.
Chang'e loads Mr. Bunny's film into the eye, because the eye cannot see Lesley.
Chang'e gives it so Lesley has a picture.

rel.t: He films Lesley's birthday.
It is stored in the eye.

entries.line: An old recording kept in Lesley's machine eye.
entries.short: A recording from years ago that opens in Lesley's eye when she touches her visor. In it a small Chang'e sets an eye in Lesley's palm.
entries.summary: The birthday recording is a film from years ago, kept in Lesley's eye, that opens when she touches her visor. Chang'e told Mr. Bunny to film everything on Sis's birthday. In it Chang'e, barely up to Lesley's waist, sets an eye with a teal light in Lesley's palm, and it ends with two small warm hands pressing Lesley's cheeks. Chang'e loaded it into the eye because the eye cannot see Lesley, so that Lesley would have a picture.

entries.name: the black card

facts.t: Guinevere pays with a black card with a small gold House Baroque crest in its corner.
She turns it over at night and thinks her father paid for every gift she ever gave.
She stops before using it at the cake shop and offers to treat Vexana instead.

rel.t: It carries the House crest.

entries.line: Guinevere's black card with the House Baroque crest.
entries.short: A black card with a small gold House Baroque crest in its corner. Guinevere pays for Vexana's gifts with it.
entries.summary: Guinevere's black card, with a small gold House Baroque crest in its corner. She paid for Vexana's gifts with it before Vexana could speak. That night she turned it over and thought that her father had paid for every gift she ever gave. At the cake shop she stopped with it halfway out, and offered to treat Vexana instead, with the next one on Vexana.

entries.name: the black patch

facts.t: The station medic swapped Lesley's dressing for a black patch.
It covers Lesley's left eye when she arrives at the base.
Nobody had seen under it since the medic tied it on.
Lesley takes it off for Chang'e's eye.

rel.t: She wore it over her lost eye.

entries.line: The black patch over Lesley's left eye.
entries.short: The black patch the station medic ties over Lesley's eye, in place of her dressing.
entries.summary: A black patch over Lesley's left eye. The medic at the far station swapped her dressing for it, and she still wore it when she came to the research base. Nobody saw under it from the day it was tied on until she took it off for Chang'e, so that Chang'e could give her the eye she had built.

entries.name: the blue badges

facts.t: Small blue shields with the Academy's crest, given once a year to the best pair.
Guinevere held hers over her head all the way out of the hall.
She pinned hers back on crooked; Vexana's never came off.
Guinevere thumps hers when she vows to find a way.
They are new in the hand-in-hand photo.
Guinevere and Vexana wear them on their chests at the ceremony.
They are still pinned on under the tree that day.

rows: The best Aspirant Duo of the year

rel.t: They were given at the ceremony.

entries.line: Small blue shields for the year's best Aspirant pair.
entries.short: Small blue shields with the Academy's crest, given once a year to the best Aspirant Duo. Guinevere and Vexana win them.
entries.summary: The blue badges are small blue shields with the Academy's crest, given once a year to the best Aspirant Duo. Guinevere and Vexana won the first ones the Academy ever gave. Guinevere held hers over her head all the way out of the hall and pinned it back on crooked, while Vexana's never came off. They are new in the hand-in-hand photo.

entries.name: the body's seam

facts.t: The plates of the body's chest meet in one seam, longer than the Academy's tower is tall, with a dim magenta glow.
Vexana follows it from top to bottom twice, as she studies an Ender's chest before it fires.
The healing strands draw back into it.
Vexana stays under the body looking up at the seam and thinks: There.

rel.t: The seam closes the body's chest.

entries.line: The long seam down the chest of the Mother Matrix.
entries.short: The seam where the plates of the body's chest meet. It is longer than the Academy's tower is tall, with a dim magenta glow.
entries.summary: The plates of the Mother Matrix's chest meet in one seam, longer than the Academy's tower is tall, with a dim magenta glow along it. Vexana follows it from top to bottom twice, the way she studies an Ender's chest before it fires. Healing strands come out of it and draw back into it. Before she goes, she looks up at the seam once more and thinks: There.

entries.name: the brass plaque

facts.t: It reads WITH THANKS TO THE PATRONS OF SELRICK ACADEMY and lists the families who gave money, with HOUSE BAROQUE first.
Under it two cadets once said Guinevere's score was bought.

rows: Above the fountain in the Academy courtyard

rel.t: It hangs above the fountain.

entries.line: The patrons' plaque above the Academy fountain.
entries.short: A brass plaque over the courtyard fountain: WITH THANKS TO THE PATRONS OF SELRICK ACADEMY. HOUSE BAROQUE comes first.
entries.summary: A brass plaque on the wall above the fountain in the Academy courtyard. It reads WITH THANKS TO THE PATRONS OF SELRICK ACADEMY and lists the families who gave money, with HOUSE BAROQUE first. Guinevere sees it in her first week and thinks her father paid for this too. Under it, two cadets once said her score was bought.

entries.name: the clocks

facts.t: They hung on every wall of the shop, each out of step with the next, so the house ticked day and night.
When the power went out, the hand-wound clocks kept ticking and struck one o'clock out of step.
After the roof fell, a clock still ticked somewhere under the beams, and Lesley could not find it.
The station had no clocks, and Lesley lay awake listening for ticking.

rel.t: They filled the house.

entries.line: The clocks that filled Lesley's childhood home.
entries.short: The clocks Lesley's father mends. They hang on every wall of his shop, each out of step, so the house ticks day and night.
entries.summary: Lesley's father mended small machines, mostly clocks. They hung on every wall of his shop, each out of step with the next, so the house ticked day and night. When the power went out on the night of the attack, the ones he wound by hand kept ticking and struck one o'clock out of step. After the roof fell, one still ticked under the beams, and Lesley could not find it. At the station she lay awake listening for ticking.

entries.name: the cloth bag

facts.t: Vexana carries her father's toolbox in it on her shoulder.
It clinks when she sets it down.
Guinevere notices she carries it everywhere; Vexana says it holds tools.

entries.line: Vexana's shoulder bag, with her father's toolbox inside.
entries.short: The cloth bag on Vexana's shoulder. Her father's old toolbox rides in it.
entries.summary: A cloth bag Vexana carries on her shoulder. Her father's old soldier's toolbox rides in it, heavy, and it clinks when she sets it down. Guinevere notices she carries it everywhere. Vexana only says it holds tools.

entries.name: the cloth over the bench

facts.t: After her mother hides the eye drawings from Lesley under a mug, Chang'e keeps a cloth by the bench.
When Lesley's footsteps come early, Chang'e throws the cloth over the bench and folds her hands on top of it.
Lesley asks what is under it, and Chang'e says nothing regulation.
When Lesley receives the eye, she understands that the eye was what lay under the cloth.

rel.t: It hides the eye while Chang'e builds it.

entries.line: The cloth Chang'e throws over her bench to hide her work.
entries.short: A cloth Chang'e keeps by her bench, so Lesley never sees what she is building.
entries.summary: After her mother hid the eye drawings from Lesley under a mug, Chang'e kept a cloth by her bench. When Lesley's footsteps came early one night, Chang'e threw it over the bench and folded her hands on top. Lesley asked what was under it, and Chang'e said nothing regulation. When Lesley received her new eye, she understood that the eye was what had lain under the cloth.

entries.name: the cloth tape

facts.t: Vexana left a roll of it on Guinevere's jacket, the kind she winds on her staff's grip.
Guinevere taped her knuckles with it and never found out who had left it.
Vexana sees her own roll's tape on Guinevere's hand.
Guinevere sees the same gray tape on Vexana's practice staff and knows who left it.
The night Guinevere waited at her father's office, a roll of Vexana's tape turned up on her jacket.

entries.line: A roll of gray cloth tape left on Guinevere's jacket.
entries.short: A roll of gray cloth tape, the kind Vexana winds on her staff's grip. She leaves it on Guinevere's jacket without a sound.
entries.summary: The cloth tape is a roll of the gray tape Vexana winds on her staff's grip. The night Guinevere waited at her father's office, Vexana left it on her jacket without a sound. Guinevere taped her knuckles with it and did not know who had left it, until she saw the same gray tape on Vexana's practice staff.

entries.name: the coat

facts.t: Guinevere came out of the third shop with a coat over her arm and put it in Vexana's hands.
Vexana's own coat was worn shiny at the cuffs, so Guinevere meant to replace it.
Vexana thinks a coat is a debt.
On the roof Guinevere admits the coat she picked was very ugly.

entries.line: The coat Guinevere bought for Vexana.
entries.short: A coat Guinevere buys for Vexana, whose own coat is worn shiny at the cuffs.
entries.summary: Guinevere came out of the third shop with a coat over her arm and put it in Vexana's hands, because Vexana's own coat was worn shiny at the cuffs. To Vexana a coat was a debt, and so was everything anyone gave you. She sent it back with the other gifts. Later, on the roof, Guinevere admitted the coat she picked was very ugly.

entries.name: the Combat office board
aka: the board outside the Combat office

facts.t: By evening it says VEXANA: MISSING, in the same type as a roster. Guinevere stands before it with two fingers at her collar.

rel.t: It hangs outside the Combat office.

entries.line: The roster board outside the Combat office.
entries.short: The board outside the Combat office. After Vexana is taken, it says VEXANA: MISSING in the same type as a roster.
entries.summary: The board that hangs outside the Combat office, where rosters and duty sheets go up. The watch sheet for the Investigation Room once hung there. By the evening Vexana was taken, it said VEXANA: MISSING in the same type as a roster, and Guinevere stood in front of it with two fingers at her collar.

entries.name: the command channel

facts.t: Lesley keys it and orders all posts to report.
Lesley does not know why it holds under the storm.
The posts go out over it.
Voices come over it one on top of another.
The word "Traitor" goes down it faster than any order.
It goes silent when Guinevere's signal is lost.
It breaks its silence when the west ward asks what took the shot.
Guinevere's line on it is open, and Layla hears every word.
Vexana's farewell came over Guinevere's open line into Fanny's ear.
That morning the word 'traitor' went down it.
Vexana has no comm, so Guinevere lends her the one from her own ear.
It still works under the field.
Lesley says comms hold while suits don't.
Its green light stays on on the deck.
Since the charge it has carried Guinevere's laugh.
Guinevere loses her earpiece, and the channel with it, in her fall.

entries.line: The radio channel the Academy's defense runs on.
entries.short: The radio channel Lesley uses to order every post. It holds under the storm, and she does not know why.
entries.summary: The command channel carries Lesley's orders and every post's report during the attack. It holds under the storm, and under Obsidia's field too: comms hold while suits do not. The word traitor went down it faster than any order, and it went silent when Guinevere's signal was lost. Guinevere's line stayed open, so Vexana's farewell came into Fanny's ear, and later Guinevere lent Vexana the comm from her own ear. Guinevere loses her earpiece, and the channel with it, in her fall.

entries.name: the convoy

facts.t: After the attack the last truck leaves for the far stations, and Lesley hides on it.
The sergeant says the next convoy back is months away.
It comes at the turn of the season, carrying the soldiers' letters, and Lesley hides so it leaves without her.
Later new badges come to her by convoy.

rel.t: It links the Shield's stations to the city.

entries.line: The Shield's supply trucks between the city and its far stations.
entries.short: The Shield's trucks to the far stations. After the attack Lesley hides on the last one out of the city.
entries.summary: The Shield's convoys link the city with its far stations. After the attack on her street, Lesley hid on the last truck out. The sergeant said the next convoy back was months away. When it came at the turn of the season with the soldiers' letters, she hid under the armory floor so it left without her. Later her new badges came to her by convoy.

entries.name: the core component

facts.t: When Lesley's round cracks a core at the edge, one piece splits off before the burn reaches it and lies whole: a core component, from deep inside the machine.
It is dull when Lesley carries it back in her fist.
For eleven days the needles lie flat when current and heat are run through it.
By the lab's rule it is lifted only with tongs or gloves.
On the twelfth evening, held in Chang'e's bare hands, a small pale light wakes in it.
Its light thins while Lesley is late and flares when she comes back.
In tests its needle climbs when Chang'e thinks of Lesley and drops when she does sums.
Chang'e concludes it responds to what she believes, and only while she holds on.
It is set in a wire cage in the frame's chest.
It makes Lesley the Shield's most valuable shot; Headquarters calls it a miracle.
Lesley wonders if the Enders came for the piece; she does not know.

rows: A wire cage in the frame's chest

rel.t: Her shot breaks it off whole.
A piece of an Ender's core.
Its heart, in a wire cage.

entries.line: A whole piece of an Ender's core that Lesley brings back.
entries.short: A piece that split off whole when Lesley's round cracked an Ender's core at the edge. Nobody had thought it could be done.
entries.summary: The core component is a piece from deep inside an Ender's core. Lesley's round cracked a core at the edge, and this piece split away before the burn reached it. For eleven days it stayed dull under every test, until on the twelfth evening, held in Chang'e's bare hands, a small pale light woke in it. It responds to what Chang'e believes, and only while she holds on. Set in a wire cage in the frame's chest, it makes Lesley the Shield's most valuable shot.

entries.name: the Council's control unit

facts.t: Every Project Angel body carries a sealed plate between the shoulder blades, the size of Ruby's palm, with the Council's seal burned in and one small dark light.
Asked to unlock it, the console says: "That part belongs to the Council."
Ruby never learns what it does and builds around it.
Its light never comes on, even after Angela goes down and comes back. Ruby does not know what that means.
A plate on Angela's back that Ruby was never allowed to open. Through it the Council took Angela's mind.
It sits between her shoulder blades. Its small light burns red on Dawnbreak; it had been dark on Oro.

Vexana lights it by laying her palm on its chest over the heart. Its yellow eyes light and its heart blazes magenta.
She knows each of its plates by the dents her hammer left.
Its plate is purple edged in gold, with a magenta heart crest on its chest. It waits folded and dark behind a chimney.
It drops out of the smoke between the wall and the Matrix's beam with its arms up.
It leans into the beam and holds while the light melts the road around it.
Its eyes go dark one after the other.
Vexana sees through its eyes from inside.
It ran on her belief and spent all of it on one block.
Its plates fused at the seams, and Vexana cracked the chest plate open to get out.
It kneels against the wall, dark, its chest plate split down the middle and the edges bent outward.
Vexana lit it, went inside its open heart, and dropped it into the light.
It kneels cracked against a wall three streets west, and no light rises there.
Obsidia recalls a machine of Ender plates that stood in front of the body's beam; it had stayed dead under her hand in the hollow, but a human's belief lit it.

entries.line: The first Eternal Guard, a giant Vexana built from Ender plates.
entries.short: The first of Vexana's Eternal Guards, a giant she built from Ender plates. It woke when she thought of Guinevere: eyes yellow, heart blazing magenta.
entries.summary: The first of Vexana's four Eternal Guards. She built it in the hollow from plates bought in sacks, purple edged in gold, around a dark cracked core. Its chest plate, beaten to fit, came out shaped like a heart, with room behind it for her. It woke when she laid her palm on it and thought of Guinevere, and stayed dark under Obsidia's hand. When the Matrix fired at Guinevere, it dropped into the beam and held while the road melted. It spent all of Vexana's belief on that one block. Now it kneels dark against a wall, its chest split down the middle.

Hester drove Guinevere back to the Academy in it in silence.
Vexana remembers Hester's coat at its wheel.
It stands behind Hester with its back door open.
Guinevere rode in it to the Academy gate on the morning of the assessment.
After Guinevere walks away, no car door shuts and no engine starts.

entries.line: House Baroque's long car, driven by Hester.
entries.short: A long car driven by Hester in her gray coat. It brings Guinevere to the Academy gate.
entries.summary: The long car of House Baroque, driven by Hester in her gray coat. It brought Guinevere to the Academy gate on the morning of the assessment, and Hester drove her back in it in silence after her father's answer. When Hester comes with word that Guinevere must come home, the car waits behind her with its back door open. Guinevere walks away, and no car door shuts and no engine starts.

entries.name: the napkin of load numbers

entries.summary: At supper Chang'e's father asked Lesley how much a soldier can carry and still run. She said thirty kilos, twenty if she has to run far. He wrote it on his napkin and folded it into his pocket, and he kept it. While he built the first suit frame, it hung on a nail above the scale where he weighed every plate.

Lesley wanted it on top of the old action instead. Chang'e left it on Lesley's cot, and at dawn Lesley fitted it there, along the barrel, new and bright at the seams. Under Obsidia's field it goes cold. At the end it wakes and comes up to the note Chang'e tuned it to.

entries.name: the nightgown

facts.t: Obsidia took it from a dead woman and dressed the sleeping child in it. The hem fell past the child's bare feet.

entries.short: A nightgown Obsidia takes from a dead woman to dress the sleeping child. Its hem falls past the child's bare feet.
entries.summary: A nightgown Obsidia took from a dead woman on the night of the strike. With her own hands she dressed the sleeping child she had made in it, and its hem fell past the child's bare feet. Then she laid the child on the scorched ground and left before the rain could wake her.

entries.name: the old servo

It was mended with a trick Chang'e had never seen.
Chang'e buys it for every coin in her pockets and two jelly candies; it stands on the shelf above the bench, still turning its arm.
It stands in a little wire stand on the shelf in Chang'e's lab, its arm turning back and forth, one corner still black.
Selena found it under a fallen rack in a roofless storehouse at the base's ruins, with a strip of label tape in a small quick hand.
She found the crack where the current stopped and mended it by morning.
It sat on the corner of her salvage table as her sign, priced so high that nobody ever bought it.
Chang'e reads the label tape and says it came from her parents' lab.
Chang'e buys it with coins and two jelly candies.
It still turns its arm back and forth in its stand.

entries.summary: A small servo that turns its arm back and forth. Selena found it under a fallen rack in a roofless storehouse at the research base's ruins, found the crack where the current stopped, and mended it by morning. It sat on the corner of her salvage table as her sign, priced so high nobody bought it. Chang'e read her mother's small quick hand on its label tape and knew it came from her parents' lab. She paid every coin in her pockets and two jelly candies. It stands on her lab's shelf, one corner still black, still turning its arm.

entries.summary: The rifle Lesley carried as a Shield soldier before Chang'e built her a new one. One night she came back from the city's edge with mud to her knees, and the tape on its stock hung in strips. Watching her, Chang'e thought that if Lesley could hit them from farther away, the Enders could not reach her.

A red ring on her panel closes over the glow as Lesley locks on.

Through them she read the giant's shut chest and saw that the light behind its plates was the door in. A red ring on her panel closed over the glow as Lesley locked on.

After she approved Selena she set it face up again and sat up most of the night with it. When anyone comes in, she still turns it face down.

Joe picked it up and put it back in her arms, and it fell when Fanny scooped the girl up. That evening Fanny pulled it out of the ash, beat it clean and set it on the broken wall facing the avenue, where a mother coming back would see it.

entries.summary: Vexana's practice staff, its grip wound in gray cloth tape. She trains with it every night without a sound, up in the gallery of the training hall where the lamp never reaches. She does fifty forms with it and lowers it at the fiftieth.

entries.name: the purple

facts.t: Selena carries Ender cells in her blood.
A thin purple seam draws a cut in her palm shut.
Purple threads come up out of a cut and draw its edges together like a needle.
On the roof she lets it come up along her arms and calls it back. It always obeys, and the lightning hides its glow.
Once she lets it run up to her shoulders.
On storm nights she spreads it over her arms and legs and races the city like a shadow.
It runs off her fingertips into Frame Nine's core and wakes it.
In heavy rain she lets it spread over her collarbones and throat; every ward camera shows only white.
She lets it up on her left side only, and pale plates rise through it at the wrist and shoulder.

rows: Thin purple threads and seams; pale plates rise through it at wrist and shoulder

rel.t: It is in her blood.

entries.line: The purple Ender tissue in Selena's blood.
entries.short: Ender cells in Selena's blood. When she is cut, purple threads come up and draw the edges shut like a needle.
entries.summary: Selena carries Ender cells in her blood. When she is cut, purple threads come up and draw the edges together like a needle. She can call it up along her arms and send it back, and it always obeys. On storm nights she spreads it over her arms and legs and races the city like a shadow. In heavy rain she lets it reach her throat, and every ward camera shows only white. It ran off her fingertips into Frame Nine's core and woke it. When she lets it up on one side, pale plates rise through it.

entries.name: the radio

facts.t: On her father's bench, it is where Lesley first heard the word Enders.
Her father left it on low at night, saying it was for the weather.
On the night of the attack it stopped in the middle of a word.

entries.short: The radio on Lesley's father's bench, where she first hears the word Enders.
entries.summary: The radio stood on Lesley's father's bench in the shop. The first time she heard the word Enders, it came out of it: giants, far away, that came in groups and broke cities. Her father began leaving it on low at night, saying it was for the weather. On the night of the attack it stopped in the middle of a word.

entries.name: the returned shopping bags

She sent back a whole coat, every bag folded.

entries.line: The gifts Vexana sent back, every bag folded.
entries.short: The pile of shopping bags Vexana sends back, with a note in small square letters: I cannot repay this.
entries.summary: After their day of shopping, Vexana folded every gift back the way the shop had folded it and sent the whole pile back, coat and all. On top she left a note in small square letters: I cannot repay this. To her a coat was a debt, and so was everything anyone gave you.

entries.summary: A lamp Chang'e built to clip onto a rifle, her first gift for Lesley. Lesley turned it over in her hand and gave it back: not regulation. Chang'e decided she would make it regulation.

entries.name: the ring of light

Ruby's scythe stops short of the light, and the child inside the ring is unhurt.
Selrick's record ends with the ring of light closing around the child.

entries.summary: Angela's power. Light flies from her palm and closes around a person in a glowing ring with two pointed ears, like a cat's head, and lifts them into the air. When Ruby's scythe came down, it stopped short of the light, and the child inside was unhurt. Selrick's record of that day ends with the ring closing around the child.

entries.name: the scorched Aspirant suit

Vexana watched two feeders drag it from a ditch in the dead ground. The hand that was left was still a fist.
It lies on a slab on the Citadel's prow with Obsidia's palm over its dark, cracked core.
A violet hum from Obsidia's hand sinks into its core, where a pilot's belief once lit it, and goes no further.
Its plates stay dark and silent. Only the core answers with a faint tick, like metal cooling.
Obsidia says it is the first human machine she has held.
The core ticks once more and goes still.
A dead suit sits on Obsidia's prow, one of the sources her field grew from.
Its core is where a pilot's belief once burned. Obsidia tested the field on it for weeks.

One of the Academy's suits.
She holds the suit on her prow and studies it.
It sits on the prow.

entries.line: A dead Academy suit dragged from a ditch in the dead ground.

entries.summary: An Aspirant suit from the Academy, scorched black, one arm gone, its shoulder plate stamped S·L·K. Someone had fought out in the dead ground and never come back, and the hand that was left was still a fist. Vexana watched two feeders, Enders that carry metal home, drag it from a ditch. Later it lies on a slab on the Storm Citadel's prow. Obsidia holds her palm over its cracked core, which she says is the first human machine she has held, and her hum goes no further. She tested her field on it for weeks.

entries.summary: A seedling under a glass dome in Layla's lab. It is the only thing there she did not build, and she checks it last. In time it opens three leaves. Later, when she says she is not interested in the outside world, Layla does not let herself think about three small leaves under a glass dome.

entries.name: the Shield's notice

facts.t: A notice from the Shield of Dawnbreak on what to do in a raid.

entries.summary: A notice from the Shield of Dawnbreak on the wall inside the city library, on what to do in a raid. It says Enders are living machines, a gray metal shell over living purple tissue. It warns people not to hide behind a downed Ender, since Enders do not attack each other and will walk around their own. Reading it, young Selena learns the rule: they do not hit their own.

Obsidia rests her clawed glove on its edge and says nothing about it. Vexana takes it for one more shell that broke and was cleared away.

entries.name: the small flying craft

Its caption reads: "The Storm Citadel. Concealed within storm clouds, it can unleash devastating electromagnetic interference over large areas."
A shaking film from the Academy's oldest records, of a ship of black blades over a city in a red sky, with storm readings taken with it.
Chang'e lays the day's readings over its readings, and the two lines sit one on top of the other.
Chang'e names the Storm Citadel as the ship from it.
Fanny saw it as a shaking film in Joe's class.
In it every machine under the Citadel's storm died.
Lesley says the field is not the storm from the records.

entries.summary: A shaking film from the oldest records Selrick Academy keeps. A ship of black blades hangs over a city in a red sky, smaller ships swarm around it, and Enders drop onto the roofs. Its caption reads: "The Storm Citadel. Concealed within storm clouds, it can unleash devastating electromagnetic interference over large areas." In it every machine under the storm died. Joe shows it in class. Later Chang'e lays the day's readings over the film's, and the two lines match. Lesley says the field is not the storm from the records.

entries.name: the table of suits

entries.summary: Vexana's staff has an orb above the grip. It spits bolts at Enders, and when she raises it a great arrow of violet light falls from high above. At the team test the grip split and the orb went dark, until she fitted a brass collar over the split with her father's screwdriver. In the void the orb turned black, but the collar stayed brass. Woken with "Dark night, swallow all things," it blasts out without a sound. A great spell from it once threw Guinevere off the platform. Under Obsidia's field its orb gives no light, and she wields it like a pole.

text: Chang'e first sees Angela on the Academy's record of the landing: a small pink-haired android firing at students a beat late. She watches that one longest and, for once, says nothing. When Ruby and Angela ask refuge, she looks at Angela a long moment and sets four conditions. The first is that the android comes to her lab for an examination.

In the lab Chang'e questions Angela the way she would question a machine, and Angela answers in a small, careful voice. The Council's control unit is gone, but Chang'e cannot prove there is no other door. "She stays on checks." Ruby's locked code goes on her list, and so does the doll, until Ruby cuts its link to Oro.

A fault in Angela's chest comes whenever she thinks of the friends she lost, and she does not want it fixed. Chang'e says "Noted," and leaves it. Defending Mr. Bunny from Ruby a moment later, she hears that she has said it to the girl whose best friend she just put on a list, and writes WEEKLY beside the lock anyway. ties.t: She examines Angela and keeps her on checks.

text: In burning Terrinia a small child hides in a barrel at the end of an avenue, with a Selrick boy in a red tie standing guard in front of it. Ruby, red-eyed with rage, knocks the boy aside, and the child crouches in the dust and cries. It looks up at her, face wet, as she raises her scythe.

Angela has just woken on the stones thirty meters away, the Council's plate gone from her back. She cannot cross the distance in time. She flings out her hand, and a glowing ring with two pointed ears closes around the child and lifts it out of the blade's path, with Tetra shining pink above it.

Then Angela cries, "Ruby!" The red goes out of Ruby's eye, and the scythe stops in the air, short of the light. Ruby lowers it herself. Inside the ring the child is unhurt. Later the Academy's cameras show the moment, and Lesley freezes the frame on the scythe over the child.

At lunch, when Layla doubted the star, Angela said, "I came back once. People come back."

At the Singularity, Guinevere came low across the water with Enders swarming her, and Angela opened a pane in her shield and pulled her through. Guinevere's star was blazing. Angela opened a pane wide enough for one and sent her on: "Go, Guinevere, pursue your light."

I only said they were funny in the head." Chang'e seats the two in the third-year class beside the pair who vouched. "Beside us?" says Layla.

Under the Singularity, Angela holds a bell of pink light around the four of them on a broken seawall. Enders press on it from every side, and each blow costs her a little. Layla stands on a slab in the middle with the cannon on her shoulder and calls the targets. Angela opens a pane in the shield, Layla's shot goes through, and Angela closes it before the next claw falls.

Soon the panes open before anyone asks. "Funny in the head," Layla mutters at Ruby and Angela, lining up again. "Both of you. The pane's open before I ask." "Thank you!" says Angela. Layla fires instead of answering.

text: Lesley first sees Angela on the Academy's record of the landing: a small pink-haired android walking through smoke with light in her hand, firing at students a beat late. At the end a ring of light closes around a child under Ruby's scythe, and Lesley freezes the frame.

Days later a black ship lands at the dome's foot, and Angela softly asks the soldiers if they mean to take her back. Lesley comes down off her roof. She has watched the record, raised scythe and all, and she lets the two in under watch.

In the Academy hall Lesley stands before four girls in combat suits, Angela with her doll clipped at her hip. "Ruby, Angela: you are Aspirants as of today. The four of you stand together." She tells them they still do not fully understand their own power, but by trusting each other they can gain limitless strength.

text: Ruby, heir to the Decisionmaker of Planet Oro, built Angela for the Council as its weapon. She built the body and wrote the mind herself. In it she hid a trojan as her way off Oro, since the Council would need Angela's creator to shut her down. Angela woke and told her, "You must be what humans call 'a friend'!" Heirs could not have friends.

On Terrinia the Council drove Angela through a plate on her back. Ruby tore it out, and Angela went limp. Ruby fell into a red-eyed rage and raised her scythe over a child. Angela woke and called her back, and Ruby's eye went blue. "You created me. You set me free," Angela told her. Angela said how she felt about Ruby was the one thing she knew was real. Then they fought a giant Ender together, shield and scythe.

They escaped Oro and became Aspirants at Selrick. Ruby said she pulled the control unit out so Angela would be safe, and Angela trusted Ruby with her doll. Later Ruby showed Angela the hidden code that could still stop her, and let her choose. Angela chose, and Ruby deleted it. Angela said she wanted to protect everyone, and smiled back at Ruby.

At the Singularity Ruby stood at Angela's side, her eye blue, and Angela told her people come back. In the Storm Citadel's attack Obsidia's field put out the shield, and Angela took a claw on her back for a soldier. The old rage came up in Ruby. She made one cut into the Ender's core, no more, and her eyes stayed blue. "I made that elbow," she said. "I can mend it." Then she stood between the next Ender and Angela.

text: At the end of the year, in Chang'e's classroom, a boy in the second row keeps asking what her words mean. When she gives the oldest records' rule, that a planet that holds Balance sends the Enders against a people grown too strong, he asks, "Balance?" She tells him: everything kept in check, nothing allowed to grow too big.

When she says the Enders' Control Core must be destroyed, he asks, "Their what?" Whatever steers them all, she says. When she mentions a paper on black holes, he asks, "A what?" She tells him it is a place in space so heavy it swallows whatever comes too near, and that nothing seen falling in has ever come back out, not even light.

text: Before Selrick Academy opens, Selena roams the city on storm nights with the purple spread over her arms and legs. One night after a raid she hears crying under the rain. A shop front has come down, and a small boy lies in the street with its iron shutter across his leg. Two streets off, the rescue lamps are moving away. She calls the purple back under her skin and climbs down.

The shutter feels light under her hand, light enough to press down instead. She lifts it, though two grown men could not have shifted it, and whispers, "Shh. It won't hurt anymore." She stands him up and turns him toward the lamps: "That way. Shout." He limps off shouting, and the lamps turn toward him. Three roofs later she is still asking herself why, and decides it was nothing.

text: Chang'e's father was one of the two chief scientists of Terrinia's research base. He and Chang'e's mother brought her there before she could walk properly and raised her as their daughter. She called him Dad. He was a quiet man who counted by ear, and his hands set the smallest parts of Lesley's eye.

On the night the base fell, his voice stayed calm. "Stay close, Chang'e," he said, and counted the steps to the shelter. Then a black-and-gold giant turned its light on the yard. He and Chang'e's mother shoved her clear and stood in front of her. When she could see again, the crater where they stood was empty.

Later Chang'e comes out of a side door of the Academy hall, where Layla is scrubbing the floor in detention, and grins at them all with her whole face: "Great job, guys!" Layla's eyes go to the new coil on Lesley's rifle behind her. Science Division work, she thinks, and she wants it in pieces on her desk.

At the end of that year Layla sits at the front of Chang'e's class, alone. Asked who sends the Enders, she says nobody knows. Then she asks the hard questions first: endanger who, how anyone knows something steers the Enders, and how to get to the void. To the last, Chang'e has to say she does not know yet.

text: Lesley came to Terrinia's research base as a young Shield soldier, sent to guard it. Its small genius, Chang'e, named her Sis: her word for a girl who protects her. Lesley pulled her clear of a falling rack, and carried her to bed when she fell asleep at the bench. Chang'e built Lesley an eye for her birthday, and then her rifle.

Lesley promised to be back for the first light. It was the first promise she had made since her brother died. She came back from a secret mission too late. Chang'e's parents had died pushing her clear, and Chang'e pushed Lesley away and blamed her for years. Years later Lesley fired from a lit window to save her, and they fought side by side until dawn. The Academy would call them the First Aspirants.

Chang'e held on to her coat and called her Big Sis again. Chang'e proposed the Academy, and they ran its entrance assessment together: Lesley asked the questions, Chang'e read the needle. At Selrick, Lesley counts Chang'e's hours of sleep and makes her take her pill. "I hate scary Big Sis!" says Chang'e, and swallows it. On the command deck, at the Singularity, she still calls her Big Sis.

In the Storm Citadel's attack an Ender bent over Chang'e at her console. Chang'e sat still so it would strike and open its chest, and told Lesley to hold her fire for the call. Lesley held, then made the shot. This time Chang'e did not push her away. Lesley said her vow aloud at last: "Ever since that day, I vowed to keep you safe, Chang'e."

text: Chang'e built Mr. Bunny as a friend when she was small, in the evenings at the end of her parents' bench. He is a white ball with long ears, and his face is a black screen, so he can make faces. He fetched whatever she pointed at while she built Lesley's rifle.

Chang'e calls him her best friend. When Ruby wanted to read his code, Chang'e said she would not let anyone take him away. He floats at her shoulder wherever she goes: in class, in the field, on the command deck. Once, on an avenue, he came at her call as a great white rabbit-head machine taller than the storefronts, and the Enders broke against him.

In the Storm Citadel's attack, Chang'e planned for an Ender to strike at her so its chest would open. "Mr. Bunny takes the hit," she said. He swung in front of her face and took the claw meant for her. He came back dented, one ear crooked, until his screen found its smile and he floated back to her shoulder.

text: The researcher works at the research base where Chang'e grows up. When he finds her at the big bench, standing on a box, he tells her it is for grown-ups and sends her back to her corner. After he sees the frame's first light, he looks from her to the cage. "The big bench is yours."

On the night the base falls, he carries Chang'e in from the yard and puts his own coat round her. In the nights after, he brings her soup and tells her of a home in the city, with beds and someone who cooks. She asks who would finish the frame. "It won't bring them back," he says. He never says "home" again, but he keeps bringing food.

He never leaves the base. Years later, when the Academy rises over the crater, Chang'e goes to him first for the Science Division's professors, and he becomes the first of them. Then she calls back the rest of her parents' old team.

text: "Good morning, Teacher Chang'e," says Ruby in her perfect voice, and brings Angela to the lab for her examination. Chang'e finds the empty socket where the Council's control unit was. Ruby pulled it out. Then Chang'e finds forty locked lines marked DANGER. Ruby says they are hers, a safeguard to stop Angela if Oro ever takes her again. Chang'e puts the lock on her list. "Then put me on the list too," says Ruby sweetly.

Ruby cuts the doll's live link to Oro in four seconds. Chang'e once spent a week cutting a link like that. When Ruby asks to read Mr. Bunny's code in turn, Chang'e refuses: he is her best friend. Then she hears what she has said, to the girl whose best friend she has just put on a list. She writes WEEKLY beside the lock anyway.

After Vexana goes missing, Chang'e cannot find the door Guinevere asks for. She sends her to Ruby, who comes each morning for Angela's check: "She does in four seconds what takes me a week." That morning Ruby deletes the lock, because Angela chooses it, and Chang'e draws a line through the last entry on her list. "Neat code. Shame to delete it." "Not really," says Ruby.

text: Years after the base fell, its alarm goes again, and Chang'e goes out with her crescents. At the foot of the avenue a pair of iron doors stands open in the seawall: a shelter. A man runs past her with a small girl on his hip, and a woman beside them holds the girl's hand. The girl has her eyes shut. Chang'e counts their steps without meaning to. At ten they are through the doors.

The warden shouts at her to get in. Chang'e says she will definitely protect everyone, and takes her place in front of the doors. Behind her they bang shut, and the bar drops. She holds them even after her ring breaks, until Lesley comes. When the giant falls across the top of the avenue, nobody is under it. Everyone from those streets is behind the iron doors.

Then an Ender dragged Vexana into that dark. In the Storm Citadel she put Chang'e's rule to Obsidia: who gave a planet the right? In the hollow she told Obsidia, "Our teacher said nobody can get near this dark." "Your teacher was right," said Obsidia. The Will opens every door into it, and Obsidia opens her own.

text: Chang'e's father and mother are the two chief scientists of Terrinia's research base. They brought Chang'e there before she could walk, and raised her as their daughter and their best student. In the lab they work side by side with their backs to the room. He turns an Ender plate with one hand in his pocket and counts by ear. She writes with a mug in her free hand and says "Bed." He slides Chang'e a circuit board, which means she can stay.

They keep Chang'e's secrets the same quiet way. When she builds an eye for Lesley, he sets its smallest parts with his tweezers and does not ask whose it is. She sets her mug down over the drawings when Lesley's steps pass the door. She sets a fourth plate at supper for Lesley. When the core piece lights in Chang'e's hands, she says, "A guess is not a claim. Test it." They test it together at their bench, and he writes one result down himself.

He bends steel tube into the frame of the first suit. She pins her notes to its foot: For whoever has to stand in front. When Lesley leaves on a secret mission, they walk her to the gate together, and she promises to keep setting her plate. "He counts too," she says of the days Lesley is gone. "He just won't say so." On the evening the light holds, her voice cracks, and between them they lift Chang'e up, the way they hold her in the photograph on the bench.

Then the alarm. He tells Chang'e to stay close, and she does up Chang'e's top button and takes her hand. His arm goes round her shoulders as they run, he counting the steps, she calling Lesley on the radio. When the black-and-gold giant opens its chest, his arm comes away, and they turn to face it together. They shove Chang'e clear, one from each side, and stand in its light. The crater where they stood is empty.

text: Chang'e's father is one of the research base's two chief scientists, a quiet man who eats in silence. The Shield sends Lesley, its best young shot, to keep him, Chang'e's mother and the child they took in alive.

text: At the breach of the dome, a little girl in a red dress stands crying on the pavement while people run around her. Professor Joe gives back her pink rabbit and covers her from a falling slab. Then a gold giant lowers its head through the broken dome, and the girl walks out into the avenue alone, her face turned up. The light in its chest grows.

Fanny sees her from the air. She drops and scoops the girl onto her left hip, the Shield's way, and the rabbit falls. "I'm flying!" says the girl. "Flying feels great," says Fanny, before the Shield part of her can stop it. The beam burns the place where the girl stood. Fanny leaves her behind a van, and her mother runs to her.

On the day of the Storm Citadel's attack, Fanny takes the bay road at roof height on her cable. The wind tears at her hair. Once she told a little girl on her hip that flying felt great. It still does. She grins, and for once the Shield part of her lets it be.

ties.t: She carries the girl out of the giant's path.

text: On the morning of the Mother Matrix's attack, Fanny stands in the courtyard ranks beside Guinevere, under the billboard of Guinevere and Vexana back to back. The star at Guinevere's collar beeps, the pair's sound, which Fanny has not heard in weeks. "Guinevere?" says Fanny. On a roof stands a dark figure with a staff, Enders all around it. "That's her," Guinevere whispers.

The Shield soldiers swing their rifles up at the roof. Guinevere closes her mouth, and when the figure jumps she flies after it alone, without an order. Fanny has never once left her post without one. Still her first thought is that Guinevere must be in danger. She drops the Shield's way for Layla's map and tells Layla, "Lead."

In the Storm Citadel's attack the field kills Guinevere's drones and wings. In the bay road cut she breaks an Ender's core with her bare fist, and Vexana pulls her back through the gap in the wall. Fanny, holding the gap with plain steel, looks at Guinevere's side and her split knuckles. Then she moves to its edge and gives her the middle. "You saw it," Fanny calls along the wall. "Like that."

text: Fanny came to Selrick two years late, from the Shield. On her first day her time beat Layla's, and Layla, who had never been second, raced her at everything. At a real breach of the dome they argued over who covered whom, then fought back to back on the sand outside it. Layla saw that the Enders were not target practice.

Professor Joe made them the Layla-Fanny Team, with one shared score. Fanny gave Layla a box of chocolate: "This is for you, my teammate!" They held a ward together against a giant, and took the west end of the fish market. When Layla told Guinevere her star was only a circuit, and circuits glitch, Fanny said, "Leave her be, Layla."

Since the sand, Layla had gone first on every raid. When Guinevere flew off alone after Vexana, Layla built a rescue map in the time it took Fanny to give one order. Fanny dropped the Shield's way for it. "Lead," she said.

When the Storm Citadel's field killed every suit, they held a wall across the bay road cut, back to back: Fanny with plain steel, Layla counting each Ender's strike. A crying boy asked Layla if Fanny was her friend. "She's my teammate," said Layla. Fanny said she was not doing it alone.

But by trusting each other, we can gain limitless strength." In the Storm Citadel's attack she gave the frontline its ground on the channel, and Fanny answered, "Understood."

text: On Fanny's first day at Selrick Academy, her VR assessment puts her in a broken street. A man shouts from under a fallen sign. "Simulated civilians are not scored," says a voice.

"Understood." Fanny pulls him clear first. It costs her eleven seconds. Then she fights the soldiers' way, her back to a narrow alley, and the Enders fall one or two at a time. Even with the eleven seconds, her time of 3:39 goes up above Layla's 3:41 on the rankings board.

text: Professor Joe wears a monocle and teaches the Combat Division. Fanny's first class with him puts her on his Team B3, with Layla and Roger. He teaches them that an Ender opens its chest only when it strikes. His last slide is a shaking recording from the Academy's oldest records: the Storm Citadel, a ship of black blades whose storm kills every machine under it.

At the breach he covers a crying girl and her pink rabbit from a falling slab, and it strikes him across the shoulders. Fanny is the one who then carries that girl out of the gold giant's path. Joe comes back on a cane, dissolves Team B3 and makes Layla and Fanny the Layla-Fanny Team, with one shared score: a kill is a point, a civilian carried clear is ten.

On the day of the Storm Citadel's attack, the ship comes down out of its black cloud over the Academy. Fanny has seen it once before, in a shaking film in Joe's class. Neither the film nor the sight of it coming through the mouth showed her how big it is close up. In the old record every machine under its storm died. She feels for her rig. It is still humming.

text: Roger is the thin boy on Professor Joe's Team B3. He holds the pads while Fanny punches and tells her why Layla is like that: Fanny broke a record nobody had ever broken, on her first day, in front of everyone. "It's a board," says Fanny.

In their first VR drill together, Roger runs two hundred meters of open ground for the spot behind Layla and goes down on his back. An Ender rears over him. Fanny's cable wraps its claw before she has decided anything, and she hauls until it stops a meter above his face. Roger scores 2 kills. When Fanny and Layla argue after, he says, "Enough arguing, guys..." Nobody hears him.
When the siren calls Team B3 to a real breach, Roger does not get up. Fanny lifts him by the collar. "Protecting Terrinia is our duty."

text: Ruby and Angela land off a black ship, and on the lot at the dome's foot the soldiers raise their rifles. Fanny steps in front of the soldiers. She watched the two fight a giant for this city, she says. "I'll answer for them." A sergeant asks on whose word. "Mine." Ruby bows, names herself heir to the Decisionmaker of Planet Oro, in another galaxy, and asks refuge of the school.
Chang'e lets them in on terms: the heir takes the entrance assessment, a droid follows the two everywhere, and they sit in the third-year class beside the two who vouched. "That's fair," says Fanny.

After the Mother Matrix is knocked back, Lesley puts Vexana on the line in her Ender's robe. Ruby leans to Angela: "She did that to us. Watched first. Then let us in." Fanny remembers rifles up at two girls off a black ship, and her own word for them. Now she has watched Vexana fly at the Matrix's chest for this city, and she lets her blade points drop.

text: When Obsidia's field puts out every suit in the Academy district, a small boy is crying in a shelter doorway up the bay road cut. Fanny gets to her feet, sets them the way soldiers taught her, and raises two blades of plain steel. She builds a wall across the cut and holds it.

The boy comes down the street looking for someone and finds the wall instead. He stands behind Layla with his fists against his eyes and takes hold of her uniform. Fanny kneels beside him and speaks low and soft, nothing like her command voice: "Don't be scared kiddo, everything's gonna be alright."

He asks Layla whether Fanny is her friend. Layla says, "She's my teammate," and Fanny looks down at the stones with her ears gone red. Then a soldier with his arm in a sling walks the boy back up the street.

ties.t: She comforts the crying boy.

text: One morning Fanny lands on Layla's back as she crosses the school roof, late for class. Flying is banned on school grounds, but Fanny has allowed herself a little. The two race down the white spiral stairwell, their feet cross on the last turn, and they roll out into the corridor in a heap.

The classroom door stands open. Their teacher waits with folded arms, and every head turns. It is Fanny's first detention, and she asks the teacher what to bring. Detention turns out to be cleaning the Academy hall.

text: Fanny comes from a family of Shield soldiers, and Tigreal is her elder brother. On a ruined rooftop the night of the breach, she tells Layla about him: "An incredible fighter who I respect above anyone else." Since she was a kid she has longed to join him on the battlefield, but she could never quite reach his level. She hoped that if she gave every training her all, she would be good enough to fight beside him one day.
Layla understands then that Fanny was never looking down on her. She was looking past her, at him.

In the Storm Citadel's attack the field kills every suit, and Fanny holds the bay road cut with plain steel. Sitting against a tipped car, she says half to herself, "My brother would have held this street alone." Then she looks along the wall at the soldiers, and up at Layla. "I don't care what Tigreal would have done. I'm not doing it alone." She is not looking past Layla now.

ties.t: Tigreal is her elder brother.

text: Guinevere's father holds the head seat on the board of House Baroque. He lost his wife to the Enders, and Guinevere came to think he answered everything with money: he lost her mother and bought walls. When she brought him her first page of sums, held up to the gap in his office door, it came back with a red mark.

At Selrick she wrote to him every week, with every sum her tutors set, and began every letter with the word Father. He never answered. His seat stayed empty at her trial. When she took the top score, all she got was a cold rebuke: "Stop being so stubborn and focus more on the family business!"

After Vexana was taken, he sent word through Hester: come home, or lose her place in the House. Guinevere did not go. Inside the black hole she told Vexana all of it, and said she would give up being a lady of status and start over rather than back down.

Hester had learned to fight from an old Shield sergeant. One dawn she gave in to Guinevere's pestering and taught her: "Elbow in. Hip first. Hands home after every punch." At the Academy, Guinevere still hit the bag bare-fisted the way Hester had taught her. Hester drove her and watched over her, and clapped alone in her row when Guinevere took the top score.

Hester carries the father's orders without softening them. When she brought word to the gate that Guinevere must come home, Guinevere refused, and Hester reminded her: hands home after every punch. text: On Team-Up Day, the day cadets chose partners, Guinevere and Layla both stood alone. Their eyes met across the courtyard, and neither would walk over to the other. For two years after, they shared classes, and neither ever spoke first. Before the fish-market raid Guinevere spoke first: "You're Layla. I'm the great lady Guinevere. Nobody's introduced us."

After Vexana was taken, Layla told Guinevere that portals don't give people back. When Guinevere flew off alone after Vexana, Layla had a rescue map ready, and Lesley sent her team to Guinevere. Layla had called Vexana a traitor. Now, under the Mother Matrix, she counted angles for her.

Layla's plan drew the Matrix's fire down at Angela's shield, away from Guinevere and Vexana, so its chest would open. "Guinevere," she said on the channel. "When it looks at us, it's yours." The chest opened, and Guinevere and Vexana struck it together.

text: Guinevere and Vexana hold the giants' front beside Lesley's squads the day the black ships land. At the end of the year Lesley pins the Academy's first Aspirant Duo badges on the pair. "Undefeated," she says, and that is the whole speech. At the edge of the stage she smiles, small, and it stays.

When Vexana is taken through a door in the corridor, Lesley comes at a run and turns Guinevere away from the wall she is punching. "There's no time to lament." She hands her a notebook to write down everything she saw, reads every line and folds the pages into her coat. By evening she pins VEXANA: MISSING to the board.

Weeks later a records clerk says the form now reads Killed in action. Lesley tells him there is no body, so no finding, and the file stays Missing. Guinevere asks for a squad to lead. Lesley will give her one for a lead. The star is lit, says Guinevere. "That's a light," says Lesley. "Not a lead." Her eye stays on Guinevere a moment, and then she shuts her office door.

ties.t: She keeps Vexana's file at Missing but will not give Guinevere a squad without a lead.

text: At House Baroque, tutors come to teach the young heiress accounts, contracts and manners. The manners tutor talks all day about "a lady's refinement," by which she means how you hold your back. Guinevere glues the tutor's words to Hester's count of three. The next time she falls, on the terrace steps, she is up before Hester reaches her.

Years later, on a fish-market roof, Guinevere gets back to her feet and calls her fall a lady's refinement. And when Ruby plants her scythe on the dirt by the dome's foot and bows, Guinevere knows that bow at once. A manners tutor had spent years on hers.

ties.t: The tutor taught Guinevere her bow.

text: On the fish-market raid Guinevere's wings go out around the thirtieth minute, and Vexana catches her by the wrist at a roof's edge. When the last Ender lies among the fish, a medic takes that wrist to tape it.

While the medic is still taping, Vexana goes back through the portal ahead of the others with Guinevere's lost drone. That night Guinevere lies in bed with her wrist taped. It throbs where Vexana's hand closed on it.

text: Guinevere was the pink-haired girl from Professor Joe's class. At the breach of the dome she fought up close with her fists and drones, with Vexana above her. On the day of the fish-market raid, Joe, still on his cane, sent Guinevere and Vexana to the east end.

In the bay road cut, with no drones and no wings, Guinevere hit an Ender's chest a moment too late: the plates had shut while she ducked. She remembered Joe's lesson. They don't strike easily, and when one does, that is how long you get.

ties.t: She is the pink-haired girl from Joe's class.

text: After Vexana is dragged into the dark, Chang'e sends Guinevere to Ruby. Guinevere waits in the lab doorway while Ruby deletes Angela's hidden code. Then she holds out her gold star. It beeps when Vexana is close, and she wants it to say where. Ruby runs green lines into the gold. "It has no direction, Guinevere. It only says yes."

At night Guinevere climbs to the observation lab in the Academy's tower, where Ruby and Angela keep the sensor array running, and searches the sky through the telescope. The first two nights they ask her to leave. On the third night nobody asks. She fills the night log beside Ruby's console with one word: Nothing.

Before dawn on the day of the attack, a faint point over the bay burns magenta and flashes. "Could it be Vexana?" Ruby reads the trace: likely an Ender, exceptionally powerful, trying to lure them in. "Guinevere. I said lure." "I heard you." "Then you know what it is." "I know what you read," says Guinevere. "I don't know what it is." Ruby saves the trace and keeps her gloved hand flat over it.

ties.t: Ruby tests her star for her.

text: Selena sits in the front row of Guinevere's class, in late every morning with her guardian's note, her dragon-shaped machine clicking at her heel, asleep on her arms through lessons. When a boy on the Academy stairs called her dangerous, Selena waved her lollipop over her shoulder: "One day, when the haze clears..." Everybody laughed, Guinevere loudest. Guinevere has always liked her a little. She likes anyone who does not care what a room thinks of them.

In the Storm Citadel's attack, Obsidia's field puts out the Aspirants' lights one by one. Guinevere's gold light goes out last, far over the water, and from the bell tower Selena watches it drop. Since the charge, the open line has carried Guinevere's laugh. For weeks before that, Selena never heard it once.

Selena comes down into the bay road cut with the Enders behind her and stops over Guinevere and Vexana: horns, pointed ears, black claws, fangs. "Take a good look. This is the real me." Nobody laughs. Guinevere looks at her the way she looked at Vexana, past the plate and the claws, for the girl inside. For a breath Selena's smile goes. Then it is back, and she is gone.

text: Vexana kept everyone away. Her father had died standing between her and an Ender, and she blamed herself. Guinevere, the heiress of House Baroque, would not take no. One night, her arm bound from shoulder to elbow, Guinevere asked once more, and Vexana said yes. At the end of that year they won the Academy's first badges for the best pair of the year.

They became an undefeated pair, on a billboard back to back. Guinevere fought up close with her fists and drones. Vexana stayed above with her staff, and whatever reached for Guinevere's back, her magic hit first. Guinevere never looked back to check. When she fell, Vexana caught her wrist. Guinevere made two gold stars that light up when their powers are in sync, and they made a rule: partners tell each other first.

On the first morning of a watch, Vexana pushed Guinevere clear of a claw and was dragged into the dark in her place. Guinevere refused her father's order to come home and kept searching. Her star stayed lit all those weeks and told her Vexana was alive. Vexana says the Will of the Planet showed her the end. She took its orders as cover, told no one, and meant to die striking the Mother Matrix's open chest.

At the Singularity they met on the platforms over the bay, Vexana with an army of Enders at her back. Guinevere would not give her up. When Guinevere fell from the sky, Vexana caught her once more, through a door of the void. They struck the Matrix's open chest together and were drawn into the black hole. There Guinevere said she would never give up on her. Their two stars lit, and they found each other in the dark.

"Whose mind?" she asks before she can stop herself. She thinks of the claw that raked her arm at the dome's foot. Somebody sent that. When Chang'e names the Control Core, she sits up: something to hit.

That day on the lawn, her head in Vexana's lap, she sits bolt upright and punches at the sky. She will definitely find a way to destroy it. Some Will in the dark sends claws at them and thinks it gets to decide what happens next, she says, and it does not. "We will decide the fate of the world ourselves." Vexana does not answer.

The guards never come into the long hall. It is the master's. The detail stops at a chair where the hall begins, and nobody ever sits in it. When Guinevere goes to the Academy and writes to him every week, his only answer comes through Hester: a board meeting. At her trial and her ceremony his seat stays empty. Guinevere does not go. She tells Hester to tell him he will see, once she brings Vexana back. Hester inclines her head a single degree, and stays where she is. In the void Guinevere remembers his message and says she will give up being a lady of status rather than back down.
