text: Roger is Layla's teammate on Professor Joe's Team B3. Before a drill Layla smiles at him: "Scared, Roger? Hide behind me, then." "Okay," says Roger. He means it. With a minute left he runs two hundred meters of open ground for the spot behind her and goes down under an Ender. Fanny's cable stops its claw, and Layla's shot passes a finger from his face.

At the breach, Roger gets an arm under the hurt Joe and drags him toward a side street. Layla sees it and keeps walking. When Joe forms the Layla-Fanny Team, Roger goes to another pair. Joe says Roger reports that he falls down less.

In the bay road cut, a small boy stands crying behind Layla at the wall. Without turning she says over her shoulder, "If you're scared, you can hide behind me." Once she said it to Roger as a joke, and he ran across open ground for the spot behind her. She does not say it as a joke now. The boy takes a fistful of the back of her uniform and holds on.

ties.t: Roger is her teammate in Team B3.
She once told Roger to hide behind her as a joke.

text: When Ruby and Angela land at the dome's foot, Layla calls them armed newcomers and says they are funny in the head. Still, when Fanny vouches for them, Layla sighs and adds her word: "Hers, apparently. And mine." Ruby bows and asks refuge of the school. Chang'e seats the newcomers beside the two who vouched. "Beside us?" says Layla.

Under the Singularity, the four of them stand on a broken seawall inside Angela's pink shield. Layla stands in the middle with her cannon and calls the strikes. "I've locked on to the enemies! Ruby, left. Fanny, high." Soon Ruby's scythe goes through the panes before anyone asks. "Funny in the head," Layla mutters at Ruby and Angela, lining up again. "Both of you. The pane's open before I ask."

ties.t: She vouches for Ruby and Angela.
She directs Ruby's strikes.

text: When Obsidia's field kills Layla's cannon, she comes down off her roof to the bay road cut. Up the cut, in a shelter doorway, a small boy is crying. Layla holds the wall across the cut with Fanny, counting each Ender's strike aloud.

The boy comes down the street looking for someone and finds the wall instead. He stands behind her with his fists against his eyes. Layla does not turn from the wall. "If you're scared, you can hide behind me." She once said it as a joke. Not now. He takes a fistful of the back of her uniform and holds on.

Fanny kneels and comforts him. He asks Layla whether Fanny is her friend. Layla looks at Fanny and says, "She's my teammate." A soldier with his arm in a sling walks the boy back up the street. Later Ruby makes herself hear his crying, to keep hold of herself.

ties.t: She lets the crying boy hide behind her.
She is one of the three in Team B3.

text: One morning Layla runs along the school roof, bent low, four minutes late for class, sure that nobody checks the roof. Fanny lands on her back, and the two race down the white spiral stairwell until their feet cross and they roll into the corridor in a heap.

The classroom door stands open. The teacher waits with folded arms, and every head turns. "They're really going to throw the book at us this time," says Layla. Then she hears herself add that at least they will be in detention together. Detention is cleaning the Academy hall.

ties.t: Layla's class teacher.
She sits in the third-year lounge.
The newcomers are seated beside her in the third-year class.
She goes out with the third years from the gate portal.

text: Layla and Vexana have shared classes for two years, and neither has ever spoken first. In the breach in the northeast sector, Layla sees Guinevere and Vexana hold the other end, Vexana's magic striking whatever reaches for Guinevere's back. Everyone knows them. Their undefeated record is on the courtyard billboard. Layla's is on a rankings board, in second place.

At the gate portal before the fish-market raid, Guinevere introduces herself, and Vexana gives her own name, in case it was needed. Layla keeps score: two years of nothing, and now that she has a team, Vexana talks. She went first. One to her.

Professor Joe sends the Layla-Fanny Team to the west end of the market and the other pair to the east. Weeks later, when Ruby and Angela become Aspirants, Layla turns round in the hall and sees Guinevere waving her whole arm at Vexana by the door.

text: Lesley's little brother followed her from room to room and held on to her leg. She was Sis to him, and he never called her anything else. Every night he held her sleeve and asked what would happen if an Ender came. "Then I'll stand in front," she told him, every night.

In 983 an Ender broke the house. Lesley stepped in front of him, and it took her left eye. "Sis?" he said behind her: his last word. In the morning she found his hand under a beam, and it did not hold on. She had kept her promise, and he died anyway. After that she promised nobody anything.

Years later, at the research base, Chang'e held her sleeve the same way and asked her to promise, and Lesley did. In the Storm Citadel's attack, when an Ender bent over Chang'e, Lesley's feet started round the chair to stand in front, as she had told her brother every night. Chang'e told her to stay at her back.

ties.t: Her little brother, who called her Sis.

Her brother, who died.
She stood in front of her little brother every night.

Lesley's comm.

Chang'e's eye is fitted into her empty socket.
It is fitted into Lesley's left socket.
Her teal eye.
Lesley's left eye.
It is Lesley's eye.

text: Lesley's father mends small machines, mostly clocks, in a shop on a street that runs down to the bay. The clocks hang on every wall, each one out of step, so the house ticks day and night. He lets Lesley stand on a crate at his bench and hold the parts. He tells a clock that will not start, "Don't sulk." For her last birthday he makes her a tin bird that hops and clicks its beak.

When the radio on his bench talks of Enders, he turns it down. On the wet night in 983 when an Ender comes, every lamp dies, but the clocks he wound by hand keep ticking. He tells the children to stay where they are. As the wall goes, he shouts Lesley's name from the doorway. Then the roof comes down. In the morning she finds him where the doorway had been.

Years later Chang'e gives Lesley a rifle with no cell and no cable: a spring, a pin and a bolt. Its bolt sounds like her father's bench with every clock going, and she thinks it will still work in the dark. On the morning the Storm Citadel's storm comes through the Singularity, violet light moves in the cloud over the bay again. Lesley remembers that only his hand-wound clocks kept ticking, and her thumb finds the old bolt.

ties.t: Her father, who mended clocks.
Her father.
Her father wound clocks by hand.

text: Lesley's mother laughs from the kitchen door when her husband tells a clock not to sulk. "He says that to all of them." At the one table in the kitchen she decides who had the worst day, and that one gets the biggest piece. She keeps one candle stub in a drawer for birthdays. "Wish fast. And wish small. It's a small candle." Lesley wishes for a bigger candle, and her mother calls her sensible.

On the wet night in 983 when an Ender comes, she brings the lit candle upstairs, one hand cupped around the flame. "It isn't a birthday," says Lesley's brother. "No," says her mother. "It's for seeing." Then the wall goes and the candle goes out. As the roof falls she reaches past Lesley's father, one hand out toward the children's bed. In the morning Lesley finds her beside him and sits down in the rain between them.

Years later, on the night the research base falls, Lesley comes back minutes too late and finds Chang'e in the ash, her parents gone. Once Lesley sat in the rain between her own parents. She knows what this is better than anyone, and she has let it happen to Chang'e.

ties.t: Her mother.
Her mother; Lesley once sat in the rain between her parents.
The long rifle is her weapon.
Chang'e gives it to her.
Lesley's rifle.
She sleeps there in a chair.

It comes in behind her.

They are Lesley's squads.
Her squads held the giants' front.

text: The officer has Lesley's file open on his desk. "Terrinia's research base," he says. "Two chief scientists, and a child they've taken in. You're the best young shot we have. Keep them alive." "Understood." Lesley takes it like any other mission.

When Lesley brings in a core piece whole, he comes out to the base himself. He will not give these orders over the comm. The piece makes her the most valuable shot the Shield has, he says, and she is going on a top secret mission, for as long as it takes, with no radio and no letters. Another soldier takes her gate.
Lesley sees that the piece has made her worth sending away, and sets it aside. In the Shield she has never refused an order. "Understood."

ties.t: He gives Lesley her orders.
She accepts his order to go on the mission.

text: The night the base falls, Lesley comes back to find the city's edge burning. On the Shield's channel the squads call for a commander, and nobody answers. On a roof she finds a Shield officer with gray in his beard and a rank armband, shouting into his radio handset while nobody on the channel listens to him. He looks at her face. "You're Lesley," he says. "The rail yard."
He holds out the handset. She says her name into it, and the channel goes quiet. Then the squads answer her, and they hold the avenues, barely.
Between shots she sees a giant walking toward the water, toward the base. "No! It's a decoy!" She shoves the handset back into his hands, tells him to hold there, and runs.

ties.t: He hands her his radio handset.
Lesley's old rifle.
She keeps a room at its top.

text: After Lesley and Chang'e make peace, Chang'e builds a glove wired to a dial that reads aspirant power. Lesley's hand goes in first, and the needle swings hard past the line. With the dial Lesley chooses her instructors. She tests only Shield soldiers she has fought beside, and most needles stop short of the line. One she keeps is a young soldier with a monocle, named Joe.

Over the crater the Academy rises wall by wall. On its first morning Lesley becomes its Chief Combat Instructor, head of the Combat Division, and Joe is one of its first instructors. Years later he is Professor Joe of the Combat Division, still with his monocle.

ties.t: She picks him as one of her instructors.
She chooses him as an instructor.

text: When Ruby and Angela land at Selrick and ask for refuge, Lesley has already watched the record of the landing: Ruby's scythe raised over a child, then lowered. She lets the two in under watch. From that day her rifle is on Ruby.

In the Academy hall, Lesley stands before Ruby, Angela, Layla and Fanny with her hands behind her back. "Ruby, Angela: you are Aspirants as of today. The four of you stand together." Ruby keeps her eyes on the floor in front of Lesley's boots. Lesley tells them that by trusting each other they can gain limitless strength.

When the Singularity opens over the bay and Guinevere flies at it alone, Lesley sends the frontline after her on Layla's plan. Ruby runs through the hall with her scythe on her shoulder. "Your sector, Commander," she says on the channel, dry. Lesley's rifle has been on her since the day she landed. Ruby takes the order without a word against it.

text: In 983 an Ender took Lesley's left eye and her whole family. She climbs onto the last truck for the far stations and hides behind the crates in a Shield station's storeroom. The sergeant, a heavy man with a burned hand, finds her that afternoon. "Who are you with?" "Nobody." He has a boy her size in the city, he says, and the station is no place for either of them. She is to go back on the next convoy.

When the convoy comes, she lies flat under the armory floorboards. He lifts a board and looks down at her a long time. "If you're staying, you work." He gives her the rifles to clean. Once a week he lets her fire one round with the gunners, at a fence post in the grass. "One. Let's see how you like the kick." The kick knocks her off her box. The next week she gets back on. In time he gives her five rounds a week.
She is the only child at the station. In a raid she is meant to go to the bunker. She goes up the wall instead. The first time, the sergeant carries her down. After that he only looks.

One dawn an Ender crosses the wall in one stride, and he shouts "Fall back!" Lesley stays flat on the wall walk and kills it with one shot. He comes out first and looks at the dead Ender, at the soldier in the mud, then up at the wall. "Report." "Another threat eliminated." That night he holds out the chalk, and she makes her own stroke on the armory door. Then the Shield takes her as a soldier.

ties.t: He carries her down from the wall in her first raid.

text: Vexana's father, a Shield soldier, dies standing between her and an Ender, and she grows up in a home, training alone at dawn with a wooden pole. Years go by. One dawn Lesley stands at the yard's railings in a white officer's coat, a sheet with the home's stamp in her hand. "Father, Shield of Dawnbreak. Killed in action," she reads. Vexana waits for her to say she is sorry. She does not.

"I'm Lesley. The Academy tests its first intake this year. Come." Lesley folds the sheet and walks away without waiting for an answer. Vexana thinks that at the Academy she could break more Enders, and picks up the pole again.

Years later, when the Mother Matrix is knocked back, Vexana comes out of the black hole with Guinevere, in an Ender's robe. Lesley says she watched the Matrix fire on her, then watched her charge it. "You're on the line. Frontline assault, with Guinevere." Vexana grounds her staff and brings her heels together. "Understood, Commander." Chang'e says her file still says Missing. "Change it," says Lesley.

ties.t: She found Vexana at the home and brought her to the Academy.
She puts Vexana on the line.
She takes Lesley's order and calls her Commander.
Lesley wears it.

text: Lesley came to the far Shield station after an Ender took her family. The youngest soldier there stands the dawn watch beside her. She aims at the grass and counts under her breath, waiting for an Ender's chest to open. He counts out loud: the days to his leave. "Forty-one," he says one morning, and asks why she never talks. She does not lower the rifle. "Bullets are the only language the enemy understands." He laughs. Then he sees her face, and stops.
That night he asks her to play cards. She goes back to the rifles. She thinks: if I don't know him, it won't matter when he's gone.

One dawn an Ender crosses the wall, and the soldiers fall back to the bunker line. He slips at the foot of the ladder and goes down in the mud, and the Ender turns to him. Lesley lies on the wall walk and waits for its chest plates to split. She fires once, into the core. Its arm strikes the mud beside him.

That night, outside, he holds out the cards again. "Twelve days," he says. "Then I'm gone. One game." Lesley goes past him to her bunk and sleeps. When she wakes, the sun is high. More, she thinks. More strokes.

ties.t: She shoots the Ender that turns on him.
He is the boy's father.
She is the boy's mother.

Obsidia says the Mother Matrix is the Will's body.

Chang'e calls it Mr. Bunny's new friend.
She was grown in the nest.
She grew in a small place in the nest.

He works the night shift at the base.

It happens in the Northeastern sector.

A sector of the city.

Obsidia sends it.

text: Obsidia made Selena. She grew her in the nest, where her kind slept, and changed her face again and again until it was right. On the storm night of 983 she carried the sleeping child down herself and left her in the mud of Terrinia: the first of her making with a perfect human form. Then Obsidia took the Storm Citadel far away, to watch what grew.

Obsidia calls Selena her seed and her pawn. Selena knew her only as the huntress who made her. Selena sold Obsidia last year's Academy numbers for pay, but never a name or a place where people die. Obsidia sent recall after recall, and Selena ignored them all.

When Obsidia's field put out the Aspirants, Selena chose to follow the last recall, and rode her lightning up into the Storm Citadel. "It's been a while, my dear creator," she said. Obsidia tipped up Selena's chin and looked her over like something she had carved herself. Then she bound her in chains of bone. Selena tore them apart and declared war on her maker: "I'll never be your puppet again!"

Selena cut the throne down instead of taking it. Obsidia's weapon went through her side, and a point-blank shot threw her out of the burning ship. As the Citadel was drawn into the Singularity, Obsidia rose in a new form of silver and gold and opened her arms. "Come back, my puppet." Selena thought of Karina and the Academy, and charged. There the story leaves them.

ties.t: She made the child and grew it in the nest.
Obsidia planted it as a seed and calls it hers.
One pawn among the humans is hers.
She says she set down this seed with her own hands.

She gives Selena orders and calls her a pawn, but Selena has not obeyed.
She made Selena in the nest and shaped her face.
She greets Obsidia as her creator.

Her weapon goes through Selena's side.
The Storm Citadel is her ship.
It is Obsidia's ship.
She commands the Citadel; it answers to no one else.
It answers to her alone.
She says the ship in the storm is hers.
She built most of it from what she ended.
It carries her across the stars.
She sits on its throne, the spine every block hangs from.
It is Obsidia's ship, steered from her throne.
Her grip on the throne wakes the whole ship.
It wakes and moves at Obsidia's grip.
She stands in her throne hall.
Obsidia approves their augmentation.
She approves their augmentation.

text: Vexana first meets Obsidia in the void, under the vast face of the Mother Matrix, where Obsidia breaks off her own healing with a word. Her eyes stop on Vexana's right sleeve, where the star Guinevere gave her is pinned, and she says nothing about it. She asks what the Will showed her instead. She names herself the first Ender to wake into a self and calls herself the flaw. She knows Vexana's name, and says she reads it in the Will's orders.

Vexana goes to the Storm Citadel on her own, looking for the Control Core. Obsidia walks her through hanging streets she says she built from what she ended, and tells her of Balance and the purge. She says she wishes to see what a human does with it. The Core she puts off: "Another time."

On the prow by the gate, over a dead Aspirant suit, Obsidia tells her the body goes through first, and that nothing made of matter ever comes back out of the black hole at the gate's center. The Core, she says, she has never seen. She asks if Vexana still believes she has a choice. Vexana answers that as long as the Aspirant voice echoes, she will resist the darkness. Obsidia asks where that arrogance comes from, and lets it pass again.

Later Obsidia turns up in Vexana's hidden hollow, a palm on a Guard's heart. The Guards light for Vexana, and Obsidia never asks what they are for. She has expected Vexana to turn since she first saw that sleeve, and tells her nothing of what the Will means to do with her. When the Matrix draws back, she has watched every Ender on the platforms turn on Vexana, and two lights go into its open chest and come back out. She does not know how.

ties.t: Vexana declares against the darkness to her face, and she lets it pass.
She knew Vexana would turn.
She slept in the void for ages.

text: Something vast and cold made the Enders to kill on instinct. Obsidia was one of them, until one day she turned and looked at herself. Long after, she woke from a sleep in the void with a question: when nothing is left to purge, what are we for? The thing that made her had no answer.

Under the Mother Matrix, Obsidia tells Vexana what that thing is. She says the Will of the Planet is the mind, and the Mother Matrix is its body. It made her, she says, as it makes every Ender: as its commander, made to watch a battlefield and to shape the pulse, the Will's voice that every Ender hears at once. For ages there was no "I" in her. Only the next order, and hunger, and the pulse.

The others, she says, perished in war, and the body made more. Her it healed, again and again, for longer than humans have kept records. She says she alone was both made to watch and kept. At her post on the edge of a great door, while a world ended under her, she noticed the one doing the watching, and it was her. She says her end of the line shut the day she woke: what the Enders see runs back to the Will, but what she sees stays with her.

The body still mends her. She says its healing sets a made thing back to what it was made for, and each time it smooths some of her away. So she takes it only when she must, and stops it with one hand. "That's enough recalibration." It made her and mends her by one rule, she says: free will is a flaw that must be corrected. "I am the flaw." She still reads the Will's orders. She says she listens to everything.

ties.t: She says she was made as the Will's commander.

text: Professor Joe teaches the Combat Division, and Vexana sits his lesson on weak spots with Guinevere beside her. His last slide is a shaking recording from the Academy's oldest records: a ship of black blades over a city in a red sky. The Storm Citadel. Under its storm, every machine died.

On the day Ruby and Angela become Aspirants, Joe, still on his cane, sees the third years off at the gate portal. The dome is torn over the fish market. He sends the Layla-Fanny Team to the west end and Vexana and Guinevere to the east. Guinevere walks into the portal's light as if it had been lit for her, and Vexana follows without a word.

Dragged into the void, Vexana one day sees a violet storm turning far past the Mother Matrix, something huge and black-bladed inside it. She knows it from Joe's slide. On the night before the attack she climbs a ruined tower beyond the dome and sees the city's lamps still burning under the thunderheads. She remembers that every machine under that ship's storm died, and knows the ship itself is still behind the sky.

text: Ruby's father leads the Decisionmakers, who give Oro's orders, and grown-ups bow low to him. Ruby is his heir, and she has been told since before she could read that heirs can have no friends and no feelings. When he hears she laughed again, alone, he calls her to the dark Council hall. Oro has gone unopposed for thousands of years, he says, because its rulers do not bend.

Ruby keeps her head down, and the tears run anyway. His boot comes down on them. "You cannot allow yourself to be so weak. Do not disappoint me, Ruby." She answers, "Yes, Father," and he walks out into white light without looking back. Alone, she whispers that she has a plan. She has none yet.

Later, at his desk of black glass, he tells her that Oro's three powers have voted: Dawnbreak will be cleansed. Ruby objects that its people have done nothing to Oro. He answers that they make weapons from the Enders' dead, and that her objection is overruled. Afterward he stands in the doorway of her dark laboratory, where he has never once come. His mouth opens a little and closes, and he goes without a word.

ties.t: He is her father.
He is her father; she calls him Father.
It is Ruby's own rage.
The scythe is her weapon.

text: On Planet Oro, Ruby's tutor gives her lessons in the Council hall, among pillars that go up into the dark. One day, sure nobody is around, she makes her pink doll bow to the empty floor and laughs. Her tutor is standing in the shadow of the next pillar. She did not hear him come. She makes her face go blank. He does not look at the doll. "The lesson, Heir. How did everything begin?"

Ruby recites it. Everything began with a single burst of chaos, and Balance keeps it in order. Some worlds grow a will of their own, even far ones like Dawnbreak. Long ago Oro fought a terrible war with the Enders, and now nobody on Oro may grow strong enough to upset the order. "That includes the heir," says the tutor. "Yes," says Ruby.

The lessons go on year after year, in the same hall under the same high windows. Ruby grows taller, and the doll is put away. Her face stays blank whenever anyone looks. She still laughs sometimes, when she is sure the hall is empty. She is not always right.

text: Ruby and Selena share the third-year classroom. Selena sits in the front row, and Ruby by the wall, one row behind her. The day Selena shows the class her design for a suit of Ender plating, Ruby leans forward. "Does it come in my size?" "Everything does," says Selena. "For a price."

Later, in Chang'e's lab, Ruby sits at the next bench, where Angela comes each week for her check. Selena's phone flashes red, and she swipes the message away unread. Ruby looks up. "You didn't even read it." "Never do." Ruby smiles at her as if she had pulled a coin out of the air.
After that Ruby says good morning to Selena every day. Selena never finds out why. The red messages are recalls from the Enders, and Selena ignores every one.

Days after Ruby and Angela become Aspirants, the door slides open in the middle of a lesson. Selena comes in with a lollipop in her cheek, and Silverbolt clicks in at her heel. "Selena," says the teacher. "Late again." "My guardian already called it in," says Selena. The teacher checks a tablet and sighs. The note is there.
Selena drops into her desk and lays her head on her arms. "I'm taking a little nap. You all just keep going." The teacher looks at the sleeping head and goes on with the lesson.

text: After Vexana is taken into the void, she needs armor and something to carry her up. Every student in her year knows who sells wreckage: Selena, at the crews' yard outside the outer fence, after dark. Vexana waits in the dark until a buyer leaves, then steps into the lamplight in Ender plate. Selena only moves her lollipop and says, "Nice hair." Vexana takes it for a dealer's nerve and asks nothing about where the plating comes from.

Missing people draw no stipend, so Vexana pays in places: whole dead Enders lying where no crew has been yet. Selena says, "Deal." Over the sack she remarks that most of them think Vexana is dead, and that her partner does not. Vexana's face does not move, but her hand starts toward her right sleeve and stops halfway.

Selena sells to her openly, curious to see how another pawn like herself might escape the game, and sure the girl cannot tell on her without telling on herself. Vexana comes back for knees, a thigh, forearms, a hip, then cores at three places each. Four come over the weeks. A suit takes one, and Selena never asks what the other three are for.

One storm night Selena sees a figure with a staff on top of the ruined tower, facing the Academy. She rides past Guinevere under the billboard and keeps the two words that would do it, dead ground, to herself. From the bell tower she tilts her lollipop at the lit telescope window, then at the tower in the dark: not a word, to either of them.

text: Vexana is small when all the guns on the wall fire at once. Her father, a Shield soldier, carries her to the shelter and tells her to stay back, and she slips out to find him. A tall gray Ender steps out of a side lane with its claw raised, and her father comes down the wall stair and stands between them.

Then arms catch her from behind. A soldier throws her over his shoulder and runs. Over his shoulder she watches her father's back until the smoke closes over him. She shouts for him once, her hands closing into fists, and the soldier only runs faster.
Years later, dragged into the void in Guinevere's place, Vexana remembers it: a soldier carried her off down the street while her father stayed. This time she is the one who stayed behind.

text: Vexana's father was a soldier of the Shield of Dawnbreak who kept the big guns on the city wall working. They lived in a Shield house under the wall. He taught her to press a bent bracket straight with two fingers. He led her up the wall stair to look out over the dark ground, and gave her a small star of her own.

One evening the guns on the wall all fired at once. Vexana slipped out of the shelter to find him, and an Ender stepped into her path. He stood between her and it and said, "Stay back." It was the last thing he ever said to her. A soldier carried her off. Another told her that Ender never got past him while he stood. The record listed him killed in action, and his toolbox was all that came back.

Vexana blamed herself, and kept everyone away so nobody would die for her again. At the Singularity, facing a tall Ender, she set her boots wide on the stone, the way he had once stood between an Ender and his daughter. Inside the black hole she told Guinevere at last: her father, a soldier, died saving her, and she wished it had been her instead.

text: In Chang'e's class the Will of the Planet was only a word on a screen: the mind behind the Enders. When an Ender dragged Vexana into the void, she says, the Will came to her as a giant in dark violet armor and showed her the end, with Guinevere lying broken. It marked her with a cold point in her chest.

Vexana decided to let it use her. She would take its orders, walk among its Enders as one of them, and keep close to its body. The orders came through the mark: a place and a time, never a reason. She obeyed them as cover.

In the Storm Citadel, Obsidia told Vexana the Will did not hate humans. Then it could not be begged, Vexana decided. It had to be broken. She went on obeying. On the morning of the attack the order came as a voice inside her: "The Academy. Now." Its Enders ran with her as if she led them.
